title: Gene Burden Testing for Rare and Genetic Disease Studies: A Practical Beginner-Oriented Workflow
synopsis: This methods chapter gives a beginner-oriented, disease-agnostic workflow for gene burden testing of rare variants in sequencing studies. It covers study design, QC, annotation, qualifying-variant definitions, choosing burden versus kernel tests, covariates and interpretation, with emphasis on reproducibility choices such as ancestry matching and frequency thresholds.

title: BASIN: Background-Anchored Signal Normalization with Integrated Quality Control for CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag
synopsis: Spike-in-free normalization for CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag when a perturbation changes the overall level of a chromatin mark. BASIN treats reproducible peak-like background in IgG controls as an internal reference, derives per-sample scale factors from it, and includes a QC step that tests whether the normalization assumptions hold. It stayed stable over a >100-fold range of cell input and picked up the global H3K36me3 loss in Drosophila Set2 mutants that read-depth normalization hid; a ready-made anchor panel is provided for Drosophila.

title: Combining family history, polygenic scores, and childhood trauma to predict major depressive disorder
synopsis: Asks whether adding family history of psychiatric disorders, multi-trait polygenic scores, childhood trauma and background factors together predicts lifetime major depression better than any subset of them. Elastic net and XGBoost models were trained and cross-validated in GLAD+ (about 14k people) and UK Biobank (about 111k). The combined models reached AUC 0.83 in GLAD+ and 0.74 in UK Biobank, held up in external validation, and family history and trauma each predicted better than the polygenic scores.

title: Cross- species developmental multiomics identifies RHOJ as a regulator of human-enriched cortical progenitor states
synopsis: Compares time-resolved paired snRNA/snATAC profiles of human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex and finds human-enriched outer radial glia programs that include the gene RHOJ. An intronic RHOJ enhancer drives more reporter activity with the human sequence than with other primate versions, partly because of a human-specific change in an AP-1 motif. Deleting the enhancer in human cortical organoids lowered RHOJ expression and impaired organoid growth and progenitor composition.

title: Fixed group shrinkage exposes the fairness accuracy Pareto frontier for cross ancestry polygenic risk scores
synopsis: Introduces cluster_fixed, a shrinkage framework that uses ancestry labels to trace the whole trade-off curve between overall PRS accuracy and the accuracy gap between populations, instead of returning one optimized model. In 1000 Genomes simulations and Pan-UK Biobank height effects it cut the worst-case subgroup disparity by roughly 50-72%, usually at a cost in overall accuracy, though both can improve when population-specific effects are large. Other correction strategies did not match its fairness gains.

title: From benchmarking to application: a scalable mitochondrial DNA analysis and variant identification framework for whole-genome sequencing
synopsis: The authors benchmarked four mtDNA variant callers (MitoHPC, mtSwirl, mity, mtDNA-Server 2) on 1000 Genomes data and simulations. MitoHPC and mtSwirl performed best overall, especially in non-European haplogroups. Based on MitoHPC they built MARVel, a reproducible workflow with QC reports, interactive variant curation and an mtDNA PCA reference, and it recovered known pathogenic variants in an ataxia cohort.

title: Genetic analysis of non-familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease patients
synopsis: The authors compared 87 sporadic early-onset Alzheimer's cases with late-onset cases and ADSP controls using GWAS, SKAT gene tests, polygenic scores and a rare-variant review of known AD genes. The only strong signals were at the APOE locus. Early-onset cases did not carry extra rare variants in APP, PSEN1, PSEN2 or modifier genes and had intermediate polygenic risk, which suggests their genetics overlap with late-onset AD.

title: Genomic foundation models and complementary variant-scoring strategies in LGMD-associated genes: architecture, adaptation, and sequence context
synopsis: Benchmarks six genomic foundation models, plus GPN-Star and AlphaGenome native scores, on about 7,000 ClinVar SNVs in ten limb-girdle muscular dystrophy genes. It compares frozen embeddings, supervised fine-tuning and different context lengths. Evo2 was the strongest of the six (AUROC up to 0.96 with 501-bp context), and GPN-Star and AlphaGenome native scores reached even higher MCC; longer context helped most models.

title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
synopsis: Builds a TF-enhancer-gene network for triple-negative breast cancer by combining public enhancer-targeting CRISPRi Perturb-seq data from MDA-MB-231 cells with ENCODE TF ChIP-seq binding priors. On held-out CRISPRi results it predicts regulatory links much better than GENIE3 or co-expression (AUPRC about 0.87 versus 0.63-0.68). Central regulators such as CTCF, EP300, MYC and AP-1 factors were prioritized and their signatures were associated with survival.

title: Meta-analysis of Sequencing Data Identifies Candidate Endometrial Cancer Susceptibility Genes
synopsis: The authors ran gene-level burden tests on rare protein-truncating and deleterious missense variants in 2,675 endometrial cancer cases and about 160,000 controls, meta-analysing UK Biobank and the 100,000 Genomes Project. They recovered MSH6, MLH1, MSH2 and PTEN with large relative risks. They also report 19 more exome-wide significant genes from the PTV analysis (including PHKG2) and 8 from the missense analysis as candidates that still need replication.

title: NanoHIV-DR: a Nextflow workflow for consensus and read level HIV-1 drug resistance profiling from Oxford Nanopore sequencing
synopsis: Few workflows exist for analysing HIV-1 drug-resistance data from Nanopore sequencing. NanoHIV-DR is a Nextflow pipeline that goes from raw POD5 files to consensus building, then interprets resistance with Sierra and also detects resistance mutations at the read level, below the consensus. It writes clinician-readable reports linked to sample metadata, so users need less bioinformatics expertise.

title: Optimizing Exomiser to prioritize candidate genes underlying monogenic forms of common disease
synopsis: The authors benchmarked and tuned the Exomiser rare-variant prioritization tool on exomes from a kidney stone disease cohort (701 cases, 200 controls). The tuned pipeline placed 94% of known gold-standard gene-patient pairs in its top five and proposed 62 new candidate genes. They checked these against gene-level rare-variant enrichment in an extended cohort and in UK Biobank, and ABCC6 was the best-supported risk gene.

title: Quantification of Bias-Variance Tradeoffs in Genome-Wide Polygenic Indices: When 'Good' PGIs are Bad and 'Bad' PGIs are Good
synopsis: Asks how much SNP heritability different polygenic score methods (clumping, LDpred2-inf/auto, SBayesR, PRS-CS-auto) actually capture once GWAS estimation error is corrected for, using independent GWAS halves (including a way to split existing summary statistics synthetically). Methods that shrink effects hard give better raw accuracy but worse error-corrected accuracy, whereas LDpred2-inf nearly recovers full SNP heritability after correction. Aggressive shrinkage can also bias associations with other phenotypes.

title: SpliceVarMech: A causal generative framework for mechanistic interpretation of non-canonical splicing variants
synopsis: Introduces SpliceVarMech, which compares wild-type and mutant sequences, generates possible splice outcomes with discrete diffusion and uses Bayesian inference to give disruption probabilities with uncertainty for non-canonical splicing variants. On a small validated set from male-infertility genes (31 variants) it outperformed 16 splice predictors including SpliceAI. Fine-tuning on BRCA1 saturation genome editing data raised AUROC from 0.72 to 0.84 on 203 held-out variants.

title: The IGVF Catalog Knowledge Graph
synopsis: The IGVF consortium built a knowledge graph to support variant-to-function interpretation. It joins 657 MPRA, CRISPR-perturbation and coding-variant assay datasets and predictive enhancer-gene models with public GWAS, QTL, LD and annotation data, giving about 3 billion nodes and 8.6 billion edges that can be queried through a portal, an API and an MCP server. Case studies at type 2 diabetes, liver-trait and coronary artery disease loci show how it resolves likely causal variants, their target genes and whether they act through coding or regulatory changes.

title: The IGVF Data Portal: a repository for insights into genome function
synopsis: This paper describes the IGVF Consortium's data portal, which holds more than 240 TB of assay and computational results on how genomic variation affects function. The data can be reached through a web browser, an API and agentic tools. The paper summarizes the available data and the design of the portal.

title: EPIC2: integrating single-cell chromatin accessibility with human genetics to identify trait-relevant cell types
synopsis: EPIC2 is a statistical framework that finds which cell types matter for a trait by testing whether GWAS signal tracks with cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility in single-cell ATAC data. It accounts for linkage disequilibrium, runs the test at both SNP and regulatory-peak resolution, and merges the two P-values with a Cauchy combination test. It is released as an R package with vignettes and test data.

title: Read&Tag enables antibody-independent combinatorial and multifactorial chromatin profiling
synopsis: Presents Read&Tag, a CUT&Tag-style method that fuses engineered chromatin reader domains or intrabodies straight onto Tn5, so no antibodies are needed. It profiles active and repressive histone marks, DNA methylation and elongating Pol II, and works in frozen tissue and low-input samples. Dual-specificity readers only tagment fragments that carry both H3K4me3 and H3K27me3, so bivalency is measured directly, and barcoded complexes read out four chromatin features in a single reaction.

title: A Super-Enhancer-Like Element and a Positive Feedback Loop Drive Ultra-High Expression of CCS for Red Pepper Ripening
synopsis: Explains the extremely high ripening-specific expression of the pepper CCS gene through a super-enhancer-like array of 22 tandem CArG-box repeats in its promoter, split up by MITE insertions. CaRIN-CaTAGL1 activate the gene in a way that scales with repeat copy number, demethylation lifts repression during ripening, and CaRIN forms phase-separated condensates at the promoter within a positive feedback loop.

title: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
synopsis: This is the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative GWAS of endometriosis: over 1 million participants, 32% of them of non-European ancestry, with new procedure-confirmed case definitions. It found 58 risk regions, 27 of them new, including loci seen only in African and admixed American groups. Follow-up comorbidity scans and multi-omic analyses pointed to 314 genes as possible drug targets.

title: Brain Cell-Type-Specific X-Chromosome Gene Regulation Reveals Sex-Biased Candidate Genes in Neurodegeneration
synopsis: The authors mapped X-chromosome cis-eQTLs in seven brain cell types from 423 older individuals and found 212 genetically regulated X-linked genes, most of them cell-type specific and some with sex-dependent effects. Combining this resource with X-chromosome GWAS through TWAS, Mendelian randomization and colocalization nominated 11 candidate causal genes, each tied to a cell type, for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and multiple system atrophy.

title: Brain-derived multi-omics prioritization of mitochondria-related genes in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder
synopsis: The study tested mitochondria-related genes for psychiatric risk by running SMR, HEIDI and colocalization with brain methylation, expression and protein QTLs against GWAS of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and depression. A tiered evidence framework ranked ACADVL and SLC25A24 as the strongest schizophrenia candidates, and ENDOG emerged as a regulatory signal driven by methylation.

title: CELL-X: A Single-Cell Transcriptomics Framework for Cell-Type and Disease-State Prioritization of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Genes
synopsis: CELL-X aims to work out which genes at T2D GWAS loci matter and in which islet cell type they act. It scores 37 genetically supported T2D genes for cell-type specificity and for expression changes across normal, prediabetic and T2D states, using an islet single-cell atlas of about 246,000 cells. Beta cells came out as the main disease-relevant cell type, and known causal genes such as SLC30A8, GLIS3, GCK and TCF7L2 ranked highly in a 30-gene benchmark.

title: One blood methylation profile stratifies ten-year risk across 21 common diseases
synopsis: Built ten-year survival methylation risk scores for 21 common diseases in 12,785 adults from Generation Scotland and the Mass General Brigham Biobank, using reproducible probes, null-calibrated feature selection and an untouched holdout set. Eight scores reached a holdout C-index of 0.80 or higher (including CKD, COPD, heart failure, type 2 diabetes and dementia), with hazard ratios of 2.6-4.1 per SD. Most of these top scores compared favourably with published polygenic and methylation scores.

title: Rare copy number variation in alcohol use disorder using whole-genome sequencing in the All of Us Research Program
synopsis: The authors asked whether rare copy number variants (MAF <1%) called from All of Us short-read WGS help explain alcohol use disorder risk. They ran genome-wide, gene-set and region-level rCNV burden tests in about 56,000 participants from European, African and Admixed American ancestry groups and combined them by cross-ancestry meta-analysis. Genome-wide burden and large rCNV regions were not associated with AUD. They found a global protective signal for duplications, a modest risk effect of deletions in a neurodevelopmental gene set, and a significant 58 bp deletion at 16p12.1, which suggests rCNVs add little to AUD liability at current sample sizes.

title: VEGABrain: a Visualizer of Enriched Gene Analysis for the developing human brain
synopsis: VEGABrain is a web tool that needs no installation. It maps bulk RNA-seq expression onto cortical and subcortical brain atlas surfaces across five developmental windows, from the first trimester to adulthood. It provides precomputed ssGSEA enrichment maps for about 19,000 gene sets and computes maps on demand for gene lists that users upload.

title: Dosage compensation is regulated by segregated chromatin modules during development in Drosophila
synopsis: Combines sexed epigenomic and 3D genome data from Drosophila embryos to adults to study how X-chromosome dosage compensation is tuned across genes. About 30% of X-linked genes are compensated only in specific stages or tissues. Housekeeping genes compensated in all samples form constitutive long-range contacts with HAS elements at stable TAD boundaries, while stage-specific genes gain contacts with PionX and 1.688 satellite elements over development.

title: Optimizing phenotype scale improves genetic analyses in large-scale biobanks
synopsis: The authors present SIQReg, which picks a data-driven transformation of a phenotype so that genetic effects are similar across its quantiles. Across 25 UK Biobank traits the default scale was rejected for 24, and most variance-QTL and other nonadditive signals turned out to be artefacts of scale. On the new scale, GWAS loci rose by 11% and polygenic prediction accuracy by 10%, and these gains replicated across ancestry groups.

title: Cellular reconfiguration of Alzheimer’s disease genetic susceptibility across aging and pathology
synopsis: Asks which brain cell types carry Alzheimer's GWAS risk genes and how this changes with ageing and disease stage. The authors built scGIPA, which combines AD association results, brain regulatory data and hippocampal single-nucleus RNA-seq with in silico perturbation to score each cell type's contribution. Six functional modules shifted between cell types across stages, with lipid-clearance and amyloid programmes strongest in early pathology, and about half of the contributing genes acted in both ageing and pathology, often in the same cell types.

title: Functionally decoupled cis-regulatory signals at PCOLCE2 link fibroblast-lineage collagen maturation to pelvic organ prolapse
synopsis: The study asks which cell type and regulatory signal carry a suggestive pelvic organ prolapse GWAS signal at PCOLCE2. It combines fibroblast-eQTL cis-MR, colocalization, CAUSE, stratified fine-mapping, pQTL deconvolution and single-cell data. It finds that the risk acts through a fibroblast-restricted cis-regulatory effect on PCOLCE2 that is separate from a blood signal controlling circulating protein, although the index signal is not genome-wide significant and still needs replication.

title: MitoArc: A Reproducible Short-Read Workflow for Human Mitochondrial Genome Analysis with Circular-Coordinate and NUMT-Aware Evaluation
synopsis: MitoArc is a Nextflow workflow for calling human mtDNA variants from FASTQ/BAM/CRAM. It handles circular-coordinate shifting, NUMT evidence, haplogroups and contamination, and runs Mutect2 and mutserve2 side by side. On 18 synthetic benchmark datasets (100x-5000x), strict mitochondrial mapping removed NUMT false positives at some cost to recall, and GATK recall increased with depth (0.74 to 0.92).

title: PDAC BioPortal: An Integrated Web Resource for Multi-Scale Analysis of Pancreatic Cancer Transcriptomics
synopsis: PDAC BioPortal is a web platform that brings together pancreatic cancer bulk (TCGA-GTEx), treatment-associated, single-nucleus (~225k nuclei) and spatial transcriptomics. It offers interactive differential expression, enrichment, pseudobulk and spatial analyses, plus an LLM-based natural-language assistant. As a case study it profiles NRF2 redox-network remodeling across disease and treatment contexts.

title: Sparrowhawk: harnessing WebAssembly for private microbial genomics, and beyond
synopsis: Sparrowhawk is a framework that turns computational methods into interactive browser apps that run locally through WebAssembly, so users need no installation, no command line and no data uploads. For genomic epidemiology the authors wrote new lightweight assembly, AMR-gene annotation and taxonomic identification tools. These reproduce or closely match the results of existing pipelines, and the authors show that methods from other fields can be ported quickly.

title: VPHYL: A Web Application for Converting Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s Nanopore 16S rRNA Abundance Tables into phyloseq and BIOM Objects
synopsis: VPHYL is an R Shiny app that lets non-programmers convert Nanopore 16S classifier output (Emu, EPI2ME wf-16s) into phyloseq or BIOM objects, with automated QC and diversity reports. Its output matched an independent script for all nine classifier-database combinations, and it reproduced the profiles of a published respiratory microbiome study.

title: YAP1-induced super-enhancer rewiring mediates gene-environment-driven malignant reprogramming and metastatic ecosystem formation in head and neck cancer
synopsis: Uses integrated epigenomic profiling of mouse models and multiregion human HNSCC samples to track enhancer landscapes during tumor progression. Global chromatin architecture stays mostly stable, while YAP1 moves to newly formed super-enhancers with enhancer DNA hypomethylation; a YAP1–PITX2 axis drives partial EMT, fibroblast activation and lymph node metastasis.

title: nf-core/pairgenomealign: a scalable pipeline for pairwise whole-genome alignment
synopsis: With genome assemblies piling up, the authors built a community nf-core Nextflow pipeline for reproducible pairwise whole-genome alignment based on the LAST suite. It runs on local, HPC and cloud systems and outputs MAF/BAM/BCF/CRAM. It also packs many genomes aligned to one target into a single file that genome browsers can show directly. In benchmarks it is competitive with established aligners, with adjustable speed/sensitivity trade-offs.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
synopsis: Asks how pairs of chromosomal loci (e.g. enhancer and promoter) find each other in living cells. Combining live-cell imaging in Drosophila embryos and mouse ESCs with theory and polymer simulations, the authors show nearby loci move together far more than polymer models predict, due to ATP- and cohesin-dependent spatially correlated fluctuations. These fluctuations make encounters rarer but longer, a trade-off with direct consequences for enhancer–promoter communication.

title: Regularized ensemble polygenic risk prediction with GWAS summary statistics
synopsis: Current ensemble PRS methods, used as the final step of most multi-ancestry PRS tools, need individual-level genotypes to fit the ensemble weights, which are often unavailable for non-European groups. The authors build a regularized ensemble that combines many candidate PRS models using GWAS summary statistics alone. Across several traits and populations it beat state-of-the-art PRS methods both within and across ancestries, and new PRS models can be added to the ensemble easily.

title: Joint Associations of Cardiovascular Health and Polygenic Risk with Incident Cardiovascular Disease across the CKM Syndrome Continuum: A Prospective Cohort Study
synopsis: In 242,951 UK Biobank participants, the authors looked at how Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health and a CVD polygenic score jointly relate to incident CVD across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0-3. Ideal cardiovascular health was linked to about half the CVD risk (HR 0.47) in every genetic-risk group, with no weakening in advanced CKM stages. The effect of the polygenic score, by contrast, became stronger in later CKM stages.

title: A harmonized functional reference framework for GBA1
synopsis: Most rare GBA1 variants lack functional evidence, which makes them hard to interpret in Gaucher and Parkinson's disease. The authors used a multiplexed assay to measure lysosomal glucocerebrosidase activity for over 10,400 GBA1 variants, covering 97% of possible single amino-acid substitutions. Loss of function matched curated pathogenicity, flagged 94 of 186 VUS as impaired, and in GP2 data greater impairment was linked to earlier PD onset and higher PD odds ratios.

title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer
synopsis: A review of how to prioritize and validate non-coding variants in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. It covers in silico steps (GWAS fine-mapping, colocalisation, machine-learning functional annotation), epigenomic profiling (ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN) and experimental assays (reporter assays, EMSA, chromatin conformation capture, CRISPR perturbation).

title: Genetic regulation of ALK inhibitor response in diverse human cell types
synopsis: iPSC-derived heterogeneous differentiating cultures from 49 donors were treated with five ALK inhibitors and profiled by scRNA-seq to study genetic effects on drug response by cell type. The study maps 4,371 eQTLs across 21 cell types. Of these, 2,137 are response eQTLs whose effects differ between treated and untreated cells, giving candidate genes for ALK-inhibitor toxicity.

title: LAMP sheds light on how sequence to function models learn variant effects during post-training
synopsis: Sequence-to-function models such as Enformer underestimate causal variant effects, so they fine-map poorly and fine-tuning on personal genomes barely helps. LAMP inserts artificial, easy-to-learn SNVs that disrupt TF motifs into personal-genome data, and Enformer still fails to learn them on held-out genes and people. The authors trace this to pretrained priors that downweight distal enhancers and to motif-context variability, and propose data-augmentation strategies that substantially improve learning.

title: Joint Analysis of Common Regulatory and Rare Coding Variants for Improved Power in Kernel Association Tests
synopsis: Standard gene-based rare-variant tests ignore the common cis-regulatory background on which rare coding variants sit. PrediXSKAT adds PrediXcan-predicted gene expression to the SKAT kernel as a similarity weight, which concentrates rare-variant signal among individuals who share similar genetic and regulatory backgrounds. In simulations it kept type I error controlled and had more power than standard SKAT. In Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project WGS data it recovered known loci and strengthened signals at new candidate genes.

title: Projected clinical utility of polygenic risk score-stratified cancer screening: a systematic review
synopsis: This systematic review pooled 25 studies, mostly decision-analytic models, on PRS-stratified screening for breast, colorectal, prostate, lung and gastric cancer. Most models projected gains in QALYs, and some projected lower mortality or less overdiagnosis, but the extra benefit over uniform screening was modest and harms rose in the intensified high-risk groups. Certainty of evidence was very low throughout, so the authors say PRS-stratified screening should stay investigational until prospective trials are done.

title: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories
synopsis: The authors present Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that jointly uses age-varying effects of polygenic scores and monogenic variants on EHR disease histories, applied to 348 diseases, 36 PGS and 34 monogenic conditions in three biobanks. Allowing polygenic effects to change with age improved one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested (median AUC 0.95 vs 0.92) and found more new cases among the top 5% at risk. It also recovered known gene-disease links and timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2.

title: In Silico Prioritization of GWAS-Derived 3' UTR MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci Detected in Hispanic Patients from the All of Us Research Program
synopsis: The study screened 38 colorectal cancer GWAS variants in 3'UTRs, checked them in Hispanic All of Us participants and expanded them with Admixed-American LD proxies, then scored miRNA-binding effects with TargetScan and RNAhybrid. Nineteen variants in nine genes changed predicted miRNA binding. Risk alleles at DCBLD2, GREM1 and SMC1B break strong miRNA sites, which fits with these genes being overexpressed in tumours through lost miRNA repression rather than promoter changes.

title: A multi-tissue atlas of age-associated differential transcript usage in mouse reveals predominantly regulatory isoform switching across brain, liver, and adipose
synopsis: This atlas maps age-related differential transcript usage and isoform switching in mouse brain, liver and adipose, in natural aging and in Ercc1 progeroid mice. Many switches changed non-coding transcript features rather than protein sequence. With age, 3'UTRs lengthened overall in brain and shortened in adipose.

title: Hyperglycemia-responsive circRNA drives diabetic neuropathic pain by competing for PUM2 binding and promoting proNT3/CCL2 in DRG neurons
synopsis: The circular RNA cRps6kb1 rises in sensory (DRG) neurons in mouse models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes and in human donors with diabetic neuropathic pain. It competes with the Nt3 3'UTR for the translational repressor PUM2, which frees Nt3 mRNA and increases its stability and translation. This raises proNT3 and CCL2 and causes pain hypersensitivity; blocking the circRNA eased the pain.

title: Inferring chromatin looping interactions from microscopy-based measurements: opportunities and pitfalls
synopsis: Asks how reliably loop probability, lifetime and search time can be estimated from live-cell 3D distance trajectories. Using polymer simulations with known ground truth, the authors show that simple distance thresholding badly misestimates these parameters when localization error is close to the contact distance. Noise-aware inference methods recover the looping parameters much more accurately.

title: The Gata2 3'-distal region is essential for IL-3 responsiveness in basophil and mast cell progenitors
synopsis: Identifies G2DMBE, a GATA2-bound and acetylated enhancer 53 kb downstream of mouse Gata2 that is active in mast cells and basophils. Deleting it blunted Gata2 upregulation in progenitors and lowered expression of the IL-3 receptor beta-chain genes. As a result, IL-3-driven mast cell differentiation and basophil expansion were impaired.

title: Excluded causal variants produce false discoveries in genetic fine-mapping
synopsis: At 499 All of Us loci the author compares fine-mapping with and without the usual MAF < 1% and indel filters. 20-32% of high-confidence calls after filtering are not supported by the unfiltered analysis, because the signal of an omitted causal variant is moved to a tagging SNP (e.g. the blood group O frameshift). The new SuSiE-OUT model, or imputing the omitted variants, prevents most of these errors.

title: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping
synopsis: jaxQTL is a fast pseudobulk sc-eQTL framework built on count models (negative binomial). In OneK1K it found 16% more eGenes than linear models and ran much faster than single-cell Poisson mixed models. Fine-mapped sc-eQTLs lay further from the TSS and were more enriched in cell-type-specific enhancers than all-cell eQTLs.

title: ATP8B1-TMEM30B flippase activity maintains stereocilia lipid asymmetry required for hearing
synopsis: Because the MET channel proteins TMC1/2 scramble membrane lipids, the authors looked for a flippase that restores lipid asymmetry in hair cells. They found that the P4-ATPase ATP8B1 and its chaperone TMEM30B are expressed specifically in mouse outer hair cells and enriched in stereocilia. Knocking out either gene raised ABR thresholds, exposed phosphatidylserine and caused rapid outer hair cell loss, which makes TMEM30B a new deafness gene.

title: Genomic and multi-omic insights into the heterogeneity of diabetic kidney disease
synopsis: This review frames diabetic kidney disease as a heterogeneous condition and separates it from non-diabetic CKD in people with diabetes. It surveys how genomic, epigenomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures, polygenic scores, clustering and single-cell kidney atlases are being used to define endotypes. It also covers the remaining hurdles: validation, equitable ancestry representation and clinical implementation.

title: Overlapping enhancer activity robustly regulates rax expression during ocular development in zebrafish
synopsis: Maps five new ocular enhancers that reproduce rax expression at key stages of zebrafish eye development. Single and combined enhancer deletions showed that rax regulation is largely buffered by redundant enhancers. Some perturbations still caused microphthalmia or anophthalmia.

title: SPACE-Tag Enables High-Throughput Spatial Chromatin Profiling With CUT&Tag
synopsis: Presents SPACE-Tag, a spatial CUT&Tag method that turns histone-mark-tagged DNA into polyadenylated RNA so it can be read out on standard spatial transcriptomics platforms. The authors profiled five histone marks plus the transcriptome across the aging mouse brain. In the isocortex, an H3K4me1 module that grows with age was enriched at super-enhancers and tracked the upregulation of plasticity genes.

title: Optogenetic induction of TAD boundary pairing promotes gene activity
synopsis: Tests directly whether TAD structure affects transcription of the genes inside it. The authors built OptoTet, a light-controlled tool that forces the two boundaries of a TAD to pair without mutating or depleting proteins. Forced boundary pairing increased transcriptional bursting of ERRFI1 and partly rescued cohesin loss there, but left MYC unaffected, so the effect of boundary pairing depends on the gene.

title: Robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch
synopsis: RSparsePro is a probabilistic graphical model with variational inference for summary-statistic fine-mapping when the external LD reference does not match the GWAS sample. In simulations it gives credible sets with higher power and coverage than existing methods. In cis-pQTL and complex-trait loci its credible sets are more functionally enriched and replicate better across studies and LD panels.

title: Efficient and accurate mixed model association tool for single-cell eQTL analysis
synopsis: SAIGE-QTL is a Poisson mixed model that maps eQTLs directly on single-cell read counts, accounting for donor- and cell-level covariates and uneven cell numbers per donor. It is well calibrated and scalable, and in 1.2 million immune cells found 48.8% more eGenes than pseudobulk analysis. It also supports genome-wide trans-eQTL mapping and rare-variant set tests.

title: Metabolic syndrome, genetic susceptibility, and risk of cardiovascular disease: a prospective study in the UK Biobank
synopsis: In 385,036 UK Biobank participants, the authors studied how metabolic syndrome and a polygenic risk score jointly relate to incident cardiovascular outcomes. Metabolic syndrome raised risk of CVD, CHD, stroke, AF and heart failure, more strongly in women. The PRS was associated with CVD and CHD, and the joint effects suggested some additive interaction, though the authors call this exploratory.

title: Translation of a small upstream open reading frame functions as a rheostat for the regulation of lin-41 by the Let-7 microRNA in Caenorhabditis elegans
synopsis: The study asks how the modest repression by let-7, which binds two sites in the lin-41 3'UTR, combines with other mechanisms to control this dose-sensitive target in C. elegans. Using genome editing, it finds a separate repressive layer in somatic cells: a 5' regulatory exon with a seven-amino-acid uORF and structured 5'UTR that limits initiation at the main start codon. Together with let-7 this gives multi-tiered control that keeps LIN-41 at levels compatible with normal development (published version of a September 2026 bioRxiv preprint).

title: Leveraging short and long-read sequencing to comprehensively characterize alternatively polyadenylated and alternatively spliced transcripts
synopsis: Using mantle cell lymphoma as a model, the authors combined short- and long-read RNA-seq to catalogue transcripts produced by alternative polyadenylation and alternative splicing. Disease genes SOX11 and ATM made short-3'UTR isoforms, but transcriptome-wide 3'UTR shortening was not seen; both canonical and non-canonical polyA signals were used, and selected ones were confirmed experimentally. Long reads also turned up splice variants (e.g. PTEN, EZH2), and GLS1 was validated at the protein level and with GLS1 inhibitors.

title: PRISM-AD quantifies clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive risk prediction
synopsis: PRISM-AD combines nonlinear clinical functions with a polygenic risk score term to forecast progression from normal cognition to MCI and from MCI to Alzheimer's dementia in 4,435 European-ancestry participants. Overall accuracy matched logistic regression and adding the PRS did not significantly improve it. However, the modelled genetic contribution was higher in people who later developed AD at similar cognitive risk, which the authors present as exploratory.

title: Reference-Guided De Novo Retrieval of 3D Chromatin Organizational Features with Representation Learning
synopsis: Introduces C-Fetch, which finds instances of a user-defined contact-map pattern by learning from example patches instead of relying on a dedicated feature caller. A label-free 3D autoencoder trained on Hi-C and Micro-C patches ranks candidate patches by similarity to the examples. It retrieves Polycomb contacts, loops and domain-like patterns, improves on Mustache loop calls, and also works on Region Capture Micro-C and HiChIP data.

title: Single-nucleus chromatin accessibility time course of excisional wound repair in rat skin
synopsis: A data resource: single-nucleus ATAC-seq of rat skin before wounding and at five time points over 19 days of excisional wound repair. After QC, 37,555 nuclei across 23 cell types are available for studying regulatory element dynamics during healing.

title: NAD Metabolism Drives CTCF-Cohesin Chromatin Regulation in EBV-Transformed B-Cells
synopsis: Examines whether the high PARP1 activity in EBV-positive B cells, which consumes NAD+, connects metabolism to chromatin folding. EBV transformation depends on the NAD salvage pathway to keep PARP1 active and maintain CTCF-cohesin loops. Blocking NAMPT with FK866 disrupted chromatin architecture and loop extrusion in the same way as PARP1 loss, and reduced tumor growth in xenografts.

title: Acceleration of the GrimAge2 epigenetic clock is associated with atherogenic inflammageing and independently predicts acute coronary syndrome incremental to SCORE2-OP and PREVENT
synopsis: In 535 community-living Hong Kong adults aged 60-99, the authors tested whether blood DNA-methylation age acceleration adds to clinical ASCVD risk scores. Of five epigenetic clocks, GrimAge2 acceleration was most tied to atherogenic inflammageing and predicted ASCVD/acute coronary syndrome hospitalisation (11% higher hazard per year). Adding it raised the C-index of SCORE2-OP (0.693 to 0.734) and PREVENT (0.682 to 0.725).

title: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids
synopsis: Transcriptome and proteome profiling showed that three-week mouse brain organoids are close to neonatal mouse brain. The organoids reproduced most of the alternative splicing and polyA-site usage events that define neural identity in vivo. Most mRNA changes carried through to protein, including a complex network of synaptic proteins.

title: Association Between Saturated Fat Intake and Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Across the Genetic Spectrum
synopsis: Among 20,940 genotyped women in the Women's Health Initiative, the authors tested whether an LDL-C polygenic score changes how saturated fat intake relates to LDL-C and incident ASCVD. The polygenic score modified both associations: more saturated fat was linked to higher ASCVD risk only in the top PGS quartile (HR 1.26 per 5% of energy). This suggests genetic risk could help target dietary advice.

title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer
synopsis: Profiles Hi-C, ATAC-seq and RNA-seq in 18 clinical prostate samples (BPH, primary cancer, CRPC) with a framework that corrects A/B compartment calls for copy number and purity. Recurrent B-to-A compartment shifts occur in both primary and castration-resistant tumors and coincide with active marks, accessible chromatin bound by AR, FOXA1 and HOXB13, and cancer-associated genes such as PCA3.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Using a Polygenic Risk Score and DNA Methylation
synopsis: In two Korean cohorts (1,318 and 358 people), the authors trained machine-learning classifiers for prevalent type 2 diabetes using baseline features, then added a PRS and T2D-related CpG methylation. Each layer increased discrimination, and the full model reached AUROC 0.896 with greater net benefit in decision curve analysis. The PRS was the strongest single feature, while methylation features contributed most as a group.

title: Long-range chromatin interactions nominate candidate susceptibility genes at non-coding PDAC risk loci
synopsis: Links fine-mapped pancreatic cancer GWAS variants to target genes using a capture-based chromosome conformation method (GWAS Capture-C). Across 25 loci it nominated 273 candidate genes, including contacts longer than 1 Mb with KRT genes and a roughly 280 kb contact with SOX9. At 7p14.1, a roughly 900 kb contact with the INHBA promoter, an eQTL and CRISPRi of the fine-mapped variants together point to a distal enhancer that controls INHBA.

title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation
synopsis: Genetically multiplexed snATAC and snRNA profiles from 287 skeletal muscle biopsies found more than 7,000 eQTLs and 100,000 caQTLs across 13 cell types, including context-specific effects. Nearly 3,500 GWAS signals across 38 traits colocalized, mostly in a cell-specific way.

title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
synopsis: TenK10K phase 1 profiled more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types with matched WGS from 1,925 individuals, analysed with single-cell (not pseudobulk) models. Common regulatory variants were found for 83% of 21,404 genes tested, and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47%.

title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
synopsis: Published PRSs often transfer poorly to new cohorts and populations, so the authors recalibrate them locally: several published scores for a disease are combined and reweighted by machine learning according to how well each predicts in the target cohort. In the MGB Biobank, the locally optimized scores raised C-statistics by about 20% for coronary artery disease, 9% for prostate cancer and 8% for breast cancer compared with published scores. They also caught many more cases in the high-risk group, and the approach needs no new GWAS.

title: Genome-wide LD scores enable robust heritability and genetic correlation estimation from summary statistics across genetic ancestries
synopsis: SUMMIT uses genome-wide LD scores (computed with random projections that capture long-range LD) with summary statistics to estimate heritability, annotation enrichment and genetic correlation in structured and admixed cohorts. In UK Biobank EUR, SAS and admixed AFR samples it is less biased than prior methods and closer to WGS-based estimates. It finds many more cross-trait genetic correlations in non-European groups than cov-LDSC.

title: Functional architecture of rare protein coding variation across 786,871 exomes
synopsis: KASM combines many functional annotations into a kernel describing how allelic effects covary within a gene, and was applied to 26 traits in 786,871 UK Biobank and All of Us exomes with 35 structural and predictive annotations. Rare missense heritability was at least 1.27% on average, exceeding pLoF heritability (0.87%) and earlier missense burden estimates (0.54%). AlphaMissense was the most enriched single predictor, but a composite score doubled its enrichment.

title: Genomic foundation models do not yet boost common variant discovery beyond standard functional annotations
synopsis: The authors test whether annotations from AlphaGenome, Borzoi or GPN-Star help functionally informed GWAS discovery (surrogate functional FDR) across 27 UK Biobank traits. AlphaGenome and Borzoi increase locus discovery less than baselineLD does, and GPN-Star decreases it. Adding foundation-model annotations to baselineLD gives no further gain.

title: Sequence-based variant-effect predictions reveal trait-specific regulatory-layer profiles of complex-trait heritability
synopsis: AlphaGenome Atlas predictions are grouped into 12 lineages and 6 regulatory layers and used as S-LDSC annotations for 11 traits. Which layer is most informative differs by trait: predicted DNase effects for height and bone density, predicted CAGE effects for Alzheimer's, brain traits and cholesterol. CAGE predictions stay informative after conditioning on fine-mapped eQTLs.

title: The landscape of polygenic score prediction accuracy and transportability across the phenome in ancestrally diverse populations
synopsis: Evaluates 3,994 published PGSs across the phenome in the ancestrally diverse CCPM biobank; predictive effects frequently differ across ancestry groups; accuracy/portability depend on continuous vs thresholded use; mixed models identify score-development, genome and cohort features linked to better portability.

title: A common germline 3' UTR variant controls DDIT4 translation efficiency and stress responses in cancer cells
synopsis: The authors built a pipeline that compares total and polysome-bound mRNA to find common SNPs that change ribosome loading without changing mRNA level. Their lead hit, the DDIT4 3'UTR variant rs1053639, changes binding of the RNA-binding protein RBMX, which alters DDIT4 mRNA localization, translation and protein output in edited cells. The alleles differ in mTORC1 repression under stress, autophagy, fitness in co-culture and xenografts, and drug response, and genotype was linked to outcome in colorectal cancer.

title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney
synopsis: Kidzoi adapts the Borzoi sequence-to-function model to human kidney single-nucleus chromatin accessibility through transfer learning, so it predicts cell-type-specific regulatory activity. It improves regulatory variant effect prediction in proximal tubule cells by up to 23% AUROC over existing models. It also prioritizes fine-mapped eGFR GWAS variants and resolves the cell types they act in, and only 32-64 kb of flanking sequence is needed.

title: A heritability-optimized method for functional prioritization of rare coding variants in complex traits
synopsis: RovHer scores the probability that a rare missense variant is functional by learning from exome-wide association statistics of 4.9 million rare variants with 75 variant- and gene-level features. Across 21 traits in up to 357,086 UK Biobank participants, the top 1% of RovHer-ranked missense variants explained on average 16.1% of rare-variant heritability, a 10-fold gain over seven alternative methods. Its predictions were independent of allele frequency and generalized in multi-ancestry replication.

title: GeneSIS: enhancing transferability of polygenic scores with variant-level gene-by-sex interaction effects
synopsis: GeneSIS jointly models additive and gene-by-sex effects at variant level from individual data (UKB, 406,659, 99 traits); modeling GxS improves prediction for 32 traits in non-European individuals, e.g. 3.7-fold for hip circumference in Africans.

title: All of Us diversity and scale yield context-dependent improvements in polygenic prediction
synopsis: Multiancestry PRSs for 32 traits using 245,388 All of Us WGS plus UK Biobank; AoU diversity improved accuracy especially in under-represented groups; for less polygenic traits AoU-only training was best in African ancestry; accuracy decays linearly with ancestry divergence, attenuated by multiancestry training.

title: SPLENDID incorporates continuous genetic ancestry in biobank-scale data to improve polygenic risk prediction across diverse populations
synopsis: SPLENDID: penalized regression modeling genetic ancestry as a continuum to give one model without ancestry labels; in All of Us (n=224,364) and UKB (n=340,140) improves accuracy over existing methods, especially for non-European and admixed individuals.

title: Beyond exons: Linking noncoding heritability and polygenicity across complex human traits and disorders
synopsis: Using a MiXeR-based framework, the authors partition the heritability of 34 traits across 74 functional annotations. Exons carry a minority of heritability, which falls from about 22% in less polygenic traits to 13% in highly polygenic psychiatric and cognitive traits. Highly polygenic traits lean more on conservation and variant-effect annotations, less polygenic ones on promoter and chromatin annotations.

title: Systematic benchmarking of multi-ancestry fine-mapping under variant heterogeneity and LD mismatch
synopsis: Nine multi-ancestry fine-mapping methods are benchmarked using UK Biobank-based simulations and All of Us data. Joint models have the best power for causal variants shared across ancestries. Post-hoc integration is more robust for ancestry-specific variants, and all methods lose power under LD mismatch. The authors propose a locus-adaptive strategy for choosing between the two approaches.

title: Whole-exome sequencing in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder and chronic tic disorders identifies 36 large-effect risk genes
lab: the Tourette International Collaborative Genetics (TIC Genetics)
synopsis: Exome analysis of 3,964 people with OCD and/or chronic tic disorders (2,418 trios) found an excess of de novo and rare damaging variants and 36 high-confidence risk genes at FDR < 0.1. Several genes overlap with OCD GWAS loci and with other neurodevelopmental disorders, extending SCHEMA-style rare-variant gene discovery to OCD and tics.

title: Efficient genome-wide mapping of reproducible, context-dependent eQTLs at single-cell resolution
synopsis: Dynema uses a Poisson model with cluster-robust variance estimators to map context-dependent and context-independent eQTLs without pseudobulking. It is calibrated and scales genome-wide. In two independent T-cell datasets it found reproducible cell-state-dependent eQTLs, some missed by pseudobulk approaches.

title: Deciphering the mechanisms of transcriptome remodeling in residual HCC recurrence post-radiofrequency ablation via long-read sequencing
synopsis: The authors used Nanopore long-read RNA-seq on paired hepatocellular carcinoma tumour and adjacent tissue from five patients, before and after incomplete radiofrequency ablation, to profile expression, transcript usage and APA. Incomplete ablation reshaped the APA landscape. Oncogenes such as SAE1 and SPINK1 had APA-driven 3'UTR changes that may stabilise transcripts and help them escape miRNAs, alongside overexpression of proliferation genes and isoform switches in DNA-repair genes.

title: Cell-type-specific eQTLs underlie the genetic architecture of complex traits
synopsis: A variance-component model applied to OneK1K PBMC scRNA-seq characterizes cell-type-specific eQTLs without bias. Cell-type-specific eQTLs, but not shared ones, were enriched for complex-trait heritability, and specificity tracked with selective constraint, enhancer complexity and network connectivity. Trans-eQTLs were mostly cell-type-specific.

title: Methylation profile scores in child and adolescent health: a practical guide
synopsis: A practical review of how methylation profile scores are used in children and adolescents: as exposure proxies, biological proxies, risk stratifiers, diagnostics and treatment monitors. It explains why developmental context changes score behaviour, gives criteria for judging pediatric studies, and concludes that most scores are still research tools rather than clinical tests.

title: Mapping the NFYA 3'UTR landscape identifies alternative polyadenylation as a targetable vulnerability in prostate cancer
source: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
synopsis: The study asks whether APA changes NFYA output in prostate cancer, using bulk, single-cell and 3'-end sequencing to re-annotate and quantify its four 3'UTR isoforms. Tumours showed NFYA 3'UTR shortening that tracked grade, metastasis, higher NF-YA protein and proliferation, while quiescence and enzalutamide caused lengthening; long isoforms lowered protein through reduced stability, poorer translation and nuclear retention, not through more miRNA repression. Forcing 3'UTR lengthening with CRISPR deletion or ASOs that mask polyA signals lowered NF-YA and reduced aggressive traits in vitro and in vivo.

title: Novel prediabetes subtypes and genetic variants predict differential risk of progression to type 2 diabetes: a data-driven cohort analysis
synopsis: In 1,016 Thai adults with prediabetes, the authors clustered clinical and metabolic variables into four subtypes with very different rates of progression to type 2 diabetes. They then tested SNP-by-cluster interactions and a polygenic risk score within each cluster. Genetic risk refined stratification, especially within the metabolic-syndrome and low-risk clusters, which supports combining phenotypic and genetic risk.

title: Integrated Analysis of Skeletal Muscle Transcriptional Networks Characterizes Dysregulation in Pathways and Trait-Associated Regulatory Regions in Type 2 Diabetes
synopsis: The study asks which pathways and driver genes are dysregulated in skeletal muscle in type 2 diabetes. WGCNA on 301 muscle biopsies gave 56 modules, which were annotated with snRNA-seq cell-type signatures and transcription-factor networks and linked to snATAC-seq regulatory elements. Muscle-fiber and endothelial modules were enriched for T2D and related-trait GWAS signals, and the work names candidate drivers such as ATP5L, SIRT1, JAM2 and IRF8.

title: Risk factor control and type 2 diabetes event risks in people with high genetic susceptibility to diabetes
synopsis: In 382,313 UK Biobank participants, the authors looked at how a T2D polygenic risk score and the number of six well-controlled modifiable risk factors (smoking, activity, diet, sleep, BMI, blood pressure) jointly relate to incident type 2 diabetes. People at high genetic risk who controlled all six factors had lower T2D risk than people at low genetic risk (HR 0.79). Prediabetes, however, kept risk raised even when all factors were controlled.

title: Genetic determinants of serum creatinine and cystatin C independent of kidney function generate bias in filtration markers
synopsis: Using UK Biobank GWAS, the authors separated loci that affect creatinine or cystatin C levels without affecting GFR: 52 creatinine-specific and 48 cystatin C-specific loci, linked to muscle metabolism and inflammation respectively. Polygenic scores built from these loci quantify the genetic bias in eGFR for each individual. This bias differed by self-reported race and was validated against measured GFR in two cohorts.

title: Leukocyte DNA methylation-based signatures for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in the Million Veteran Program
synopsis: Built elastic-net methylation risk scores for incident ASCVD in 44,674 Million Veteran Program participants, using one subcohort for EWAS-based CpG selection and another for training and testing. The scores roughly doubled hazard per SD and modestly improved discrimination and reclassification beyond clinical risk factors.

title: Scalable context-dependent single-cell eQTL mapping reveals disease-relevant regulatory variation beyond static models
synopsis: CASTIE is a Poisson mixed-model framework that tests genotype-by-context interactions genome-wide on single-cell counts. In 1.2 million PBMCs from 982 OneK1K donors it found 3,155 context-dependent eQTLs, including 2,022 eGenes with no static effect. These gave 374 GWAS colocalizations across 94 traits, 197 of them missed by static eQTLs.

title: SuSiNE: Genetic fine-mapping with signed functional priors and multi-basin ensembling
synopsis: SuSiNE extends SuSiE with signed functional annotations (e.g. AlphaGenome effect directions) as a prior mean. It runs over many variational optima and combines them, and shows that purity filtering can throw away real signal. In calibrated simulations it raises AUPRC for the main causal variants from 0.25 to 0.31, and it changes the top variants at several GTEx lung loci.

title: The CTCF Paralog BORIS Contributes to the Ovarian Cancer Transcriptional Program by Relaxing CTCF-mediated 3D Genome Organization
synopsis: Studies how the germ-cell CTCF paralog BORIS (CTCFL), which is switched on in ovarian cancer, affects 3D genome organization. Losing BORIS binding collapsed a BORIS-dependent transcriptional program in clustered neighbouring genes and changed CTCF/cohesin occupancy, histone marks and accessibility. Without BORIS, TAD insulation, A/B compartments and loops became stronger, which suggests BORIS loosens CTCF-mediated insulation to reprogram transcription.

title: Polygenic risk-informed white matter integrity improves deep learning-based prediction of youth depression
synopsis: The authors pretrained a 3D convolutional network on diffusion MRI white-matter maps using polygenic risk scores as targets in 4,741 ABCD youths, then fine-tuned it to predict current and two-year depression and suicidality. The combined genetics-plus-imaging model beat genetics-only and brain-only models (AUC 0.61-0.66). It generalised to an independent Korean youth sample (AUC 0.67).

title: Stress-Related Methylation Risk Scores Predict Coronary Heart Disease
synopsis: Ran an EWAS of stressful life events in 3,857 Women's Health Initiative participants and built stress methylation risk scores from 841 and 13 CpGs. The scores predicted incident coronary heart disease (HR ~1.35) and mediated ~17% of the stress-CHD association; the 13-CpG score replicated in JHS and MESA, and deconvolution pointed to monocytes.

title: Uromodulin T62P variant causes kidney tubular stress and injury modulated by age and polygenic risk
synopsis: In 882,306 people from UK Biobank, All of Us and MyCode, the intermediate-effect UMOD T62P variant raised CKD risk in an age-dependent way. In tubular cells, T62P caused defective uromodulin maturation, ER retention and ER stress. Penetrance was strongly modified by a genome-wide polygenic score: carriers in the top score quintile had about 5-fold higher CKD risk than the population average.

title: External validation of four breast cancer risk prediction models for personalized screening in a prospective Dutch screening cohort
synopsis: The study tested how well Gail, BCSC, BOADICEA and IBIS predict 5-year breast cancer risk in 38,767 women from the Dutch PRISMA screening cohort, using questionnaire risk factors and breast density but no genetic data. BCSC, BOADICEA and IBIS discriminated only modestly (C-index about 0.60); BCSC and BOADICEA were well calibrated, IBIS overpredicted and Gail did worst. The authors conclude that better models, for example ones adding more data, are needed before risk-based screening is rolled out nationally.

title: ELF3 links kidney function GWAS loci to maladaptive epithelial inflammation
synopsis: This study identifies ELF3 as the effector gene at a kidney function GWAS locus. ELF3 is induced in injured proximal tubule cells in mouse models and human CKD, and in those cells it amplifies inflammation through noncanonical NF-kB signalling. Deleting Elf3 after injury reduced injured-tubule accumulation, cytokines and immune infiltration, and ELF3 levels tracked disease progression in human kidneys.

title: Impact of African-enriched GATM regulatory variants on creatinine-derived estimated glomerular filtration rate
synopsis: Whole-genome sequencing in Ugandan and South African cohorts, combined with eQTL, metabolomic and iohexol-measured GFR data, showed that common African-enriched GATM variants raise creatine synthesis and serum creatinine. Each allele lowers creatinine-based eGFR by about 2 ml/min/1.73m2 without changing measured GFR or cystatin C eGFR. In Million Veteran Program African Americans, these variants increased CKD diagnoses but not kidney failure.

title: PRANA: A Deep Learning Method for Adapting Polygenic Risk Scores to Diverse Ethnic Groups
synopsis: PRANA deep-learning framework that adapts a European-trained PRS to other ancestries using modest target cohorts; across seven traits in South Asian, East Asian and Ashkenazi Jewish populations improves beta and R2 by ~5-20% and mostly outperforms cross-ancestry multi-PRS approaches.

title: Scalable penalized regression boosts accuracy and computational efficiency for single- and cross-ancestry polygenic prediction
synopsis: Spike-and-slab lassosum ensembles: SSL (single ancestry) and pSSL (borrowing European GWAS) for cross-ancestry PGS; across 32 traits in UKB and Chinese DFTJ cohort, pSSL ranked first for 71.9% of traits with +12.3% R2 over PRS-CSx, at under one-third the runtime.

title: Improved heritability partitioning and enrichment analyses using summary statistics with graphREML
synopsis: graphREML is a likelihood-based alternative to S-LDSC for heritability partitioning. It uses sparse LD graphical models to make the likelihood tractable on summary statistics. Its enrichment estimates agree with S-LDSC, but it finds about 2.5 times more significant trait-annotation enrichments and gives calibrated per-SNP heritabilities.

title: Multiple instance fine-mapping: Predicting causal regulatory variants with a deep sequence model
synopsis: MIFM is a multiple-instance-learning objective that groups variants in LD into weakly labelled bags. It is used to train a deep sequence classifier of causal variants on more than 13,000 GWAS. PRSs built from MIFM-prioritized variants transfer better across ancestries, and the model helps separate the effects of highly correlated variants.

title: Blood DNA methylation and breast cancer risk: a prospective nested case-control study
synopsis: Profiled pre-diagnostic blood methylation in 377 women who later developed breast cancer and 378 controls from Swedish screening and built a 22-CpG methylation risk score that validated across regions. The score performed about as well as a polygenic score, held for up to five years before diagnosis, and improved 3-5-year discrimination of established risk models.

title: Atlas of glomerular disease-specific genetic effects on blood transcriptome
synopsis: The authors paired whole-genome sequencing with blood RNA-seq in 1,822 CureGN patients with five types of primary glomerulonephritis to map disease-specific eQTLs, sQTLs and RNA-editing QTLs. They found 16,068 eGenes; about 90% of signals were shared across diseases and 5-10% were specific to one, and thousands were absent from GTEx. Interaction QTLs with age, eGFR and proteinuria, plus GWAS integration, nominated new candidate genes for each disease.

title: Live imaging and multimodal profiling reveal transdifferentiation of a cochlear supporting cell subpopulation upon Notch inhibition
synopsis: Why do neonatal cochlear supporting cells rarely regenerate hair cells? Live imaging and single-cell multiomics of Notch-inhibited mouse cochlear explants showed that Notch repression silenced supporting-cell genes broadly. However, only a rare subpopulation of Deiters' cells (tDCs) began converting to hair cells, through coordinated transcriptional and enhancer remodeling, while other supporting cells stayed refractory.

title: Population-scale genomics reveals divergent pathogenicity of variant classes across paralogous collagen IV genes
synopsis: Using whole-genome sequences from about 500,000 UK Biobank participants, replicated in All of Us, the authors tested COL4A3 and COL4A4 rare variants against haematuria, proteinuria and CKD. Glycine substitutions carried similar risk in both genes, but truncating and NC1-domain missense variants were strongly pathogenic only in COL4A4. This argues that gene identity, not just variant class, should guide interpretation and counselling for collagen IV variants.

title: Distinct and shared genetics of kidney filtration function versus albuminuria revealed by multi-trait GWAS
synopsis: A multi-trait GWAS of eGFR and UACR in about 1 million people found 812 signals and used multi-trait fine-mapping to sharpen the likely causal variants. Of 333 signals assigned to one trait, only 11 affected both filtration and albuminuria, so their genetics are largely separate. The shared signals point to glomerular filtration area (SHROOM3, EPB41L5) and sodium-driven intraglomerular pressure (NRBP1, DPEP1/CHMP1A), and fluid-intake loci were found to create spurious UACR effects.

title: MIXPRS enables multi-population and multi-method polygenic risk scores using summary statistics
synopsis: MIXPRS combines multiple multi-population PRS methods using only GWAS summary statistics (data fission, SNP pruning, NNLS weights); improves accuracy over existing methods across up to 26 traits; MIXPRS+ adds annotations/clinical PRSs for further gains in non-Europeans.

title: Cell-type-resolved genetic variation shapes inflammatory bowel disease risk
synopsis: cis-eQTLs mapped in 2.2 million cells from intestinal biopsies and blood of 421 people (125 with IBD). Cell-type eQTLs were more distal, enhancer-enriched and over 3.5-fold more likely to colocalize with IBD GWAS loci than tissue-level eQTLs, nominating effector genes at over half of known IBD loci.

title: DiscoDivas: Leveraging genetic-ancestry continuum information to interpolate PRS for admixed populations
synopsis: DiscoDivas interpolates a harmonized PRS along a continuous genetic-ancestry space using genetic distance and multiple ancestry-tuned PRS models; performs comparable to or better than conventional ancestry-matched fine-tuning, with largest gains in admixed individuals.

title: MetaSTAARlite: an all-in-one tool for biobank-scale whole-genome sequencing meta-analysis
synopsis: MetaSTAARlite is a summary-statistics pipeline for functionally informed rare-variant meta-analysis of coding and noncoding regions across biobanks, without sharing individual-level data. Using UK Biobank and All of Us WGS data, its compute time, memory and storage scaled linearly with sample size, and its results were highly concordant with a pooled analysis.

title: A large-scale single cell map of primary and conditional regulatory variation in the human brain
synopsis: snRNA-seq from 956 postmortem brains (4.8 million nuclei, seven cell types) with matched WGS. In 763 European-ancestry donors it found sc-eQTLs for 32,189 eGenes plus 6,174 conditionally independent secondary signals, aiming to resolve GWAS loci that do not colocalize with primary eQTLs.

title: Evaluating confounding in rare variant genome wide association studies
synopsis: Using 306,991 UK Biobank exomes, the authors show that recent demography is poorly captured by common- and rare-variant principal components, and that accounting for haplotype sharing does not remove false-positive rare-variant associations with non-heritable, spatially structured traits. Sibling re-analysis of 155 phenotypes showed more effect-size bias for non-uniformly distributed traits, and bias for height was driven mainly by assortative mating. Family-based designs are proposed as sensitivity analyses for rare-variant studies.

title: Mapping Genetic Risk Associations to Cellular Contexts via Deep Learning and Biological Ontologies
synopsis: Linking GWAS signals to the cell types and tissues where they act is hard because of the complex regulatory code and linkage disequilibrium between associated variants. The proposed framework combines deep learning predictions of how noncoding variants affect transcriptional regulatory elements across GWAS loci, tests these aggregated scores for significance empirically, and arranges them within biological ontologies. The result is statistically calibrated mapping of trait associations to relevant cell-type and tissue contexts across human traits.

title: New mechanistic insights from alignment of accessible chromatin and renal lineage factor DNA-binding with genetics of kidney function
synopsis: The authors overlapped credible eGFR GWAS variants with accessible chromatin across 29 human tissues and found strong overlap with liver and kidney regulatory elements. Variants were enriched at sites bound by the tubular lineage factor HNF-1beta, which resolved several signals to likely target genes. A polymorphic NDRG1 enhancer bound HNF-1beta differently by allele and regulated tubule cell growth and migration.

title: The Biobank Rare Variant consortium powers the discovery of rare genetic associations through global collaboration
synopsis: The BRaVa consortium meta-analyzed gene-based rare coding variant tests across ten biobanks and cohorts (over 1.2 million individuals of diverse ancestries) for 33 clinical endpoints and 11 quantitative traits. It found 514 gene-trait associations, 31 previously unreported; 36.1% were undetectable in any single biobank and 91 emerged only in cross-ancestry meta-analysis. Effect sizes were correlated across ancestries with concordant directions.

title: Paediatric DNA methylation profile scores: a systematic review and open-source atlas
synopsis: Systematically reviewed 119 early-life studies covering 828 methylation profile scores and found wide heterogeneity and frequent mismatches in age, tissue, platform and ancestry between training and application. The authors launch DEMETRA, a searchable atlas to help choose suitable pediatric scores.

title: An efficient LASSO framework for admixture-aware polygenic scores
synopsis: HAUDI reparameterizes the local-ancestry-aware GAUDI model as a standard LASSO, extending to multiway admixture with large speedups; outperforms GAUDI across 18 clinical phenotypes and beats ancestry-agnostic PGS for WBC and CKD; faster and more accurate than SDPR_admix.

title: FastGxC: Fast and powerful context-specific eQTL mapping in bulk and single-cell data
synopsis: FastGxC maps context-specific eQTLs by exploiting correlation across contexts; in simulations it was 9x more powerful and 10^6x faster than existing methods. Applied to multi-tissue bulk data (n=698) and PBMC scRNA-seq (n=1,218), its eQTLs showed 4-fold enrichment in context-matched open chromatin and expanded candidate causal genes by 25%.

title: DNA methylation signatures associated with bipolar disorder in peripheral blood improve prediction models
synopsis: Ran the largest blood EWAS of bipolar disorder to date (1,729 cases, 1,747 controls, 12 cohorts) and built polymethylation scores. The score explained ~2% of case-control variance (4.9% for bipolar I) and added to polygenic scores; schizophrenia and depression scores also tracked bipolar status.

title: Systematic common and rare variant association testing in 392,030 whole genomes in All of Us
synopsis: This 'All by All' analysis ran GWAS and rare-variant association tests on 3,602 phenotypes in 392,030 All of Us v8 genomes, finding 49,863 approximately independent single-variant and gene-level associations. Meta-analysis with UK Biobank (up to 786,871 participants) found 193 pLoF gene-phenotype associations not significant in either cohort alone. Results are shared through a public browser and a Researcher Workbench workspace.

title: Empirically determined baseline masking strategies and other considerations for gene-level burden tests
synopsis: The study asks how the choice of variant masks (annotation and frequency filters) changes gene-level burden test results. A literature review catalogued 664 masks across 234 studies, and applying all of them to 54 traits in 189,947 UK Biobank exomes gave between 58 and 2,523 significant associations, which explains the low (<30%) overlap between published analyses of the same data. The authors derive empirically high-power baseline masking strategies to improve power and replicability.

title: Admixture-informed polygenic risk reporting using the ePRS framework
lab: the Consortium Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine
synopsis: ePRS framework: expected PRS given global/local admixture, and residual PRS (rPRS) as ancestry-agnostic liability; in TOPMed and All of Us, adjusting for ePRS yields nearly unbiased PRS-outcome estimates without PCs, supporting equitable risk reporting.

title: Integrating common and rare variants improves polygenic risk prediction across diverse populations
synopsis: Notably, for lipid traits, RICE captures substantial predictive signal beyond established high-penetrance genes, validating its ability to leverage the broader polygenic architecture of rare variation.

title: Leveraging cell-type specificity and similarity improves single-cell eQTL fine-mapping
synopsis: CASE is a Bayesian framework that fine-maps eQTLs across multiple cell types at once, capturing effect sharing while handling LD. It outperformed SuSiE and mvSuSiE in simulations. On OneK1K it found more regulatory effects with better cell-type specificity and stronger functional and disease enrichment.

title: Analysis of rare coding variants in schizophrenia-associated genes and generalised cognition in the UK Biobank
synopsis: Tested whether rare variants in schizophrenia risk genes affect general cognition (g) in 76,783 UK Biobank exomes from people without schizophrenia. Protein-truncating variants in SCHEMA-type rare-variant genes, and damaging missense variants in common-variant credible genes, were associated with lower g, suggesting that cognitive impairment and schizophrenia partly share biology.

title: Damaging missense variants in innate immunity genes are associated with earlier age of breast cancer onset in BRCA1 185delAG carriers
synopsis: Common-variant polygenic risk scores explain under 10% of risk variability in BRCA1 carriers, so other genetic modifiers of breast cancer onset age must exist. Whole-exome sequencing of 321 Israeli women carrying the BRCA1 185delAG founder variant found that extra putatively damaging missense variants in innate immunity genes were linked to earlier diagnosis. Variants in the NATURAL_KILLER_CELL_ACTIVATION gene set gave HR 3.62 (95% CI 1.96–6.67; p=3.8×10^-5).

title: Genome-wide fine-mapping improves identification of causal variants
synopsis: Instead of fine-mapping one locus at a time, the authors fine-map the whole genome jointly with functional annotations (GWFM). It beats locus-based methods on error control, power, resolution and replication. Across 48 traits its credible sets explain about 18% of SNP heritability, 30% of them lie outside genome-wide significant loci, and fine-mapping half of the heritability is projected to need about 2 million samples.

title: Rare coding and noncoding variants map 1,342 diseases and biomarkers in 490,549 whole genomes
synopsis: The authors developed STAARpipelinePheWAS and tested rare coding and noncoding variants against 1,342 phenotypes (944 diseases, 76 clinical biomarkers, 322 metabolomic traits) in up to 490,549 UK Biobank genomes. They identified 49,121 genome-wide significant gene-trait pairs, many missed by earlier exome- or array-based studies and enriched in drug targets. All results are public through an interactive portal.

title: Systematic assessment of machine learning-based variant annotation methods for rare variant association testing
synopsis: The study benchmarks five variant annotation methods (CADD v1.6, CADD v1.7, AlphaMissense, ESM-1b, GPN-MSA) for gene-level rare-variant tests across 14 traits in up to 350,377 UK Biobank participants, using a Wasserstein-distance framework to quantify calibration and power. CADD-based tests gave the best signal separation, AlphaMissense-based tests were systematically less well calibrated, and GPN-MSA-based tests showed the highest enrichment in LoF-intolerant genes.

title: A meta-analysis of single-nucleus expression quantitative trait loci linking genetic risk to brain disorders
synopsis: SingleBrain meta-analyses snRNA-seq plus genotypes from four cohorts (5.8 million nuclei, 983 individuals), mapping cis- and trans-eQTLs across brain cell types and subtypes, including disease- and sex-specific eQTLs. It found up to 10-fold more cis-eQTLs and used colocalization and MR to link cell-type-specific genes to neurological disease.

title: Biobank-Scale Polygenic Prediction in Admixed Populations Using Local Ancestry via the Group Lasso
synopsis: Combine: biobank-scale group-lasso regression adding local-ancestry dosages to genotype features; in 99,298 admixed All of Us participants it substantially outperforms summary-statistic multi-ancestry methods (e.g., +144% vs PRS-CSx for WBC) and matches iPGS/snpnet for 7 of 9 traits.

title: Massive-scale single-nucleus multi-omics identifies novel rare noncoding drivers of Parkinson’s disease
synopsis: Preprint pairing 30x WGS with single-nucleus multi-omics (>3.3 million nuclei, 5 brain regions, 80 PD cases and 21 controls) to map cell-type-specific regulatory QTLs and train models that predict the regulatory effects of variants. Using these predictions it nominates rare noncoding variants associated with sporadic PD and candidate drivers in unexplained familial PD.

title: Scalable and accurate rare-variant association tests for whole genome sequencing time-to-event analysis in large biobanks
source: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
synopsis: GATE-STAAR is a frailty-model framework for rare-variant association tests of time-to-event outcomes (such as age at diagnosis) in WGS biobanks; it handles heavy censoring, cryptic relatedness and population structure and uses functional annotations. A rare-variant saddlepoint approximation addresses heavy censoring, and simulations showed good power with controlled type I error. Applied to ~400,000 UK Biobank genomes with validation in All of Us, it found rare-variant associations with age at diagnosis of a range of diseases.

title: Practical utility of sequence-to-omics models for improving the reproducibility of genetic fine-mapping
synopsis: The authors test whether sequence-to-omics models (AlphaGenome, Borzoi, Enformer, Sei) make eQTL fine-mapping more reproducible across GTEx, TOPMed and MAGE. Purely statistical fine-mapping often fails to replicate. Combining PIPs with model scores into functionally informed PIPs (fiPIPs) clearly lowers replication failure, with the most benefit from AlphaGenome and Borzoi.

title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome
synopsis: AlphaGenome is a single deep learning model that avoids the usual trade-off between sequence length and resolution: it reads 1 Mb of DNA and predicts thousands of genomic tracks, down to single base pairs. These cover expression, transcription initiation, accessibility, histone marks, TF binding, contact maps and splicing. Trained on human and mouse genomes, it matched or beat the best external models in 25 of 26 variant-effect benchmarks and recovered the mechanisms of clinical variants near TAL1.

title: Comprehensive benchmarking single and multi ancestry polygenic score methods with the PGS-hub platform
synopsis: Benchmarks 13 single- and multi-ancestry PGS methods across 36 traits in UKB European and African samples; LDpred2 best single-ancestry; PRS-CSx and X-Wing comparable, LDpred2-multi outperforms both; LD reference size matters below ~5,000; releases the PGS-hub platform.

title: A novel age-informative polygenic score improves predictive ability for kidney function and kidney function decline
synopsis: The authors built an eGFR polygenic score that gives each of 282 kidney-function SNPs age-specific weights through main and interaction effects, and tested it in UK Biobank and the KORA/AugUR cohorts. It explained more eGFR variance than an age-agnostic score in both young and old people, and better captured eGFR decline. Population-level separation of decline by score was similar to that of diabetes or albuminuria, but individual-level prediction remained poor.

title: Federated single-cell QTL meta-analysis reveals novel disease mechanisms
synopsis: A federated meta-analysis of 12 PBMC cohorts (2,032 individuals, 2.5 million cells) found cis-eQTLs for 6,592 genes and fine-mapped 14,985 loci across six immune cell types. The 42% of eQTLs missed by a 43,301-sample whole-blood bulk study were more enriched for GWAS loci, and anchoring bulk trans-eQTLs to sc cis-eQTLs linked 6,382 trans-eGenes to upstream regulators.
