title: Improving polygenic score prediction for underrepresented groups through transfer learning
synopsis: GPTL R package with three transfer-learning approaches (early-stopped gradient descent, penalized shrinkage to priors, Bayesian finite-mixture prior); in UKB and All of Us, outperforms single-ancestry PGS and often matches/exceeds multi-ancestry ensembles.

title: Cross-Ancestry Polygenic Prediction: Comparing Methods and Assessing Transferability Across Traits
synopsis: Compares seven cross-ancestry PGS methods for five traits in UKB; GBLUP and PRS-CSx best for highly polygenic traits (height, BMI), PRSice and PolyPred best for cholesterol; using SNPs with concordant effect direction across ancestries improves cross-ancestry accuracy.

title: Blood-based DNA methylation captures variance in adult height
synopsis: Used Bayesian penalised regression (BayesR+) in 7,654 Generation Scotland participants to estimate how much height variance blood methylation captures beyond genetics, then built a methylation profile score. Methylation captured ~25% of height variance, yet the out-of-sample score correlated only weakly with height (r 0.14-0.26), which argues against labelling traits 'null' from EWAS results alone.

title: Integrative kidney multi-omics traces genetic drivers of chronic kidney disease to targets within the renal epigenome, transcriptome and proteome
synopsis: GWAS meta-analyses of four CKD-defining traits in up to 890,000 people found 508 loci, 237 of them shared across traits. Colocalization with kidney mRNA, protein and DNA-methylation QTLs nominated 651 kidney genes, 330 of them new, and pointed to genetically regulated developmental methylation. Follow-up of the new gene CA12 linked its loss to hyperuricemia and lower kidney function, which has implications for acetazolamide.

title: A multiscale framework for hypothesis generation from sex-stratified X-linked gene networks
synopsis: The authors propose a reproducible pipeline for comparing gene co-expression networks between groups. It combines cohort balancing, bootstrap consensus networks, topology statistics, paired permutations and multiple-testing control. Applied to 90 sex-stratified networks of X-linked genes in 15 TCGA cancers, it found no differences that survived correction but flagged exploratory graphlet patterns to test in other cohorts.

title: SurvSTAAR: A Powerful Statistical Framework for Rare Variant Analysis of Time-to-Event Traits in Large-Scale Whole-Genome Sequencing Studies
synopsis: SurvSTAAR extends the STAAR framework to time-to-event traits, using censored age-at-onset information in annotation-weighted rare coding and noncoding tests while accounting for relatedness and population structure. Applied to Alzheimer's disease onset in 458,773 UK Biobank WGS participants, it reported putatively novel coding and noncoding associations and examined their likely effects on protein structure and function.

title: Patient and provider experiences with genomic risk result return: Case-based insights from eMERGE IV
synopsis: eMERGE IV returned genome-informed risk assessments to nearly 24,000 people at 10 sites, combining PRS, monogenic findings, family history and clinical risk factors for 11 conditions. This paper collects 24 cases from those disclosures and groups them into four themes: PRS-driven outcomes, challenges in returning results, primary-care provider views, and monogenic or mosaic findings. The authors call for educational materials, genetic counsellor support, care coordination and more study of how several genetic risk contributors combine.

title: Integrated Genetic Risk Stratifies Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer in Two Independent Cohorts
synopsis: The study tested GenProbCRC, a combined inherited risk measure built from a CRC polygenic score, family history and Lynch syndrome pathogenic variants, for predicting colorectal cancer before age 50. In about 103,000 UK Biobank participants under 50, the very-high-risk group had a 28-fold higher hazard than the low-risk group, and the high plus very-high groups (21% of people) held 61% of early-onset cases. Results pointed the same way in a smaller US health-system biobank.

title: CellColocDB: a disease-centred resource linking GWAS loci to genes, cell contexts, and fine-mapping evidence
synopsis: CellColocDB is a database of systematic GWAS-QTL colocalization meant to link disease loci to genes and the cellular contexts they act in. It runs coloc.abf across 2805 GWAS (1201 traits) and 316 bulk, sorted-cell and single-cell QTL contexts, adds coloc-SuSiE and SMR/HEIDI evidence, and links the top SNPs to fine-mapping results in CAUSALdb2. The release holds about 1.6 million colocalizations with PP.H4 of at least 0.8, which can be searched by disease, gene, locus or QTL context.

title: MGnify analyses in 2027: enhancing the depth and breadth of analyses across metabarcoding, unassembled metagenomes, and assembled datasets
synopsis: MGnify v6 updates EMBL-EBI's standardized microbiome analysis pipelines with amplicon sequence variants, viral and mobilome annotation of assemblies, and a minimal raw-reads analysis. The pipelines were ported to Nextflow with Prefect orchestration for better reuse. New bulk and programmatic access services support large-scale computational use of the data.

title: MIsoTEx: a mammalian transcript-isoform classification framework and database for exploring tissue distribution, expression stability, and abundance patterns
synopsis: The authors built a tissue-expression reference at the level of transcript isoforms rather than genes. Using normal adult RNA-seq from GTEx, ARCHS4 and curated SRA datasets, they sorted about 147,000 protein-coding isoforms from human, mouse and rat into ubiquitous and tissue-associated expression classes with relative-abundance subclasses and confidence scores. The database can be queried by gene, transcript, tissue pattern or ortholog, and part of the classification held up against independent RNA-seq and RT-PCR data.

title: MatriSpace: Identification and visualization of spatially resolved ECM gene expression patterns in health and disease
synopsis: MatriSpace is a framework for mining spatial transcriptomics data for extracellular-matrix (matrisome) gene expression. It maps ECM genes to cell populations, tissue niches and functional ECM units. It is available as an R package and a no-code Shiny web app, where users can upload their own data or explore a collection of public datasets.

title: Overview of recruitment strategies to reach the million milestone and characterization of the Million Veteran Program cohort
synopsis: Describes how the VA Million Veteran Program used a 2022-2023 multi-channel campaign (calls, mail, email, digital ads) to enroll its millionth participant, and how well each channel worked. The campaign contacted over 6.5 million Veterans and enrolled about 110,000; calls had the highest enrollment rate, while email brought in the most people. It also profiles the full cohort of about 1.02 million mostly male participants, which looks much like the wider VA patient population and is linked to health records for genetic research.

title: VEuPathDB: 2026 update on data, tools, and infrastructure for eukaryotic pathogens, vectors, and hosts
synopsis: VEuPathDB now holds over 2,600 datasets for more than 800 pathogen, vector and host organisms. New features include a My Datasets workspace for uploading and analysing users' own data and guided differential-expression analysis that needs no programming, and its processing pipelines now run as containerized Nextflow workflows. The update also describes how the resource kept going under a community funding model after it lost its federal grant.

title: Both Endogenous Enhancer and Retrotransposon Inserted Nearby Are Required to Induce Ectopic Expression in Danforth's Short Tail Mutation
synopsis: Investigates why the endogenous retrovirus insertion in Danforth's short tail mice drives ectopic Ptf1a expression in the notochord. Mutating the Ptf1a auto-regulatory enhancer or the ERV showed that both are needed for the vertebral phenotype, with the core activity in the enhancer half closest to the ERV. The PTF1 complex itself was not required.

title: Enduring DNA Methylation Marks of Blast and Trauma Exposures in Warfighters
synopsis: Ran EWAS of career blast and trauma exposure in 220 military breachers and grenade operators, built methylation risk scores for these exposures, and tested DunedinPACE age acceleration. The scores reached external AUCs of about 0.72-0.74 (0.52 for blast in grenade operators), and the trauma score was linked to slower reaction time after blast exposure. Exposures were also associated with faster DunedinPACE.

title: Genetic Dissection of the Mouse Class I Odorant Receptor Gene Cluster
synopsis: Uses large targeted deletions in the mouse Class I odorant receptor cluster to look for regulatory elements beyond the J element. Removing the centromeric half, which contains J, reduced expression of telomeric genes, while removing the telomeric half increased expression of centromeric genes. This supports J as the main long-range enhancer, with weaker secondary enhancers elsewhere in the cluster.

title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs
synopsis: The Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas brings together single-cell transcriptomic data from 134 species (over 148 million cells, 190 annotated cell types) and links them to each species' maximum lifespan. It provides tools that correlate genes and cell types with lifespan, plus a centenarian single-cell atlas and a human immune-aging multi-omics atlas. A knowledge graph and a retrieval-augmented assistant help with interpretation.

title: OMIGAT: Multi-Feature Enhanced Collaborative Attention and Graph Convolution Model for Cancer Driver Gene Identification
synopsis: The authors built OMIGAT to rank cancer driver genes despite noisy multi-omics data and incomplete prior interaction networks. It joins genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic features with network topology. A global branch learns a feature-similarity graph, a local graph-convolution branch learns from the biological network, and the two are fused adaptively; the model reaches an AUC of 87.46% on the PPNet dataset.

title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure
synopsis: Each RNA secondary-structure predictor has its own interface and software requirements. RNAcomp2D wraps classical thermodynamic and deep-learning predictors in containers behind one web server. Users enter a sequence or pick one from RNAcentral and compare all the predictions, and a reference structure if one exists, side by side in a single viewer.

title: pyGENIE: A Python library for programmatic access and mutational analysis of AACR Project GENIE
synopsis: Working with the huge AACR Project GENIE cancer-genomics release (>268,000 samples) usually means writing custom code around complex flat files. pyGENIE is a Python package with one API for clinical and genomic queries, tumor mutational burden and mutational-signature analysis (SigProfiler, SigMA), and it returns pandas DataFrames. In a lung adenocarcinoma case study it reproduced known mutation patterns with about ten times less code.

title: A new liability-based rare-variant burden test identifies a novel genetic association between HTRA3 and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
synopsis: Adjusting rare-variant tests for a polygenic risk score helps with quantitative traits but gives little or no power gain for binary traits. The authors developed the liability threshold burden test (LTBT), which models rare-variant burden and PRS together under a liability threshold model, and showed in simulations that it controls false positives and is more sensitive than existing methods. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis sequencing data, it found and replicated a new association between rare predicted-damaging missense variants in HTRA3 and IPF.

title: DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome
synopsis: This update of the Drug-Gene Interaction Database adds three new interaction sources, including the PRISM Repurposing Dataset and the Broad Drug Repurposing Hub. For reproducible programmatic use it adds Python/R clients (dgiPy, dgiR), versioned Docker images and a public archive of current and past releases, which widens FAIR access to drug-gene data for drug-repurposing workflows.

title: DIANA-miTED v2: an expanded microRNA tissue expression database with an integrated healthy-tissue reference atlas
synopsis: The update grows the uniformly processed human small RNA-seq collection from about 15,000 to nearly 50,000 profiles, adding GTEx v10 samples and many more from SRA, and it now covers 2,656 mature miRNAs across 96 tissues, 437 cell lines and 503 diseases. It provides a healthy-tissue reference atlas (more than 23,000 healthy donors), keeping tumour-adjacent normal samples separate. It also adds a body-map interface, co-expression networks, downloads and a REST API.

title: GI-DB: a comprehensive variant database for exploring the extensive genetic diversity of the Indian population
synopsis: South Asians are underrepresented in global variant resources, so the GenomeIndia initiative sequenced about 10,000 genomes from 83 Indian populations. GI-DB is the public browser for this data: it catalogs 136 million high-confidence variants, 44 million of them missing from other global and South Asian databases. It gives allele frequencies by tribal versus non-tribal group, region and language family, with annotations and comparisons to 1000 Genomes, gnomAD and GenomeAsia.

title: Integrating genetic and lung tissue proteomics data to identify susceptibility proteins for lung cancer
source: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
synopsis: The authors built genetic models of protein abundance from proteomes of 200 normal lung tissues and applied them in a proteome-wide association study of about 55,000 lung cancer cases. They found 29 risk-associated proteins, 15 of them more than 2 Mb from known GWAS loci, and backed them up with replication, colocalization and SMR. DSP, IL18 and TYMP had the strongest evidence and are targets of approved or late-stage drugs.

title: Aging out of the blue: Region-specific epigenetic clock calibration for a blue zone with the DNAm SuperLearner
synopsis: Trained a SuperLearner ensemble of existing epigenetic clocks and machine learners on 875 non-Nicoyan Costa Ricans (CRELES) and used it for a calibrated test of age acceleration in 206 residents of the Nicoya blue zone. Uncalibrated clocks gave conflicting answers (from ~3 years younger to ~4 years older). After age-stratified calibration, only a small advantage of about 0.35 years remained, mostly in the oldest participants.

title: GausSKAT: A Data-Adaptive Weighted Gaussian Kernel Procedure for Rare-Variant Association Testing Within the SKAT Framework
synopsis: SKAT almost always uses a weighted-linear kernel, and how well a Gaussian kernel works depends on a bandwidth that cannot be chosen in advance. GausSKAT runs weighted Gaussian SKAT over a data-driven, phenotype-independent grid of bandwidths and combines the resulting p-values with ACAT. In simulations it generally had more power than weighted-linear and IBS SKAT; in Dallas Heart Study triglyceride data its advantage over linear SKAT varied across ANGPTL gene sets.

title: Population-Scale, Genotype-First Characterization of Monogenic Diabetes in 374,973 Individuals Across Ancestries in the NIH All of Us Research Program
synopsis: Using WGS from 374,973 All of Us participants (42% non-European), the authors found pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 10 MODY genes in about 1 in 1,013 people, at similar rates in European and African ancestry groups. Diabetes penetrance was incomplete (43.5% by age 60) and was highest for GCK and lowest for non-GCK/HNF genes, whose carrier risk was below that of non-carriers in the top type 2 diabetes PRS decile. Higher T2D polygenic risk further raised diabetes risk among carriers.

title: A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes
synopsis: The authors audited cis-eQTL instruments for 15 sorted immune-cell types from DICE and used them in Mendelian randomisation against SLE and seven related FinnGen outcomes, adding colocalisation and genomic-control sensitivity analyses. After outcome-specific FDR control, 424 gene-outcome relationships remained. The SLE signals were concentrated in the MHC, and most non-MHC hits were for rheumatoid arthritis and autoimmune hypothyroidism; the authors present this as a hypothesis-generating screen.

title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts regulatory activity and variant effects across cell states
synopsis: Single-cell atlases rarely have enough donors for direct eQTL mapping, so the authors built AlphaGenome 2, a sequence model conditioned on a tissue, cell type or cell state and trained on human and mouse single-cell atlases plus bulk data. It doubles recall of causal single-cell eQTLs at 90% precision compared with fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1 and specialised models, and it generalises to unseen datasets without fine-tuning. The authors also release enhancer-gene links and variant scores for 7 million common variants across hundreds of cell types.

title: Polygenic risk scores for sleep: from portability to clinical utility
synopsis: Single-author perspective on polygenic risk scores for sleep traits and disorders, covering how well they transfer across populations and whether they are clinically useful. No abstract is available, so this summary is based on the title only.

title: Nephrotic syndrome genomic discovery in the Mass General Brigham Biobank identifies monoallelic MEFV variants as a risk factor for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
synopsis: The authors identified FSGS and minimal change cases in a 130,000-member health-system biobank and screened their exomes for 192 Mendelian proteinuria genes and APOL1. 17% of these unselected adults had a genetic form of disease, each linked to higher risk of kidney failure. Monoallelic pathogenic MEFV variants emerged as a new risk factor for SRNS/FSGS with collapsing and TMA features, supported in Genomics England and a case-control cohort (OR 3.8).

title: cellSTAAR: incorporating single-cell-sequencing-based functional data to boost power in rare variant association testing of noncoding regions
lab: the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Consortium
synopsis: cellSTAAR boosts noncoding rare-variant association tests by building cell-type-specific functional annotations and regulatory elements from single-cell ATAC-seq, with a comprehensive strategy for linking cCREs to target genes. Applied to TOPMed WGS (~60,000) with replication in UK Biobank (~190,000), it improved the detection and interpretability of associations across four lipid traits.

title: Integrating polygenic and methylation risk scores for pleural mesothelioma risk stratification
synopsis: Built polygenic and 68-CpG methylation risk scores for pleural mesothelioma in a retrospective case-control study and tested them in prediagnostic EPIC-Meso samples. The methylation score raised AUC from 0.66 to 0.85 in the test set (0.51 to 0.62 prediagnostically) and stayed robust across asbestos exposure levels; combining it with the polygenic score improved discrimination further.

title: Limited Generalizability of Epigenetic Clocks and Scores Across Pediatric Tissues and Age Ranges
synopsis: Compared 22 adult-trained epigenetic clocks and scores (BMI, CRP, cognition, smoking, telomere length) in matched blood and saliva from 291 children. Performance varied widely and cross-tissue agreement was often modest, so adult blood-trained scores should be used cautiously in pediatric saliva. The study also releases blood-saliva correlations for 815,069 CpGs.

title: Methylome-wide association studies and epigenetic biomarker development for 133 mass spectrometry-assessed circulating proteins in 14,671 Generation Scotland participants
synopsis: Ran EWAS and trained protein EpiScores for 133 mass-spec serum proteins in 14,671 Generation Scotland participants. 112 EpiScores tracked their protein in held-out data, and 16 predicted incident cardiovascular disease, compared with only one directly measured protein.

title: High cell-type specificity of eQTLs revealed by single-nucleus analyses of brain and blood
synopsis: scMetaBrain combines 3.9 million nuclei from 785 individuals across 10 brain datasets and finds 19,371 eGenes; 31% of eQTLs were highly cell-type-specific, mostly in excitatory neurons. Differences in eQTL effects between brain cell types were often as large as those between brain and non-brain bulk tissues.

title: Population-scale multiome immune cell atlas reveals complex disease drivers
synopsis: Paired single-nucleus ATAC and RNA profiles from 10 million PBMCs across 1,108 Finnish individuals. The study reports 51,083 cis-eQTLs (20,829 genes), 338,100 caQTLs, 119,094 fine-mapped variants and 496,488 enhancer-gene links, tracing paths from chromatin to expression to disease.

title: S4-multi: Enhancing polygenic score prediction in ancestrally diverse populations
synopsis: S4-Multi extends the Bayesian S4 model to multiple ancestries; benchmarked in UKB, FinnGen, BBJ, All of Us and GBMI for T2D, breast/colorectal cancer, asthma and stroke; matches best methods while using 9-77% fewer variants.

title: Chronic kidney disease
synopsis: A seminar-style review of chronic kidney disease, which affects about 850 million people worldwide; around 4 million need dialysis or transplant, and CKD is projected to be the fifth leading cause of death by 2050. Most patients become disabled or die from cardiovascular disease before they reach kidney failure. Large randomised trials since 2019 have produced treatments that slow kidney decline and also lower cardiovascular risk, so earlier detection by clinicians in every specialty could cut the global burden.

title: Scalable and accurate rare variant meta-analysis with Meta-SAIGE
synopsis: Meta-SAIGE is a summary-statistics method for rare-variant meta-analysis that accurately estimates the null distribution to control type I error for low-prevalence binary traits and reuses LD matrices across phenotypes. In UK Biobank exome simulations it controlled type I error and matched the power of pooled SAIGE-GENE+ analysis. Meta-analysis of 83 low-prevalence phenotypes in UK Biobank and All of Us found 237 gene-trait associations, 80 of which were not significant in either cohort alone.

title: PRISM: ancestry-aware integration of tissue-specific genomic annotations enhances the transferability of polygenic scores
synopsis: PRISM transfer-learning approach integrating fine-mapping and ancestry-aware tissue-specific ENCODE annotations; in UKB (406,659) gives largest gains in African ancestry (+13.1% over annotation-agnostic multi-ancestry PGS) using ~100-fold fewer annotations.

title: Computationally efficient meta-analysis of gene-based tests using summary statistics in large-scale genetic studies
synopsis: REMETA meta-analyzes gene-based tests from single-variant summary statistics using one sparse LD reference file per study, rescaled for each phenotype, instead of trait-specific covariance matrices. It adds methods for case-control imbalance and for estimating allele frequencies, genotype counts and burden-test effect sizes. Its performance was demonstrated by meta-analyzing five traits in 469,376 UK Biobank samples.

title: Estimation and mapping of the missing heritability of human phenotypes
synopsis: Using WGS of 347,630 European-ancestry UK Biobank participants, the authors estimated how much of the heritability of 34 traits is captured by 40 million variants with MAF >0.01%. WGS captured about 88% of pedigree-based heritability (20% from rare and 68% from common variants), and non-coding variants accounted for 79% of the rare-variant heritability. For lipid traits, more than 25% of rare-variant heritability could be mapped to specific loci.

title: Rare genetic variants confer a high risk of ADHD and implicate neuronal biology
synopsis: Exome rare-variant analysis of ADHD (8,895 cases, 53,780 controls) in the SCHEMA mould identified MAP1A, ANO8 and ANK2 as high-risk genes (OR 5.5-15). These genes overlap with other neurodevelopmental risk networks; rare deleterious variant load tracked lower education and IQ, and psychiatric comorbidities were linked to specific gene sets rather than a general constrained-gene burden.

title: Flexibly Modeling Rare Variant Pathogenicity Improves Gene Discovery for Complex Traits
synopsis: FlexRV improves rare-variant aggregation tests by modelling nonlinear relationships between functional annotations and phenotype. Across 62 quantitative and 44 disease traits in UK Biobank it found 51% more quantitative-trait and 102% more disease associations than Regenie, outperformed DeepRVAT and STAAR, and its hits replicated at a higher rate in All of Us. Missense and LoF variants contributed nearly equally to rare-variant burden heritability, and FlexRV weights improved rare-variant polygenic scores.

title: Specificity, length and luck drive gene rankings in association studies
synopsis: Across 209 UK Biobank quantitative traits, GWAS and rare-variant burden tests systematically prioritize different genes. The authors propose trait importance and trait specificity as prioritization criteria and show that burden tests rank trait-specific genes, whereas GWAS rank genes near trait-specific variants and can also find highly pleiotropic genes. Both designs are also affected by distinct trait-irrelevant factors, such as gene length and chance.

title: Transcriptome-wide association studies at cell-state level using single-cell eQTL data
synopsis: TWiST runs TWAS along pseudotime and models gene-trait effects as continuous curves, testing global, dynamic and nonlinear associations. It was more powerful than pseudobulk TWAS. In OneK1K it found hundreds of genes whose effects on autoimmune diseases change along immune differentiation.

title: A machine-learning framework to characterize functional disease architectures and prioritize disease variants
synopsis: V2D models disease effect sizes from genome-wide fine-mapping posteriors and functional annotations using machine learning. It shows that constrained regulatory variants are the main component of disease heritability (about 17x enrichment). Its neural-network prioritization scores (about 21x enrichment in the top 1%) beat existing scores and improve fine-mapping.

title: Exome-Wide Analysis Identifies a Rare EXD3 Missense Variant Associated With Diabetic Kidney Disease
synopsis: An exome-chip meta-analysis of up to 10,312 people with type 1 diabetes tested rare and low-frequency coding variants across 10 DKD definitions. Besides a known COL4A3 variant, a rare EXD3 missense variant (MAF 0.4%) raised DKD odds about 8.7-fold and showed supportive replication for albuminuria in UK Biobank. Knocking down EXD3 in podocytes reduced nephrin expression, and gene-level tests implicated MUC5B and others.

title: Modeling heterogeneity in single-cell perturbation states enhances detection of response eQTLs
synopsis: Instead of treating perturbation as a discrete condition, this method models each cell's perturbation state, using immune cells exposed to influenza A, Candida, Pseudomonas and M. tuberculosis. It found on average 36.9% more response eQTLs than the discrete model, and about 25% of response eQTLs had cell-type-specific effects.

title: A single-cell genetic colocalization test improves power and resolves disease-mediating cell types
synopsis: Bulk-tissue colocalization misses most GWAS loci and pseudobulk tests lose power when cell clustering is imperfect. scJLIM models eQTL interactions with continuous cell states to estimate eQTL significance and GWAS colocalization in individual cells. In benchmarks it improved power and resolved disease-mediating cell types.

title: Genetic screens of imaging-derived kidney volumes identify genes linked to kidney function
synopsis: The authors ran GWAS on deep-learning-derived MRI kidney volumes and sub-volumes from 38,816 UK Biobank participants and found dozens of loci per measure. Genes for cortex and medulla volume were enriched for kidney development and hypoxia pathways, and their effects correlated with eGFR effects. Some loci, such as PKHD1 and BICC1, affected volume but not eGFR, and rare BICC1 loss-of-function variants were linked to CKD and dialysis.

title: Mono-allelic pathogenic variants in JAG1 cause autosomal dominant tubulo-interstitial kidney disease (ADTKD-JAG1)
synopsis: Investigating 203 ADTKD families without a molecular diagnosis plus Genomics England cases, the authors found pathogenic JAG1 variants in three large families and in sporadic cases. Affected adults had isolated tubulointerstitial kidney failure without signs of Alagille syndrome. Expression and ER-stress studies pointed to haploinsufficiency, and the authors propose ADTKD-JAG1 as a new subtype.

title: MACHINE: a robust and scalable multi-ancestry fine-mapping method using a continuous global-local shrinkage prior
synopsis: MACHINE is a Bayesian multi-ancestry fine-mapper with a continuous Dirichlet-decomposition prior, so shared and ancestry-specific causal effects do not need preset sharing probabilities. It adds FDR control for summary statistics with out-of-sample LD and functional priors from g-LDSC. It controls FDR better in simulations and finds new causal variants for lipids and schizophrenia.

title: Quantifying APOL1, Human Leukocyte Antigen, and Other Genetic Contributions to Unexplained Kidney Failure
source: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
synopsis: The authors analysed whole genomes from 218 patients in the 100,000 Genomes Project with kidney failure of unknown cause starting before age 50. A monogenic diagnosis was found in 17%, mostly in younger patients. Gene-based, structural-variant and PRS case-control tests found no further causes, but high-risk APOL1 genotypes were strongly enriched in patients of African ancestry, which suggests a genetic architecture distinct from common CKD.

title: Dissecting the Predictive Accuracy of Polygenic Indexes for Behavioral Phenotypes Across Genetic Ancestries
synopsis: Systematic portability analysis of genome-wide polygenic indexes for 52 health, behavioral and social phenotypes (UKB, HRS); relative accuracy 24% in African, 37% East Asian, 51% South Asian ancestries; LD/allele-frequency differences explain 82% of loss in Africans; family-GWAS PGIs modestly help some traits.

title: fSuSiE enables fine-mapping of QTLs from genome-scale molecular profiles
synopsis: fSuSiE combines wavelet functional regression with SuSiE to fine-map variants that affect spatially correlated molecular traits such as methylation and histone acetylation. In ROSMAP brain data it gives far higher resolution than existing methods (6,355 vs 328 single-variant methylation credible sets). It also nominates causal variants colocalizing with Alzheimer's risk loci (CASS4, CR1/CR2).

title: Noncoding rare variant associations with blood traits in 166,740 UK Biobank genomes
synopsis: Using WGS from 166,740 UK Biobank participants and 42 blood traits, the authors selected noncoding variants using blood gene-regulation knowledge and deleteriousness scores and ran collapsing tests, finding hundreds of noncoding gene-trait associations. However, most reproduced known associations and were driven by linkage disequilibrium with nearby common and rare variants. The study urges caution when interpreting noncoding rare-variant association results.

title: Whole-genome sequencing of 490,640 UK Biobank participants
lab: the UK Biobank Whole-Genome Sequencing Consortium
synopsis: This paper reports WGS of 490,640 UK Biobank participants together with within- and cross-ancestry association analyses using the linked phenotypes. Compared with whole-exome sequencing, WGS improved genotyping of structural variants and of coding and UTR variation. Most disease associations were found in European-ancestry individuals, but strong or novel signals were also seen in African and Asian ancestries.

title: Whole-exome sequencing analysis identifies risk genes for schizophrenia
synopsis: SCHEMA follow-up that adds a new exome sample of 4,650 schizophrenia cases and 5,719 controls to published data, for 28,898 cases, 103,041 controls and 3,444 trios. STAG1 and ZNF136 reached exome-wide significance, and six more genes (including SLC6A1, ZMYND11 and KLC1) passed 5% FDR, with several shared with other developmental and psychiatric disorders and supporting a role for disrupted chromatin organisation.

title: Epigenetic biomarkers predict macrovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes
synopsis: Searched for blood methylation markers of incident macrovascular events in 752 newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients and built an 87-CpG methylation risk score. The score reached AUC 0.81 (0.84 with clinical factors), beating SCORE2-Diabetes, UKPDS, Framingham and polygenic scores, and a version replicated in EPIC-Potsdam/OPTIMED (AUC 0.80).

title: Rare-variant association studies: When are aggregation tests more powerful than single-variant tests?
synopsis: The study asks when gene-level aggregation tests are more powerful than single-variant tests for rare variants. Analytic calculations (with an online tool) and simulations on 378,215 UK Biobank participants show that power depends on sample size times region heritability, the number of causal variants and the number of variants aggregated. Aggregation tests win only when a substantial share of the aggregated variants is causal, so the chosen variant set (e.g., PTVs plus deleterious missense) is critical.

title: Towards improved fine-mapping of candidate causal variants
synopsis: A review of statistical fine-mapping methods, which are mostly Bayesian multiple-regression models with different effect-size priors and inference algorithms. It covers recent advances: refined modelling assumptions, use of extra information such as annotations, summary-statistic methods, and scalable algorithms that improve resolution.

title: Improved multiancestry fine-mapping identifies cis-regulatory variants underlying molecular traits and disease risk
synopsis: SuShiE (sum of shared single effects) uses LD differences across ancestries to fine-map cis-molQTLs and estimates cross-ancestry effect correlations. On 36,907 expression and protein phenotypes from TOPMed-MESA and GENOA it fine-maps 18.2% more genes with smaller, more functionally enriched credible sets. Its weights find 25.4% more genes in TWAS/PWAS of blood-cell traits in All of Us.

title: Leveraging global genetics resources to enhance polygenic prediction across ancestrally diverse populations
synopsis: Evaluates many single- and multi-source PGS methods (incl. PRS-CSx, TL-PRS, X-Wing) for 10 traits in AFR/EAS/EUR using Uganda, BBJ, UKB and MVP summary statistics; summary-statistic LEOPARD linear combinations of independently optimized scores consistently beat jointly optimized multi-source methods; implemented in GenoPred.

title: DNA Methylation Signatures of Cardiovascular Health Provide Insights Into Diseases
synopsis: Ran EWAS of the Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular-health score across five diverse cohorts, finding 609 replicated CpGs, and combined them into a methylation score. Each SD higher score was associated with 19-32% lower incident CVD risk and 27-45% lower all-cause mortality across cohorts.

title: Borzoi-informed fine mapping improves causal variant prioritization in complex trait GWAS
synopsis: Sniff combines Borzoi sequence-to-function variant-effect predictions with standard functional annotations as PolyFun priors. Across 15 UK Biobank traits it finds 9.45% more variants with PIP > 0.8 than PolyFun-baseline. The prioritized variants are supported by reporter-assay allelic activity and PoPS gene scores.

title: Cross-omics risk scores of inflammation markers are associated with all-cause mortality: The Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
synopsis: Combined polygenic, metabolomic and epigenetic risk scores for CRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha into multi-omics inflammation scores in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging. Multi-omics scores usually predicted mortality better than single-omics scores, and some outperformed circulating IL-6 itself; partial replication came from the Nurses' Health and HPFS cohorts.

title: Leveraging local ancestry and cross-ancestry genetic architecture to improve genetic prediction of complex traits in admixed populations
synopsis: SDPR_admix models two-ancestry effect sizes (null, ancestry-enriched, or shared-correlated) using local ancestry for admixed individuals; outperforms other methods in simulations and UKB European-African admixed individuals; training on All of Us (N=52,000) raised accuracy ~5-fold vs PAGE.

title: Transcriptional programs of cell identity and p53-induced stress responses are associated with distinctive features of spatial genome organization
synopsis: How does 3D genome organization relate to cell-identity gene programs versus p53-induced stress responses? Micro-C, RNA-seq and p53 ChIP-seq were run in 10 cell lines from diverse tissues before and after p53 activation, revealing hundreds of enhancer–promoter loops tied to cell-type marker expression. In contrast, p53-induced expression changes showed no such links to chromatin contacts, which supports a contact-independent, TF activity gradient model of enhancer–promoter communication.

title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Quantitative Kidney Function in 52,531 Individuals with Diabetes Identifies Five Diabetes-Specific Loci
source: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
synopsis: This study meta-analysed eGFR GWAS in 52,531 people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, adjusting for DKD status, diabetes duration, HbA1c and albuminuria. It found 13 loci; five (HIPK3, TRIM5, RORA, ERBB4, BCL6/LPP) had no effect or an opposite effect in the general population. Kidney expression and methylation QTL data (including a kidney enhancer at BCL6/LPP) support diabetes-specific roles for these genes.

title: Applying blood-derived epigenetic algorithms to saliva: cross-tissue similarity of DNA-methylation indices of aging, physiology, and cognition
synopsis: Pooled three datasets with matched saliva and blood methylation (n=107) to measure cross-tissue agreement of blood-trained methylation profile scores. After cell-composition correction, second/third-generation clocks and the CRP, BMI and cognition scores showed moderate agreement (ICC ~0.54-0.76), while first-generation clocks agreed poorly.

title: Using LDpred2 to adapt polygenic risk score techniques for methylation score creation
synopsis: Adapted LDpred2 to build methylation scores from MWAS summary statistics, replacing LD with co-methylated regions, TADs or sliding windows as the correlation prior. In schizophrenia data (N=1,227) the TAD and window versions explained ~3.6% of variance, matching existing methods, so the choice of structural prior mattered little.

title: Influence of race, ethnicity, and sex on the performance of epigenetic predictors of phenotypic traits
synopsis: Benchmarked epigenetic clocks, telomere-length, cell-proportion and plasma-protein predictors in a diverse NHANES sample, stratified by race/ethnicity and sex. Every predictor showed at least one group difference, with protein predictors generally less accurate in Mexican American and non-Hispanic Black participants, even after adjusting for cell composition and SES.

title: An atlas of single-cell eQTLs dissects autoimmune disease genes and identifies novel drug classes for treatment
synopsis: JOBS models bulk eQTLs as a weighted sum of cell-type sc-eQTLs; on OneK1K plus eQTLGen it found 586% more eQTLs, matching about 4x the OneK1K sample size. Integration with GWAS of 14 immune-mediated diseases colocalized about 30% more loci than either data type alone, and an extension supports drug repurposing.

title: Fine-mapping in admixed populations using CARMA-X, with applications to Latin American studies
synopsis: CARMA-X is a Bayesian fine-mapping model for admixed individuals. It models cross-ancestry LD, heterogeneity and small LD reference panels, and uses a robust test for out-of-sample LD. It has higher power with controlled false discoveries, and in Dominican and Mexican Biobank studies it prioritizes variants driven by African- and Native American-specific effects.

title: Haploinsufficiency of ITSN1 is associated with a substantial increased risk of Parkinson's disease
synopsis: Gene-based rare-variant analysis of UK Biobank WGS (3,809 PD cases and 247,101 controls) found that protein-truncating variants in ITSN1 raise Parkinson's disease risk about 10-fold, replicated in three cohorts (combined p = 4.5e-12). Fly and in vitro experiments support an interaction with alpha-synuclein toxicity, implicating vesicular trafficking in PD.

title: Whole-genome sequencing analysis identifies rare, large-effect noncoding variants and regulatory regions associated with circulating protein levels
synopsis: In ~50,000 UK Biobank genomes, cis association analysis of 1.1 billion variants with 2,907 circulating proteins, including 123 million noncoding aggregate tests, found 604 independent rare noncoding single-variant associations. Unlike coding variation, rare noncoding variants were almost as likely to raise as to lower protein levels. Noncoding aggregate tests identified 357 independent regions, 21% of which single-variant tests missed.

title: Benchmarking DNA Sequence Models for Causal Regulatory Variant Prediction in Human Genetics
synopsis: TraitGym is a curated benchmark of causal or strong-candidate regulatory variants for 113 Mendelian and 83 complex traits, with matched controls. On it, alignment-based CADD and GPN-MSA do best for Mendelian and complex disease traits, Enformer and Borzoi do best for complex non-disease traits, and Evo2 still trails, especially at enhancers.

title: A novel framework to build saliva-based DNA methylation biomarkers: Quantifying systemic chronic inflammation as a case study
synopsis: Proposed a way to carry blood-trained protein EpiScores over to saliva, using a reliability dataset with cross-tissue replicates, and used it to build InflammAge, a saliva-based measure of chronic inflammation. In >18,000 Generation Scotland participants, InflammAge was associated with mortality, disease and lifestyle factors, often more strongly than CRP.

title: Blood-based epigenome-wide association study and prediction of alcohol consumption
synopsis: Trained an elastic-net alcohol-consumption EpiScore in 16,717 Generation Scotland participants, testing CpG pre-filtering and sex-specific models, and validated it in four external cohorts (>10,000 people). The score correlated 0.41-0.53 with self-reported intake and, unlike self-report, was associated with poorer brain-imaging measures.

title: Cell state-dependent allelic effects and contextual Mendelian randomization analysis for human brain phenotypes
synopsis: 2.35 million nuclei from 391 case and control brains gave 13,939 eGenes, of which 16.7-40.8% (by cell type) showed disease-dependent allelic effects. 23.6% of 501 colocalizations with CNS traits were disease-dependent, and single-cell MR in control brains found 140 putatively causal gene-trait pairs.

title: Predicting RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence as a unifying model of gene regulation
synopsis: Borzoi is a sequence-to-function model that predicts cell-type- and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage directly from DNA. Statistics computed from its predicted coverage score variant effects on transcription, splicing and polyadenylation. On QTL benchmarks it is competitive with, and often better than, models built for single regulatory functions, and attribution analysis recovers cis-regulatory motifs behind expression and post-transcriptional regulation.

title: ChromBPNet: bias factorized, base-resolution deep learning models of chromatin accessibility reveal cis-regulatory sequence syntax, transcription factor footprints and regulatory variants
synopsis: ChromBPNet is a lightweight deep learning model that predicts base-resolution chromatin accessibility from DNA sequence. It separates assay-specific enzyme bias from the sequence features that actually drive accessibility, which lets it recover compact TF motif sets, cooperative motif syntax and precise footprints. In benchmarks it matches much larger models at predicting variant effects on accessibility, pioneer TF binding and reporter activity, and it helps prioritize regulatory variants for complex traits and rare diseases.

title: DNA methylation models of protein abundance across the lifecourse
synopsis: Tested 14 published protein EpiScores and trained new age-specific ones in ALSPAC at ages 9, 24 and midlife, with and without adjusting for genotype. EpiScores worked better in adults than in children (none of the Gadd scores worked at age 9), though several captured non-genetic protein variation at every age.

title: DNA methylation-based predictors of metabolic traits in Scottish and Singaporean cohorts
synopsis: Trained EpiScores for BMI, body fat, waist-hip ratio, glucose, HDL and total cholesterol in >17,000 Generation Scotland participants and tested them in Scottish (LBC1936) and Singaporean (HELIOS) cohorts. The scores transferred across populations (BMI EpiScore explained ~21% of variance in HELIOS), though the body-fat score was weaker in the Indian subgroup.

title: Nucleotide Transformer: building and evaluating robust foundation models for human genomics
synopsis: Can DNA foundation models pretrained without labels improve prediction of molecular phenotypes when annotated data are scarce? Nucleotide Transformer models (50 million to 2.5 billion parameters) were pretrained on 3,202 human genomes and 850 genomes from other species, then cheaply fine-tuned for various genomics tasks. They predicted well in low-data settings, learned without supervision to attend to key genomic elements, and improved genetic variant prioritization.

title: Exome sequencing in Asian populations identifies low-frequency and rare coding variation influencing Parkinson's disease risk
synopsis: Exome sequencing with gene-based burden tests in 4,298 Asian PD cases and 5,512 controls, replicated in about 11,000 more samples. GBA1 and SMPD1 were associated with PD; SMPD1 variants with low enzyme activity, mostly the Asian-specific p.Pro332Arg, carried the strongest risk (OR about 2.2), showing the value of rare-variant studies in diverse populations.

title: Sequence modeling and design from molecular to genome scale with Evo
synopsis: Evo is a long-context genomic foundation model trained on millions of prokaryotic and phage genomes, and its training shows scaling laws for DNA. It predicts function zero-shot across DNA, RNA and protein about as well as domain-specific models and predicts how mutations affect organism fitness. It also designed functional CRISPR-Cas and transposon systems and generated megabase-scale sequences with plausible genome architecture.

title: APOL1 Bi- and Monoallelic Variants and Chronic Kidney Disease in West Africans
source: The New England journal of medicine
synopsis: This case-control study of 8,355 Ghanaians and Nigerians asked how APOL1 risk variants relate to CKD in West Africans. Biallelic carriers were about 30% of participants and monoallelic carriers 43%. Two risk alleles raised the odds of CKD by 25% and of FSGS by 84%, and even one risk allele raised CKD odds by 18% and FSGS odds by 61%, which challenges a purely recessive model.

title: Whole-genome sequencing in 333,100 individuals reveals rare non-coding single variant and aggregate associations with height
lab: the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Consortium
synopsis: Large WGS analysis of rare (<0.1%) noncoding variation and height in 333,100 people (UK Biobank, TOPMed, All of Us), using single-variant tests and aggregate tests over proximal-regulatory, intergenic-regulatory and deep-intronic masks. It found 29 independent rare variants with large effects and replicated noncoding aggregate signals near HMGA1 and in MIR497HG, showing that noncoding rare-variant aggregation works at biobank scale.

title: Integration of variant annotations using deep set networks boosts rare variant association testing
synopsis: DeepRVAT uses set neural networks to learn a trait-agnostic gene impairment score from rare-variant annotations, offering a data-driven alternative to fixed annotation-weighted tests such as STAAR. Across 34 quantitative and 63 binary UK Biobank exome traits it found substantially more genes and better identified high-risk individuals, and it stayed calibrated and efficient at biobank scale.

title: Polygenic scores and their applications in kidney disease
synopsis: This review from Khan and Kiryluk covers how polygenic scores are built, validated and reported, with a focus on nephrology. It discusses limited transfer across ancestries and the need for models that combine polygenic, monogenic, family-history and clinical risk. It also outlines the prospective studies needed to show clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.

title: Fine-mapping across diverse ancestries drives the discovery of putative causal variants underlying human complex traits and diseases
lab: the Schizophrenia Workgroup of Psychiatric Genomics Consortium
synopsis: SuSiEx is a cross-population fine-mapping method that uses GWAS summary statistics from any number of ancestries. It models each population's allele frequencies and LD and allows several causal variants per locus. In simulations, quantitative traits shared by UK Biobank and Taiwan Biobank, and schizophrenia GWAS combining East Asian and European data, it fine-maps loci better than single-ancestry analysis.

title: Systematic rare variant analyses identify RAB32 as a susceptibility gene for familial Parkinson's disease
lab: the Project MinE ALS Sequencing Consortium
synopsis: Exome-wide rare-variant analysis of 2,184 familial PD index cases and 69,775 controls identified RAB32 p.S71R as a high-risk variant (OR about 65, found in about 0.7% of familial cases), which segregated with disease. Functional work showed that the variant increases LRRK2 kinase activity, linking RAB biology to the LRRK2 pathway.

title: A cell type–specific approach to elucidate the role of miR-96 in inner ear hair cells
synopsis: What does miR-96 do in inner ear hair cells? Bulk RNA-seq of hair cells sorted from newborn Mir96 Dmdo wildtype, heterozygous and homozygous mice found 215 upregulated and 428 downregulated genes in homozygous mutants. Downregulated genes included deafness genes such as Myo15a, Myo7a, Ush1c, Gfi1 and Ptprq, while upregulated genes tended to be supporting-cell-enriched, suggesting miR-96 represses supporting-cell programs in hair cells (data available on gEAR).

title: Leveraging functional genomic annotations and genome coverage to improve polygenic prediction of complex traits within and between ancestries
synopsis: SBayesRC combines GWAS summary statistics with 96 functional annotations, which shape both the chance that a variant is causal and its effect-size distribution, and it scales to about 7 million SNPs. Across 50 traits it beat SBayesR by 14% in Europeans and by up to 34% across ancestries, and it also outperformed LDpred2, LDpred-funct, MegaPRS, PolyPred-S and PRS-CSx. SNP density interacted with annotation information, evolutionarily constrained regions contributed most to accuracy, and nonsynonymous SNPs contributed most per SNP.

title: Drugst.One — a plug-and-play solution for online systems medicine and network-based drug repurposing
synopsis: Drugst.One aims to make network-based drug repurposing tools easier to use, since many need complex installation and lack interactive network views. With three lines of code, it turns systems biology software into a web tool for exploring protein-drug-disease networks. It has been integrated with 21 systems medicine tools and is available at https://drugst.one.

title: Large-scale whole-exome sequencing of neuropsychiatric diseases and traits in 350,770 adults
synopsis: Cross-disorder exome study of 46 neuropsychiatric diseases and 23 traits in 350,770 UK Biobank adults. It found 20 new disease genes and 30 new trait genes (for example, pleiotropic SYNGAP1 effects on cognition), and coding-variant genetic correlations showing shared rare-variant architecture across neurodegenerative and mental disorders.

title: Tissue-specific enhancer–gene maps from multimodal single-cell data identify causal disease alleles
lab: the Accelerating Medicines Partnership® RA/SLE Program and Network
synopsis: SCENT is a nonparametric method that links enhancers to their target genes by testing whether chromatin accessibility tracks gene expression in multimodal single-cell RNA+ATAC data. Applied to 9 datasets with more than 120,000 cells or nuclei, it produced 23 cell-type-specific enhancer-gene maps. These maps were strongly enriched for causal eQTL and GWAS variants across 1,143 traits, pointed to likely causal genes for common and rare diseases, and linked somatic mutation hotspots to target genes.

title: Genomic data in the All of Us Research Program
synopsis: All of Us released 245,388 clinical-grade genome sequences. The cohort is highly diverse: 77% of participants come from groups under-represented in biomedical research, and 46% from racial and ethnic minorities. More than 1 billion variants were found, over 275 million of them previously unreported.

title: PRS-Net: Interpretable polygenic risk scores via geometric learning
synopsis: Linear PRS models miss nonlinear genotype–phenotype relationships, so PRS-Net breaks the genome-wide score down into gene-level PRSs and links them with a graph neural network that models gene–gene interactions, plus an attentive readout for interpretation. Across several complex diseases it beat baseline PRS methods at predicting disease. It also highlighted influential genes and gene–gene interactions for Alzheimer's disease and multiple sclerosis.

title: The cells of the sensory epithelium, and not the stria vascularis, are the main cochlear cells related to the genetic pathogenesis of age-related hearing loss
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Earlier studies disagreed on whether sensory epithelial or stria vascularis cells drive the genetic risk for age-related hearing loss (ARHL). To settle this, four ARHL GWAS datasets were combined with four independent inner-ear single-cell RNA-seq datasets. GWAS signal was clearly enriched in cochlear sensory epithelial cells, not the stria vascularis, and the analysis explains why previous approaches missed this enrichment.

title: The predictive capacity of polygenic risk scores for disease risk is only moderately influenced by imputation panels tailored to the target population
synopsis: Does imputing a non-European target cohort with an ancestry-matched reference panel improve polygenic risk score prediction when the GWAS came from a different population? Using binary phenotypes in ethnically distinct UK Biobank and other cohorts, ethnically homogeneous imputation panels were built and PRS accuracy compared across them. Matching the panel to the target's ethnicity gave only marginal gains, and only under specific conditions.

title: Analysis of rare Parkinson's disease variants in millions of people
synopsis: Large replication effort for reported rare Parkinson's disease variants: 834 ClinVar variants in known PD genes were meta-analysed across 23andMe, UK Biobank and AMP-PD (27,590 cases, 6,701 proxies and about 3.1 million controls). Only five variants (including GBA1 and LRRK2) survived Bonferroni correction and eight more were strong candidates, showing how hard rare-variant replication is at scale.

title: MESuSiE enables scalable and powerful multi-ancestry fine-mapping of causal variants in genome-wide association studies
synopsis: Fine-mapping is usually done one ancestry at a time. MESuSiE is a multi-ancestry extension of SuSiE that takes summary statistics, models ancestry-specific LD and both shared and ancestry-specific causal SNPs, and runs fast through variational inference. In simulations and fine-mapping of four lipid traits in European and African samples, it improved resolution by 19.0–72.0% over existing methods, ran an order of magnitude faster, and gave better functional enrichment.

title: Benchmarking of deep neural networks for predicting personal gene expression from DNA sequence highlights shortcomings
synopsis: Benchmarks deep learning models that predict gene expression from DNA sequence on how well they explain differences between individuals, using paired whole-genome and expression data from 839 ROSMAP participants. The models often get the direction of variant effects wrong. This traces to poorly learned sequence motif grammar, and new training strategies are suggested.

title: Personal transcriptome variation is poorly explained by current genomic deep learning models
synopsis: Tests whether four state-of-the-art genomic deep learning models, which predict expression well across genes from the reference genome, can explain cis-regulatory expression variation between individuals. On paired personal genome and transcriptome data they perform poorly and often predict the wrong direction of effect for cis-regulatory variants.

title: DNA language models are powerful predictors of genome-wide variant effects
synopsis: GPN (Genomic Pre-trained Network) is a DNA language model pretrained without supervision on unaligned genomes of Arabidopsis thaliana and seven related Brassicales species. It learns gene structure and motifs without labels. Evaluated on 1001 Genomes allele frequencies and A. thaliana GWAS, it predicts variant effects better than phyloP and phastCons conservation scores.

title: Systematic differences in discovery of genetic effects on gene expression and complex traits
synopsis: Why do eQTLs explain so few GWAS signals? Comparing the two shows systematic differences: eQTLs cluster near TSSs at weakly constrained genes with simple regulatory landscapes, whereas GWAS hits lie near functionally important, highly constrained genes with complex, cell-type-varied regulation. A model shows how natural selection on traits hinders discovery of relevant eQTLs, which argues for complementary functional approaches.

title: A new method for multiancestry polygenic prediction improves performance across diverse populations
synopsis: Polygenic risk scores perform worse in non-European populations, so CT-SLEB was built to compute PRSs from ancestry-specific GWAS summary statistics by combining clumping and thresholding, empirical Bayes and superlearning. It was benchmarked against nine other methods using simulations (~19 million variants) and 23andMe, GLGC, All of Us and UK Biobank data (5.1 million people, 1.18 million non-European, 13 traits). CT-SLEB improved prediction in non-European groups over simple methods and matched or beat a more computationally heavy method.

title: Shared and organ-specific gene-expression programs during the development of the cochlea and the superior olivary complex
synopsis: How are gene-expression programs coordinated between the peripheral (cochlea) and central (superior olivary complex) auditory systems during mouse development? mRNA and small-RNA sequencing at E16, P0 and P16 revealed shared and organ-specific clusters enriched for inner ear development, Wnt signalling, K+ transport and axon guidance. Inverse miRNA–target expression trends pointed to six candidate regulators of both systems, including the known hearing gene miR-96.

title: Evaluation of European-based polygenic risk score for breast cancer in Ashkenazi Jewish women in Israel
synopsis: Can breast cancer polygenic risk scores built from European-ancestry GWAS data predict risk in Ashkenazi Jewish women? PRSs derived from BCAC European data were tested in 2161 Israeli AJ women (1437 cases, 724 controls), then validated with the established 313-SNP PRS in an independent Hadassah cohort of 181 women. The best PRS gave an OR per SD of 1.56 (1.58 at validation; 313-SNP: 1.64), and women in the top decile had an OR of 2.10 compared with the middle quintile.

title: Large-scale rare variant burden testing in Parkinson's disease
synopsis: Seed. Asked whether rare protein-altering variants contribute to Parkinson's disease risk, using burden-test meta-analysis of WGS/WES data from about 7,200 PD cases, 6,700 proxy cases and 51,650 controls (AMP-PD, NIH, UK Biobank, Genentech). GBA1 and LRRK2 reached exome-wide significance, and seven candidate genes (including B3GNT3 and TREML1) were nominated but did not replicate across datasets.

title: CARMA is a new Bayesian model for fine-mapping in genome-wide association meta-analyses
Current sequence-based models capture gene expression determinants in promoters but mostly ignore distal enhancers
synopsis: Do deep sequence-to-expression models such as Enformer learn causal regulatory signals, or only correlations picked up from training across the genome? Their predictions were checked against two large observational studies and five deep perturbation assays. They capture causal promoter determinants well, but largely miss enhancer effects at medium-to-long range, especially for highly expressed promoters, probably because true elements become rarer among candidates as distance grows.

title: Polygenic architecture of rare coding variation across 394,783 exomes
synopsis: How much do rare coding variants contribute to complex-trait heritability, and how does their architecture compare with common variants? Burden heritability was estimated for 22 traits and diseases in 394,783 UK Biobank exomes. Rare coding variants explain about 1.3% of phenotypic variance on average, mostly through ultrarare loss-of-function variants.

title: FinnGen provides genetic insights from a well-phenotyped isolated population
synopsis: FinnGen tests whether Finland's founder bottleneck, which concentrates harmful alleles in low-frequency variants, helps find common-disease genes. Analysing 224,737 participants linked to national health registers, with Estonian and UK biobank meta-analyses, it found 30 new associations for 15 well-studied diseases, mostly from Finnish-enriched low-frequency variants. A GWAS of 1,932 endpoints found 2,733 genome-wide significant associations at 2,496 loci, with 148 coding variants implicated by fine-mapping.

title: The LHX2-OTX2 transcriptional regulatory module controls retinal pigmented epithelium differentiation and underlies genetic risk for age-related macular degeneration
synopsis: Which transcription factors set up retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) identity, and does their regulatory network help explain genetic risk for age-related macular degeneration (AMD)? Working in stem-cell-derived human RPE and mouse models, with transcriptomic and proteomic profiling, the study shows that LHX2 and OTX2 act together with LDB1 and SWI/SNF (BAF) to control RPE gene expression. Overlaying the LHX2-OTX2 cistrome with eQTL, RPE ATAC-seq and AMD GWAS data, then testing hits in a reporter assay, identified a causal risk SNP that changes LHX2 activity at the TRPM1 promoter and so alters TRPM1 expression.

title: Discovery and systematic characterization of risk variants and genes for coronary artery disease in over a million participants
synopsis: A coronary artery disease GWAS of 181,522 cases among 1,165,690 mostly European-ancestry participants found 241 associations, 30 at new loci, and meta-analysis with a Japanese GWAS added 38 more new loci. Functionally informed fine-mapping and eight gene-prioritization approaches nominated 220 candidate causal genes. CRISPR–Cas9 experiments validated an enhancer in MYO9B that appears to affect CAD risk through vascular cell motility.

title: Meta-analysis fine-mapping is often miscalibrated at single-variant resolution
lab: the China Kadoorie Biobank Collaborative Group
synopsis: Heterogeneity across cohorts in sample size, phenotyping and imputation miscalibrates fine-mapping of GWAS meta-analyses. SLALOM is a summary-statistic QC method that flags suspicious loci by detecting outlier association statistics; it was validated in simulations and the GWAS Catalog. Across 14 GBMI meta-analyses, 67% of loci looked suspicious, and these were 2.7× depleted for nonsynonymous lead variants (p = 7.3 × 10^-4).

title: A framework for detecting noncoding rare-variant associations of large-scale whole-genome sequencing studies
lab: the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Consortium
synopsis: Seed. Presents STAARpipeline, which annotates a WGS study automatically and runs noncoding rare-variant tests both gene-centric (STAAR on functional noncoding categories) and non-gene-centric (fixed windows and dynamic SCANG-STAAR windows). Applied to lipid traits in 21,015 TOPMed genomes, it found noncoding rare-variant sets that partly replicated in 9,123 further samples, and it was also run on five non-lipid traits.

title: The construction of cross-population polygenic risk scores using transfer learning
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Because most GWASs come from European-ancestry cohorts and PRS models transfer poorly to other ancestries, TL-PRS uses transfer learning: gradient descent fine-tunes a PRS model built from large-sample GWASs to a target-ancestry dataset. On seven quantitative and two binary traits in UK Biobank (10,285 South Asian and 8,168 African-ancestry individuals), TL-PRS on a PRS-CS baseline gave 25% and 29% average relative gains in predicted R² over standard PRS-CS.

title: A saturated map of common genetic variants associated with human height
synopsis: A height GWAS of 5.4 million people of diverse ancestries found 12,111 independent SNPs that capture nearly all common-SNP heritability. The SNPs cluster in 7,209 segments covering about 21% of the genome. They explain 40% of height variance in Europeans but only 10–20% in other ancestries, likely because of LD and allele-frequency differences, since effect sizes and regions are similar.

title: Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative: Powering genetic discovery across human disease
synopsis: Most biobanks are mostly made up of people of European ancestry, so GBMI was set up as a network of 23 biobanks on 4 continents covering over 2.2 million people with genetic data linked to electronic health records. The network meta-analyzes GWAS summary statistics from harmonized genotypes and phenotypes for 14 exemplar diseases and endpoints. Despite differences in case definitions and recruitment, the combined analyses boost GWAS power, help understudied diseases, improve risk prediction, and point to disease genes and drug candidates.

title: Alternative cleavage and polyadenylation generates downstream uncapped RNA isoforms with translation potential
synopsis: Thousands of previously undescribed 5' uncapped, polyadenylated transcripts (5' UPTs) arise downstream of APA sites and increase when APA is activated. Their 5' ends resist exonucleases because of strong RNA structure and m6A modification; they are enriched in polysomes and drive non-canonical translation and changes in cell-surface peptide presentation. Bcl2's entire coding sequence is produced as a 5' UPT from APA sites inside its 5' UTR.

title: Identifying disease-critical cell types and cellular processes by integrating single-cell RNA-sequencing and human genetics
synopsis: sc-linker combines scRNA-seq, epigenomic SNP-to-gene maps and GWAS summary statistics to find the cell types and cellular programs through which risk variants act. Besides recovering known biology, it linked GABAergic neurons to major depressive disorder, a disease-dependent M-cell program to ulcerative colitis and a complement cascade process to multiple sclerosis. In autoimmune disease, both healthy and disease-dependent immune programs were enriched, but only disease-dependent epithelial programs were, suggesting the epithelium responds to disease rather than starting it.

title: SAIGE-GENE+ improves the efficiency and accuracy of set-based rare variant association tests
synopsis: SAIGE-GENE shows inflated variance-component set tests when restricted to very rare variants (MAF ≤ 0.1% or 0.01%). SAIGE-GENE+ fixes this with much better type I error control and speed, and it gains power by combining multiple MAF cutoffs with functional annotations. Applied to UK Biobank exome data for 30 quantitative and 141 binary traits, it found 551 gene–phenotype associations.

title: Efficient and accurate frailty model approach for genome-wide survival association analysis in large-scale biobanks
synopsis: A frailty-model method for genome-wide survival analysis of censored time-to-event phenotypes accounts for population structure and relatedness. A saddlepoint approximation handles heavy censoring (>90%) and variants down to minor allele count 20. It was validated by simulation and on five phenotypes, including lifespan, in ~400,000 UK Biobank and ~180,000 FinnGen participants, then applied to 871 UK Biobank phenotypes with results browsable in PheWeb.

title: Two-layer design protects genes from mutations in their enhancers
Polygenic enrichment distinguishes disease associations of individual cells in single-cell RNA-seq data
synopsis: scDRS links GWAS polygenic risk to single-cell RNA-seq by scoring each cell for excess expression of disease-associated genes, without needing cell-type labels. Across 74 traits and 1.3 million cells from 31 tissues, it reproduced known cell type–disease links. It also found disease-associated subpopulations, such as IBD-linked T cells, schizophrenia-linked neurons and triglyceride-linked hepatocytes.

title: Systematic single-variant and gene-based association testing of thousands of phenotypes in 394,841 UK Biobank exomes
synopsis: Single-variant and gene-based tests of 4,529 phenotypes in 394,841 UK Biobank exomes, aimed at mapping the effect of rare coding variation on human disease. Whether an association is discovered depends strongly on allele frequency and correlates with deleteriousness and selection metrics. The results are released as a public resource through the Genebass browser.

title: CellRegMap: a statistical framework for mapping context‐specific regulatory variants using scRNA‐seq
synopsis: CellRegMap is a statistical framework that uses population-scale scRNA-seq to test how genetic effects on expression change across cellular contexts, without needing predefined discrete cell types. It models genotype-context interactions for known eQTL, covering both cell subtypes and continuous cell-state transitions. After validation on simulations, it found hundreds of context-dependent eQTL in two differentiating iPSC studies and fine-grained regulation in neuronal subtypes at disease-colocalized eQTL.

title: The sequences of 150,119 genomes in the UK Biobank
synopsis: Whole-genome sequencing of 150,119 UK Biobank participants yielded 585 million SNPs (7.0% of all possible), 58.7 million indels, 895,055 structural variants and 2.5 million microsatellites. A depletion rank score showed that coding exons make up only a small part of the strongly conserved genome. British-Irish, African and South Asian cohorts were defined, an imputation reference panel was released, and new large-effect rare-variant trait associations were reported.

title: Fine-mapping from summary data with the “Sum of Single Effects” model
synopsis: Extends the SuSiE fine-mapping model from individual-level data to summary data (z-scores plus reference-panel LD) by swapping in a summary-data likelihood. The same framework also explains how FINEMAP and CAVIAR work. New diagnostics catch mismatches between z-scores and LD, a refinement step improves model fits, and in simulations SuSiE on summary data matches the best methods in speed and accuracy.

title: A sequence-based global map of regulatory activity for deciphering human genetics
synopsis: Sei maps any sequence or variant to regulatory activity using a deep learning model predicting 21,907 chromatin profiles across more than 1,300 cell lines and tissues. From these it derives 'sequence classes', a global vocabulary of regulatory activities such as cell-type-specific enhancers. Predictions are supported by tissue expression, eQTL and evolutionary constraint data, and reveal tissue-specific regulatory architecture of complex traits and pathogenic mutations.

title: Variant to function mapping at single-cell resolution through network propagation
synopsis: SCAVENGE uses network propagation to overcome sparsity and noise in single-cell (especially epigenomic) data and map causal GWAS variants to relevant cells, states and trajectories at single-cell resolution. It was applied to blood traits across stages of human hematopoiesis, to monocyte subsets that raise the risk of severe COVID-19, and to intermediate lymphocyte developmental states that predispose to acute leukemia, revealing mechanisms behind these genetic associations.

title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis identifies 48 risk variants and highlights the role of the stria vascularis in hearing loss
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: A genome-wide association meta-analysis of clinically diagnosed and self-reported hearing impairment in 723,266 people found 48 significant loci, 10 of them new. Many hits were missense variants, and half of those fall within known familial hearing loss loci. Mapping the results onto mouse cochlea and brain single-cell RNA-seq pointed to spindle, root and basal cells of the stria vascularis.

title: The Tabula Sapiens: A multiple-organ, single-cell transcriptomic atlas of humans
synopsis: Tabula Sapiens is a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of nearly 500,000 cells from 24 tissues and organs, many taken from the same donors. It characterizes more than 400 cell types and how their gene expression varies by tissue. Sampling many tissues from one donor allowed tracking of T-cell clones across tissues, tissue-specific B-cell mutation rates, cell-cycle states, and cell type–specific RNA splicing.

title: Improving polygenic prediction in ancestrally diverse populations
synopsis: PRS-CSx builds polygenic risk scores from GWAS summary statistics of several populations at once, coupling effects across populations through a shared continuous shrinkage prior and exploiting LD diversity between discovery samples. Across simulations with varied genetic architectures, cross-population overlap and GWAS sizes it outperformed alternative methods. It improved prediction of quantitative traits and schizophrenia risk in non-European populations.

title: Predicting RNA splicing from DNA sequence using Pangolin
synopsis: Pangolin is a deep learning model that predicts splice-site strength from DNA sequence in multiple tissues. It beats state-of-the-art splicing predictors across tasks and better predicts how common, rare and lineage-specific variants affect splicing. It also detects loss-of-function mutations with high accuracy and recall, especially those that are neither missense nor nonsense.

title: Mapping genomic loci implicates genes and synaptic biology in schizophrenia
synopsis: A two-stage schizophrenia GWAS of up to 76,755 cases and 243,649 controls found 287 loci. The associations were concentrated in genes expressed in excitatory and inhibitory CNS neurons. Fine-mapping and functional genomics prioritized 120 genes, involved in synaptic organization and transmission.

title: Single-cell eQTL mapping identifies cell type–specific genetic control of autoimmune disease
synopsis: To map cell-type-specific genetic regulation of immune gene expression, the study ran scRNA-seq on 1,267,758 PBMCs from 982 healthy donors. Across 14 cell types it found 26,597 independent cis-eQTLs and 990 trans-eQTLs, mostly cell-type specific, plus dynamic eQTL effects during naïve-to-memory B-cell transition. Mendelian randomization then tied 305 autoimmune risk loci to causal routes in specific cell types.

title: New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
synopsis: A two-stage GWAS of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias included 111,326 clinical or proxy cases and 677,663 controls. It found 75 risk loci, 42 of them new, and confirmed amyloid/tau and microglia pathways. Gene prioritization pointed to 31 genes, including TNF-alpha signalling through the LUBAC complex.

title: Leveraging fine-mapping and multipopulation training data to improve cross-population polygenic risk scores
synopsis: PolyPred aims to make polygenic risk scores more accurate in non-European groups by blending a fine-mapping-based predictor of causal effects, which helps with linkage disequilibrium differences between populations, with BOLT-LMM. Trained on UK Biobank British data and tested on 49 traits in four UK Biobank populations, it beat BOLT-LMM by +7% (south Asians) to +32% (Africans). PolyPred+ also used Biobank Japan data and raised east Asian accuracy by +24% over BOLT-LMM and +12% over PolyPred.

title: Incorporating regulatory interactions into gene-set analyses for GWAS data: A controlled analysis with the MAGMA tool
synopsis: Asks whether adding public regulatory-interaction maps to MAGMA's default proximity-based SNP-to-gene mapping improves gene and gene-set analyses of GWAS data. Across ten phenotypes, augmented and proximity-only mappings were compared, revealing confounders that required new controls. With these controls, augmentation only occasionally strengthened enrichment, though brain interactions implicated acetylcholine receptor subunits CHRNB2 and CHRNE in schizophrenia.

title: DNA methylation-based predictors of health: applications and statistical considerations
synopsis: Review of DNA methylation-based predictors of age, smoking and other exposures, and of early detection or progression of cancer, cardiovascular and neurological disease. It assesses what machine learning has contributed and how widely key statistical practices are used: data-driven feature selection, avoiding data leakage, and generalizable, well-powered training sets.

title: The DOMINO web-server for active module identification analysis
synopsis: A web server that makes the DOMINO active module identification algorithm easier to use. Given a gene network and gene activity scores, it runs DOMINO, performs GO enrichment, draws the modules and exports results in formats suited to downstream analysis. It accepts several gene identifier types and organisms and is available at domino.cs.tau.ac.il.

title: CT-FOCS: a novel method for inferring cell type-specific enhancer–promoter maps
synopsis: CT-FOCS uses linear mixed-effect models to infer enhancer–promoter links that are active in only one cell type or a small subset of cell types. On 808 FANTOM5 samples covering 472 cell lines, primary cells and tissues, it inferred these links more accurately than recent state-of-the-art methods. The analysis also shows that strictly cell type-specific enhancer–promoter links are very rare in the human genome.

title: DunedinPACE, a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging
