synopsis: Can a single blood draw measure how fast someone is aging, so that interventions meant to slow aging can be evaluated? Using the Dunedin 1972–73 birth cohort, where decline in 19 organ-system markers was tracked across four time points over two decades, elastic-net regression on reliable CpG probes condensed that decline into DunedinPACE. In five more datasets the score had high test-retest reliability, tracked morbidity, disability, mortality and childhood adversity, and predicted outcomes beyond GrimAge.

title: Epigenetic scores for the circulating proteome as tools for disease prediction
synopsis: Can DNA methylation proxies of circulating proteins help predict disease? Epigenetic scores (EpiScores) for 953 plasma proteins were trained across four cohorts; 109 explained 1–58% of protein variance beyond known pQTL effects. Applied to Generation Scotland (n=9,537) with 14 years of follow-up, they gave 130 EpiScore–disease associations that held up after adjusting for immune cell proportions, lifestyle factors and biological aging; the diabetes EpiScores reproduced top proteomic diabetes biomarkers.

title: Improved analyses of GWAS summary statistics by reducing data heterogeneity and errors
synopsis: Summary-statistic methods can be biased by errors in GWAS data or the LD reference, or by mismatch between the two. DENTIST is a QC method that uses LD among variants to detect and remove such errors and heterogeneity. In simulations it lowered false-positive secondary signals in conditional and joint (COJO) analysis, especially for imputed rare variants (from >28% to <2%), and it also improved fine-mapping.

title: Lineage-tracing and translatomic analysis of damage-inducible mitotic cochlear progenitors identifies candidate genes regulating regeneration
synopsis: Can greater epithelial ridge (GER) cells in the neonatal mouse cochlea regenerate supporting cells by dividing? After Lgr5+ supporting cells were ablated in Lgr5-DTR mice, lineage tracing showed that GER progenitors divided, migrated into the organ of Corti and became lasting inner phalangeal-like cells with coordinated calcium transients. RiboTag RNA-seq identified 11 gene clusters marking the quiescent and damaged GER, including damage-responsive genes for migration and mitotic regeneration.

title: An open approach to systematically prioritize causal variants and genes at all published human GWAS trait-associated loci
synopsis: Open Targets Genetics systematically fine-maps and prioritizes causal genes across 133,441 published GWAS loci, integrating GWAS Catalog and UK Biobank data with transcriptomic, proteomic and epigenomic colocalization across 92 cell types and tissues. A machine-learning model trained on 445 gold-standard loci outperforms nearest-gene assignment. Prioritized genes are enriched for approved drug targets (OR = 8.1), and results are available via a web portal.

title: Exome sequencing and analysis of 454,787 UK Biobank participants
synopsis: Exome sequencing of 454,787 UK Biobank participants found 12 million coding variants, about 1 million of them loss-of-function. Testing these against 3,994 traits gave 564 gene–trait associations, and 91% of the rare-variant signals were independent of common GWAS signals. Protective genes included SLC9A3R2 (hypertension), MAP3K15 and FAM234A (diabetes) and SLC27A3 (asthma), and 81% of testable signals replicated across ancestries.

title: Incorporating functional priors improves polygenic prediction accuracy in UK Biobank and 23andMe data sets
synopsis: LDpred-funct adds trait-specific functional priors to polygenic prediction. The priors are fit with the baseline-LD model (coding, conserved, regulatory and LD-related annotations), and posterior effect sizes are regularized by cross-validation. On 21 heritable UK Biobank traits (average training N≈373K) it beat SBayesR by 4.6% in relative accuracy (mean R²=0.144; height R²=0.413, which rose to 0.431 when 23andMe data were added for N=1,107K).

title: Effective gene expression prediction from sequence by integrating long-range interactions
synopsis: Can gene expression be predicted more accurately from DNA sequence by capturing distal regulatory elements? Enformer, a deep learning model that integrates interactions up to 100 kb away, substantially improves expression prediction and variant effect estimates for natural variants and MPRA saturation mutagenesis. It also infers enhancer–promoter interactions from sequence alone, competitive with methods using experimental data.

title: Identifying causal variants by fine mapping across multiple studies
synopsis: GWAS of the same trait in different populations have different LD structures, which could sharpen fine-mapping. MsCAVIAR extends CAVIAR to multiple studies with a random-effects model. It needs only summary statistics and LD, allows several causal variants per locus, and lets effect sizes differ between populations.

title: A cell-type-specific atlas of the inner ear transcriptional response to acoustic trauma
synopsis: RiboTag and single-cell RNA-seq were used to map cell-type-specific transcriptional responses in the mouse inner ear after noise trauma. STAT3, IRF7 and immune genes were induced across cell types, but cell-type-specific changes dominated. These included ATF3/ATF4 stress-pathway induction in noise-resilient type 1A neurons, lower potassium-transport genes in the lateral wall, and lower deafness-associated genes in most cell types.

title: Large-scale cis- and trans-eQTL analyses identify thousands of genetic loci and polygenic scores that regulate blood gene expression
synopsis: The eQTLGen Consortium studied how genetic variants control gene expression using blood expression data from 31,684 people. Cis-eQTL were found for 88% of genes and replicated across tissues. Trans-eQTL were found for 37% of 10,317 trait-associated variants and worked mostly through transcription factors, and polygenic scores for 1,263 phenotypes correlated with the expression of 13% of genes.

title: Genome-wide association studies
gEAR: Gene Expression Analysis Resource portal for community-driven, multi-omic data exploration
Computationally efficient whole-genome regression for quantitative and binary traits
synopsis: GWAS across thousands of phenotypes is slow when relatedness and population structure must be accounted for. REGENIE is a machine-learning whole-genome regression method for quantitative and binary traits that loads only local genotype blocks, analyzes many phenotypes in parallel and adds a fast approximate Firth test for unbalanced case-control traits. On UK Biobank (up to 407,746 individuals), it stayed accurate while using much less time and memory.

title: An atlas of alternative polyadenylation quantitative trait loci contributing to complex trait and disease heritability
synopsis: Using GTEx data from 46 tissues in 467 individuals, a multi-tissue atlas maps about 0.4 million common variants linked to 3′UTR alternative polyadenylation (3′aQTLs). These variants act by changing poly(A) motifs, RNA structure and RBP binding sites, which CRISPR experiments supported, and they pointed to regulators such as LARP4. 3′aQTLs colocalize with about 16.1% of trait-associated variants and are largely distinct from eQTLs.

title: ArchR is a scalable software package for integrative single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis
synopsis: ArchR is an R package for complete analysis of single-cell chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) data. It handles doublet removal, clustering, peak calling, trajectory analysis, linking regulatory elements to genes, TF footprinting, predicting gene expression from accessibility and integration with scRNA-seq. It can process more than 1.2 million cells in 8 hours on a standard laptop.

title: Sequencing of 53,831 diverse genomes from the NHLBI TOPMed Program
lab: the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Consortium
synopsis: Describes the design, resources and early findings of TOPMed, which whole-genome sequenced ancestrally diverse, deeply phenotyped individuals to study heart, lung, blood and sleep disorders. The first 53,831 genomes contained over 400 million SNVs and indels; 97% had frequency below 1% and 46% were singletons. TOPMed haplotypes plus modern imputation extend GWAS down to variants of about 0.01% frequency.

title: Regulatory genomic circuitry of human disease loci by integrative epigenomics
synopsis: EpiMap compiles 10,000 epigenomic maps from 800 samples to define chromatin states, enhancers, enhancer modules, upstream regulators and target genes. Applied to 20,000 loci for 232 traits, it predicts relevant tissues, candidate causal variants and tissue-specific target genes, and splits complex traits into tissue-specific factors. Top loci often carry several driver variants acting through multiple enhancers, genes or tissues, pointing to widespread pleiotropy.

title: A comprehensive enhancer screen identifies TRAM2 as a key and novel mediator of YAP oncogenesis
synopsis: Genome-wide YAP ChIP profiling mapped YAP/TEAD4-bound enhancers, and a functional genetic screen then uncovered a network of enhancers required for YAP-driven proliferation. Follow-up focused on the TRAM2 enhancer, because TRAM2 expression correlates most strongly with YAP activity in nearly all tumor types. TRAM2 reproduces YAP-induced proliferation, migration and invasion, predicts poor survival, and acts largely through its direct client FSTL-1.

title: DOMINO: a network‐based active module identification algorithm with reduced rate of false calls
synopsis: Do active module identification (AMI) algorithms report network modules that are truly specific to the omics data analyzed? Testing six popular AMI methods on gene expression and GWAS data showed that GO terms enriched in modules from the real data often also turned up in modules from permuted data. A permutation-based GO validation scheme was used to define five performance criteria, and the new algorithm DOMINO beat all six methods on them.

title: Genetic mapping of developmental trajectories for complex traits and diseases
synopsis: A bioinformatics method that integrates GWAS signals with developmental scRNA-seq data to link cell differentiation trajectories to complex traits, find the pathways behind these links, and rank candidate genes. Applied to 11 traits and 12 scRNA-seq datasets, it recovered known links such as cortical inhibitory interneuron maturation with schizophrenia, hepatocytes with cholesterol, and pancreatic beta cells with type-2 diabetes. For each link it flagged top genes tied to both the trajectory's kinetics and genetic risk.

title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of prostate cancer identifies new susceptibility loci and informs genetic risk prediction
synopsis: A multi-ancestry meta-analysis of prostate cancer GWAS (107,247 cases, 127,006 controls) found 86 new risk variants, bringing the total to 269. Men in the top genetic risk score decile had an OR of 5.06 in European and 3.74 in African ancestry. Mean GRS was 2.18 times higher in African-ancestry men and 0.73 times lower in East Asian-ancestry men than in European-ancestry men, suggesting germline variation contributes to population differences in risk.

title: LDpred2: better, faster, stronger
synopsis: LDpred2 updates the LDpred method for building polygenic scores from GWAS summary statistics and an LD correlation matrix, fixing robustness problems in the first version. It also adds a 'sparse' option that lets effects be exactly zero and an 'auto' option that estimates both model parameters from the data. Across 8 real traits it reached a mean AUC of 65.1%, beating lassosum (63.8%), PRS-CS (62.9%) and SBayesR (61.5%), and it works best when run genome-wide rather than chromosome by chromosome.

title: Functionally informed fine-mapping and polygenic localization of complex trait heritability
synopsis: PolyFun uses functional annotations genome-wide, not just at significant loci, to set prior causal probabilities for fine-mapping tools like SuSiE and FINEMAP. Across 49 UK Biobank traits (average n=318,000), PolyFun+SuSiE found 3,025 variant-trait pairs with PIP>0.95, over 32% more than SuSiE. Polygenic localization showed that the SNPs explaining 50% of heritability range from 28 (hair color) to 2 million (number of children).

title: Expression pattern of cochlear microRNAs in the mammalian auditory hindbrain
synopsis: Do miRNAs abundant in the cochlea also act in the central auditory system? Expression of 12 such miRNAs was measured by qRT-PCR in the cochlea, auditory hindbrain and prefrontal cortex at E16, P0 and P30, and by in situ hybridization. All 12 were expressed in all three tissues, mostly with tissue- and stage-dependent differences, and were widespread in the cochlear nucleus and superior olivary complex.

title: Identification and characterization of key long non-coding RNAs in the mouse cochlea
synopsis: Four lncRNAs expressed in the mouse cochlea and also found in the human transcriptome were picked using inner-ear relevance criteria, to begin exploring lncRNA roles in hearing. Bioinformatic analysis confirmed they lack coding potential and are poorly conserved, and RNAscope showed each localizes to specific inner ear cell types with its own subcellular pattern and varied expression across tissues. A possible inner-ear pathway for Gas5 is proposed.

title: Genetic mapping of etiologic brain cell types for obesity
synopsis: Which cell types drive genetic predisposition to obesity? Mouse scRNA-seq covering 727 cell types across 17 organs was combined with BMI GWAS from over 457,000 people using a new integration strategy, identifying 26 cell types enriched for BMI heritability, all of them neurons from regions such as the hypothalamus, midbrain and cortex. Genes carrying obesity-linked coding mutations replicated the enrichment in midbrain anterior pretectal nucleus and periaqueductal gray cell types, pointing to brain areas that integrate sensory input, learning and memory.

title: Open Targets Genetics: systematic identification of trait-associated genes using large-scale genetics and functional genomics
synopsis: Open Targets Genetics is an open portal that links GWAS loci to likely causal variants and genes. It combines GWAS data with eQTL, pQTL and chromatin interaction data, and runs colocalization across 92 cell types and tissues, including the eQTL Catalogue. Users can search by variant, gene or study through regional, PheWAS and credible-set plots, bulk downloads or a GraphQL API, to support drug target discovery and repurposing.

title: The GTEx Consortium atlas of genetic regulatory effects across human tissues
synopsis: The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project dissects how genetic variation affects gene expression and splicing.

title: GFI1 functions to repress neuronal gene expression in the developing inner ear hair cells
synopsis: Asks what transcriptional programs GFI1 controls in developing inner ear hair cells. Using Gfi1cre;RiboTag mice to profile the hair cell translatome without GFI1, hair cell differentiation genes dropped while neuronal genes rose, including Pou4f1, Neurod1, Atoh1 and Insm1, matching the NEUROD1 regulon. Auditory and vestibular hair cells shared few changed genes, suggesting GFI1 both represses neuronal genes and activates hair cell maturation genes.

title: Dynamic incorporation of multiple in silico functional annotations empowers rare variant association analysis of large whole-genome sequencing studies at scale
lab: the NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Consortium
synopsis: Seed. Introduces STAAR, a scalable variant-set test that combines variant categories with multiple in silico functional annotations (summarised as annotation principal components) through dynamic weighting, while accounting for relatedness and population structure. Applied to lipid traits in about 30,000 TOPMed genomes, it found and replicated new rare-variant associations, including NPC1L1 missense variants and an intergenic region near APOC1P1 for LDL cholesterol.

title: Polygenic background modifies penetrance of monogenic variants for tier 1 genomic conditions
synopsis: Does polygenic background change penetrance in carriers of monogenic variants for familial hypercholesterolemia, hereditary breast/ovarian cancer and Lynch syndrome? In 80,928 individuals, risk by age 75 among carriers varied widely with polygenic score: 17–78% for coronary artery disease, 13–76% for breast cancer and 11–80% for colon cancer. Adding polygenic background should therefore sharpen risk estimates for monogenic carriers.

title: Systematic identification of functional SNPs interrupting 3’UTR polyadenylation signals
synopsis: Can common SNPs that disrupt the canonical polyadenylation signal (AAUAAA/AUUAAA) change 3'UTR alternative polyadenylation, gene expression and human traits? Among 2,305 PAS-disrupting SNPs, pA-QTL tests on GTEx RNA-seq found 330 that significantly altered use of their p(A) site, mostly causing 3'UTR lengthening and lower expression (~10% instead shortened the 3'UTR), and a few dozen colocalized with eQTL or GWAS signals.

title: Expanded encyclopaedias of DNA elements in the human and mouse genomes
synopsis: ENCODE phase III widened its maps of transcription, chromatin state and modification, DNA methylation, chromatin looping, and transcription factor and RNA-binding protein occupancy in human and mouse, including across mouse fetal development. The effort added 5,992 new datasets and combined selected regulatory data types into a registry of 926,535 human and 339,815 mouse candidate cis-regulatory elements, covering 7.9% and 3.4% of the two genomes. The registry can be searched through the SCREEN web server.

title: Tutorial: a guide to performing polygenic risk score analyses
synopsis: Protocol setting out guidelines for running and interpreting polygenic risk score analyses from GWAS summary data. It covers standard quality control, compares PRS calculation methods and comes with an introductory online tutorial. It also addresses common misreadings of PRS results, best-practice recommendations and open challenges.

title: PWAS: proteome-wide association study—linking genes and phenotypes by functional variation in proteins
synopsis: PWAS detects gene–phenotype associations driven by altered protein function. It aggregates all variants in a protein-coding gene, scores their combined functional impact with machine learning and probabilistic models, then tests whether inter-individual functional variability correlates with the phenotype, capturing recessive inheritance too. Compared with GWAS and other methods, it recovers causal coding genes and finds new associations; available as a command-line tool.

title: A Simple New Approach to Variable Selection in Regression, with Application to Genetic Fine Mapping
source: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
synopsis: SuSiE (sum of single effects) is a Bayesian variable-selection model fitted with iterative Bayesian stepwise selection (IBSS), a variational method that yields a credible set for each effect. It suits fine-mapping, where predictors are highly correlated and real effects are sparse. In numerical experiments it outperformed existing methods, and it was applied to fine-map genetic variants affecting alternative splicing in human cell lines.

title: The mutational constraint spectrum quantified from variation in 141,456 humans
synopsis: gnomAD combines 125,748 exomes and 15,708 genomes and, after artefact filtering, identifies 443,769 high-confidence predicted loss-of-function variants. Using an improved mutation-rate model, genes are ranked along a spectrum of tolerance to inactivation. The ranking is validated with model-organism and engineered human cell data and boosts gene discovery for both common and rare diseases.

title: Polygenic risk scores: from research tools to clinical instruments
synopsis: This review asks how polygenic risk scores could move from research into clinical use. Their discriminative ability in the general population is low, so they may be more useful in higher-prior-risk settings such as early diagnosis or choosing treatment. Remaining obstacles include weaker evidence in non-European ancestries and converting a PRS percentile into an absolute lifetime risk.

title: Transcription Dynamics Regulate Poly(A) Tails and Expression of the RNA Degradation Machinery to Balance mRNA Levels
synopsis: How do mammalian cells coordinate mRNA synthesis with mRNA decay? Slower transcription of specific genes, including at IRES elements that act as transcriptional pause sites, increases m6A deposition, favors CCR4-Not activity and shortens poly(A) tails, which destabilizes those mRNAs. When transcription changes globally, cells buffer mRNA levels instead: stress-induced elongation blocks inhibit the degradation machinery and stabilize mRNAs, while enhanced transcription after B cell activation or glucose stimulation has the opposite effect.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome
synopsis: HuRI is a systematic all-by-all map of human binary protein interactions, containing about 53,000 interactions, roughly four times the number of high-quality curated interactions from small-scale studies. Combined with genome, transcriptome and proteome data, it reveals the subcellular roles of specific interactions. Inferred tissue-specific networks suggest how context-specific functions arise and point to possible mechanisms for tissue-specific phenotypes in Mendelian diseases.

title: The nf-core framework for community-curated bioinformatics pipelines
Activity-by-contact model of enhancer–promoter regulation from thousands of CRISPR perturbations
synopsis: How do enhancers choose their target genes? CRISPRi-FlowFISH perturbed enhancers to test over 3,500 candidate enhancer-gene pairs for 30 genes. A simple activity-by-contact (ABC) model, built from chromatin state data, predicted these connections much better than earlier methods and can produce genome-wide enhancer-gene maps for a given cell type to help interpret noncoding disease variants.

title: MaveDB: an open-source platform to distribute and interpret data from multiplexed assays of variant effect
synopsis: Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs), such as deep mutational scans and massively parallel reporter assays, have had no standard place to find or share their data. MaveDB (mavedb.org) is a public, interoperable repository for large-scale variant impact measurements. It comes with MaveVis, a companion tool that retrieves, visualizes and contextualizes variant effect maps.

title: Scaling computational genomics to millions of individuals with GPUs
synopsis: Genomics methods will need to scale from thousands to millions of samples, and general-purpose GPU libraries such as PyTorch and TensorFlow are proposed as a cheap way to get there. Using them for genomic computations cut runtime more than 200-fold and cost about 5-10-fold compared with CPUs.

title: GWAS Identifies 44 Independent Associated Genomic Loci for Self-Reported Adult Hearing Difficulty in UK Biobank
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: GWASs of two self-reported hearing phenotypes in more than 250,000 UK Biobank participants aged 40-69 sought the genetic basis of age-related hearing impairment. They found 44 independent genome-wide significant loci, 34 of them new for any form of hearing loss, enriched for auditory, neuronal and inner-ear processes and genetically correlated with personality and psychological traits. Mouse cochlea immunohistochemistry pointed to NID2, CLRN2 and ARHGEF28.

title: A global overview of pleiotropy and genetic architecture in complex traits
synopsis: To map pleiotropy and genetic architecture across traits, 4,155 public GWASs were analyzed, with in-depth study of well-powered GWASs for 558 traits. Trait-associated loci cover more than half the genome, and 90% overlap loci of multiple traits. Likely causal variants are enriched in coding, flanking and regulatory regions, and traits vary in polygenicity and discoverability; results are available in the GWAS ATLAS.

title: The “All of Us” Research Program
synopsis: Introduces the All of Us Research Program, a US cohort that aims to enrol at least 1 million diverse adults through more than 340 recruitment sites. It collects questionnaires, EHRs, physical measurements, digital health data and biospecimens. By July 2019 over 175,000 people had given biospecimens, more than 80% from groups under-represented in research, and EHR data covered over 112,000 participants from 34 sites.

title: A CRISPR-Cas9 screen identifies essential CTCF anchor sites for estrogen receptor-driven breast cancer cell proliferation
synopsis: Are CTCF-binding elements (CBEs) near ERα-bound enhancers needed for ERα-driven breast cancer cell proliferation? A CRISPR screen targeting such CBEs found four functional sites, one of which reshapes chromatin conformation to activate PREX1, a key ERα target gene. High PREX1 expression marks ERα dependency in cell lines and is associated with good outcome after anti-hormonal therapy.

title: PRSice-2: Polygenic Risk Score software for biobank-scale data
synopsis: PRSice-2 is C++ software for running polygenic risk score analyses quickly on biobank-scale genotyped or imputed data. It reports empirical association P-values that are not inflated by overfitting, supports several inheritance models and can test many continuous or binary traits at once. Compared with PRSice-1, LDpred and lassosum, it runs much faster and uses far less memory while predicting about as well.

title: A Fast and Flexible Framework for Network-Assisted Genomic Association
synopsis: NAGA (Network Assisted Genomic Association) is a fast network-propagation tool that strengthens GWAS signals using protein networks drawn from NDEx, finishing a genome-wide analysis in under 5 minutes on a laptop. On schizophrenia data it recovered many known disease genes and boosted less appreciated ones such as amyloid beta precursor. Across eight gene–disease tasks it beat conventional methods at recovering known genes and producing replicable results, with Cytoscape used for visualization.

title: The EXPANDER Integrated Platform for Transcriptome Analysis
synopsis: EXPANDER is a 'one-stop shop' for transcriptome analysis of RNA-seq or array data, with built-in support for 18 organisms. Starting from an expression matrix, it covers normalization, differential expression, clustering, biclustering, enrichment, network and motif analyses. Developed since 2003, it has over 18,000 downloads and 540 citations, and the recent version adds combined expression and ChIP-seq analysis for inferring transcriptional networks.

title: CUT&Tag for efficient epigenomic profiling of small samples and single cells
synopsis: CUT&Tag profiles chromatin features in small samples. An antibody binds the target protein in situ and tethers a protein A–Tn5 transposase, which cuts and tags the nearby DNA to give high-resolution libraries with very low background. The whole protocol runs in one tube or microwell in a single day.

title: Polygenic prediction via Bayesian regression and continuous shrinkage priors
synopsis: PRS-CS builds polygenic risk scores from GWAS summary statistics and an external LD reference panel, using high-dimensional Bayesian regression with a continuous shrinkage prior on SNP effects. The prior adapts to different genetic architectures, is computationally efficient, and models local LD jointly. In UK Biobank simulations and on 6 diseases and 6 quantitative traits in the Partners HealthCare Biobank, it predicted more accurately than existing methods, with the largest gains at large training sample sizes.

title: Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities
synopsis: Argues that today's polygenic risk scores, built mostly from European-ancestry GWAS, predict several times better in Europeans than in other ancestries. Clinical use would therefore benefit European-descent groups most and could widen health disparities. Early diversification efforts help even with smaller non-European samples, and the authors call for more diverse cohorts and public release of summary statistics.

title: Opportunities and challenges for transcriptome-wide association studies
synopsis: Perspective on how well transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) prioritize causal genes at GWAS loci. It uses simulations and curated candidate genes for schizophrenia, LDL cholesterol and Crohn's disease. TWAS beats simple baselines but can flag non-causal genes because of shared eQTLs, especially when using non-trait-relevant tissues, and the authors propose best practices.

title: ACAT: A Fast and Powerful p Value Combination Method for Rare-Variant Analysis in Sequencing Studies
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Set-based rare-variant tests lose power when only a few variants in a set are causal, and they are sensitive to effect directions and weighting. ACAT, an aggregated Cauchy p value combination method, yields a variant-level set test (ACAT-V) and an omnibus test (ACAT-O) combining burden, SKAT and ACAT-V. In simulations and ARIC whole-genome sequencing data, ACAT-V complemented SKAT and burden tests, and ACAT-O gave more robust, higher power.

title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan
synopsis: Can DNA methylation stand in for plasma protein levels and be combined into a lifespan predictor? Seven DNAm surrogates of plasma proteins (including PAI-1 and GDF15) plus a DNAm estimate of smoking pack-years were combined into DNAm GrimAge. Validated in thousands of individuals, it beat other clocks at predicting time to death (P=2.0E-75), coronary heart disease and cancer, and age-adjusted GrimAge (AgeAccelGrim) was tied to comorbidities, menopause age and lifestyle factors.

title: BOADICEA: a comprehensive breast cancer risk prediction model incorporating genetic and nongenetic risk factors
synopsis: The BOADICEA breast cancer risk model was extended to combine truncating variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, CHEK2 and ATM with a 313-SNP PRS, a residual polygenic component, lifestyle, hormonal and reproductive factors, and mammographic density. Of all factors, the PRS spread predicted UK risk the widest, followed by mammographic density. With every factor combined, predicted lifetime risk ranged from 2.8% at the 1st percentile to 30.6% at the 99th, giving the strongest risk stratification.

title: A Genome-wide Framework for Mapping Gene Regulation via Cellular Genetic Screens
synopsis: To link candidate enhancers to their target genes, random combinations of dCas9-KRAB perturbations were introduced into many cells and read out by single-cell RNA-seq, an approach modeled on eQTL mapping. Across 5,920 targeted enhancers and 254,974 transcriptomes, 664 cis enhancer-gene pairs were found (470 high-confidence). These pairs were enriched for specific transcription factors, non-housekeeping genes, and linear and 3D proximity to their targets.

title: Predicting Splicing from Primary Sequence with Deep Learning
synopsis: A deep neural network (SpliceAI) predicts splice junctions from pre-mRNA sequence alone, flagging noncoding variants that cause cryptic splicing. Predicted splice-altering synonymous and intronic variants often validate by RNA-seq and are strongly selected against in humans. Such de novo variants are enriched in autism and intellectual disability (21 of 28 patients validated), and they may explain 9–11% of pathogenic mutations in rare disease.

title: Polygenic Risk Scores for Prediction of Breast Cancer and Breast Cancer Subtypes
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Breast cancer PRSs optimized for ER-specific disease were built from 94,075 cases and 75,017 controls using stepwise or lasso regression. They were then validated in 10 prospective studies and 190,040 UK Biobank women. The best 313-SNP PRS gave an OR of 1.61 per SD (AUC 0.630), was well calibrated, and the top centile had a 32.6% lifetime risk.

title: The NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog of published genome-wide association studies, targeted arrays and summary statistics 2019
synopsis: The 2019 update of the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog, a curated collection of published GWASs that now also covers targeted and exome arrays. As of September 2018 it held 5,687 GWASs with 71,673 variant-trait associations from 3,567 publications, plus 284 full summary-statistics datasets. New features include a RESTful API, an improved web interface, a summary statistics database and a proposed standard format for summary statistics.

title: Helios is a key transcriptional regulator of outer hair cell maturation
synopsis: Ikzf2, which encodes Helios, is identified as a transcription factor essential for outer hair cell maturation and hearing in mice. In the cello mouse, an Ikzf2 point mutation causes early-onset sensorineural hearing loss, with much weaker prestin-dependent electromotility and lower Slc26a5 and Ocm expression. Forcing Ikzf2 expression in inner hair cells turned on outer-hair-cell genes, reduced inner-hair-cell genes and made the cells electromotile.

title: Expert specification of the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines for genetic hearing loss
synopsis: The ClinGen Hearing Loss Expert Panel adapted the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines to genetic hearing loss. Of the rules, 3 were kept unchanged, 4 removed and 21 specified for hearing loss, then tested on a pilot set of 51 variants. Applying the specified rules and pooling evidence across labs changed the classification of 37% (19/51) of the pilot variants.

title: The UK Biobank resource with deep phenotyping and genomic data
synopsis: UK Biobank is a prospective cohort of about 500,000 UK adults aged 40–69, with deep phenotyping that includes biomarkers, imaging, lifestyle data and linked health records, plus genome-wide genotyping. The paper covers central genotype QC, population structure, relatedness, phasing and imputation to about 96 million variants. HLA alleles at 11 genes were also imputed, recovering known HLA-disease associations.

title: Fine-mapping type 2 diabetes loci to single-variant resolution using high-density imputation and islet-specific epigenome maps
synopsis: A type 2 diabetes GWAS of 898,130 European-descent individuals used high-density imputation and found 243 loci, 135 of them new, with 403 distinct signals. Fine-mapping placed over 80% posterior probability on a single variant at 51 signals, rising to 73 after adding islet epigenomic annotations. Coding variants pointed to 18 genes, chip heritability explained 18% of T2D risk, and prevalence differed more than ninefold between polygenic score extremes.

title: Genomic Landscape and Mutational Signatures of Deafness-Associated Genes
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: The Deafness Variation Database (DVD) combines genetic, genomic and clinical data with expert curation to classify variants in 152 hearing-loss genes. Of 876,139 variants, more than 8,100 were classed pathogenic or likely pathogenic, over 172,000 benign or likely benign, and over 695,000 of uncertain significance; 1,270 were reclassified, 300 with clinical impact. Over 96% of coding variants were rare or novel, and pathogenicity depended on allele frequency, variant effect and protein domain.

title: Genomic meta-analysis of the interplay between 3D chromatin organization and gene expression programs under basal and stress conditions
synopsis: A meta-analysis combining Hi-C data from 13 cell lines with dozens of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq datasets, under basal and treated conditions, asked how 3D chromatin organization relates to gene expression. Differences in A/B compartments between cell lines tracked differential expression and TF binding, and basal compartments also correlated with treatment-induced programs. However, many differential events occurred in loci in the A compartment in both cell types, so other factors also shape cell-type-specific transcription.

title: Functional CRISPR screen identifies AP1-associated enhancer regulating FOXF1 to modulate oncogene-induced senescence
synopsis: Which enhancers are needed to establish oncogene-induced senescence? Genome-wide eRNA profiling found enhancers activated by oncogenic stress and enriched for AP-1 motifs, and a CRISPR-Cas9 screen of these AP-1-associated enhancers identified Enh AP1-OIS1, whose AP-1 site mutation lets cells bypass senescence. The enhancer's target is FOXF1, which mediates its effect, revealing an AP-1–FOXF1 senescence cascade.

title: Genome-wide polygenic scores for common diseases identify individuals with risk equivalent to monogenic mutations
synopsis: Asks whether genome-wide polygenic scores can find people whose risk is as high as that of monogenic mutation carriers. Scores built and validated for five diseases flag 8.0%, 6.1%, 3.5%, 3.2% and 1.5% of the population at more than threefold risk for CAD, atrial fibrillation, T2D, IBD and breast cancer. For CAD, that is 20 times the carrier frequency of comparable monogenic mutations.

title: Bioconda: sustainable and comprehensive software distribution for the life sciences
From genome-wide associations to candidate causal variants by statistical fine-mapping
synopsis: Review of statistical fine-mapping for moving from GWAS associations to candidate causal variants, weighing the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches. Topics include linkage disequilibrium, choice of fine-mapping method, trans-ethnic studies, integrating functional annotation, and study design factors that affect performance.

title: The Galaxy platform for accessible, reproducible and collaborative biomedical analyses: 2018 update
synopsis: Galaxy is a web-based open-source platform for accessible, reproducible and shareable analysis of large biomedical datasets in genomics, proteomics, metabolomics and imaging. This 2018 update covers two years of work on the core framework, user interface, tools and training, which now supports analyses of tens of thousands of datasets and offers more than 5,500 tools in the ToolShed. Community-written tutorials for common genomic analyses were added, and the numbers of public servers, developers and users all grew substantially.

title: The personal and clinical utility of polygenic risk scores
synopsis: Review of whether polygenic risk profiling is useful for individuals and in the clinic, after early GWAS seemed to offer little predictive value. It weighs recent evidence that polygenic profiles can pick out groups of people who would benefit from knowing their probabilistic disease susceptibility.

title: Exploring the phenotypic consequences of tissue specific gene expression variation inferred from GWAS summary statistics
synopsis: S-PrediXcan computes PrediXcan gene-expression association results from GWAS summary statistics, shown to be accurate and robust to misspecified reference sets. Applied to 44 GTEx tissues and over 100 phenotypes, it builds a public catalog of expression–trait associations, with replication in an independent cohort. Most associations are tissue-specific, and monogenic disease genes are enriched among associations for related traits.

title: FOCS: a novel method for analyzing enhancer and gene activity patterns infers an extensive enhancer–promoter map
synopsis: Current methods for linking enhancers to promoters from activity data give many false positives. FOCS is a new inference method that, benchmarked against ChIA-PET, HiChIP and eQTL data, has a lower false discovery rate and more power. Applying it to 2630 samples from ENCODE, Roadmap Epigenomics, FANTOM5 and a new GRO-seq compendium produced extensive enhancer–promoter maps, available online.

title: An epigenetic biomarker of aging for lifespan and healthspan
synopsis: Earlier epigenetic clocks were trained on chronological age; this work instead trains on a composite clinical phenotypic age to better capture lifespan and healthspan. A two-step approach gives DNAm PhenoAge, which predicts mortality, cancers, healthspan, physical function and Alzheimer's disease better than earlier clocks and tracks age in every tissue tested. In sorted cells, faster epigenetic aging was linked to higher pro-inflammatory and interferon signaling and lower DNA-repair, translational and mitochondrial activity.

title: Heritability enrichment of specifically expressed genes identifies disease-relevant tissues and cell types
synopsis: Identifies disease-relevant tissues and cell types by testing, with stratified LD score regression, whether heritability is enriched near genes specifically expressed in each tissue. Across 48 diseases and traits (average N = 169,331), 34 showed significant tissue-specific enrichment (FDR < 5%). Brain analyses found inhibitory over excitatory neuron enrichment for bipolar disorder and the reverse for schizophrenia and BMI.

title: QAPA: a new method for the systematic analysis of alternative polyadenylation from RNA-seq data
synopsis: QAPA infers alternative polyadenylation from ordinary RNA-seq and is faster and more sensitive than other methods. Applied to neurogenesis data, it revealed discrete, temporally coordinated APA programs with little overlap with genes regulated by alternative splicing. Modeling the data uncovered an APA sequence code.

title: Sequential regulatory activity prediction across chromosomes with convolutional neural networks
synopsis: Aims to predict cell-type-specific epigenetic and transcriptional profiles across large mammalian genomes from DNA sequence alone. A convolutional neural network (Basenji) learns promoters and distal regulatory elements and combines them to predict gene expression. Predicted variant effects on expression align well with causal eQTL variants, supporting use in mechanistic hypotheses and disease-locus fine-mapping.

title: The Human Cell Atlas
synopsis: Sets out the Human Cell Atlas, an international effort to define every human cell type by molecular profiles such as gene expression and to connect them to classical features like location and morphology. It describes the project's goals, possible uses for studying development, regulation and disease, early proofs of concept, and design choices, including a commitment to open data, code and community.

title: Association analysis identifies 65 new breast cancer risk loci
synopsis: A breast cancer GWAS of 122,977 cases and 105,974 controls of European ancestry, plus about 14,000 cases and 13,000 controls of East Asian ancestry, found 65 new risk loci. Most credible risk SNPs lie in distal regulatory elements, and their predicted target genes overlap strongly with somatic driver genes in breast tumours. Heritability from SNPs in regulatory features was enriched 2–5-fold, especially at certain transcription factor binding sites.

title: Characterization of noncoding regulatory DNA in the human genome
synopsis: A review of how functional noncoding regulatory DNA is mapped in the human genome, a key question because most common-disease variants fall outside genes. It covers chromatin accessibility and epigenetic marks for finding candidate elements, and the limits of reporter assays that remove elements from their chromosomal context. It argues that genome-editing perturbation screens can lead to an unbiased functional map of noncoding elements.

title: 10 Years of GWAS Discovery: Biology, Function, and Translation
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Review of the first decade of GWAS, covering discoveries in population and complex-trait genetics, disease biology and translation toward therapeutics. It also looks ahead to the next ten years. Studies are expected to use millions of imputed array samples and hundreds of thousands of whole-genome sequences.

title: The contribution of rare variants to risk of schizophrenia in individuals with and without intellectual disability
synopsis: Seed (closest title match to the user's wording). Meta-analysed exome rare coding variants, de novo mutations and CNVs in schizophrenia and found an excess of rare damaging variants in about 3,500 loss-of-function-intolerant genes. The burden is concentrated in neurodevelopmental-disorder genes in patients with intellectual disability but persists, more weakly, in patients without it, pointing to shared risk with neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Network propagation: a universal amplifier of genetic associations
synopsis: Review of network-based methods that boost weak genetic association signals, built on the principle that genes behind the same phenotype tend to interact. Techniques based on random walks, information diffusion and electrical resistance are shown to be variants of one framework, network propagation. That framework is broadly useful for finding disease genes, modules and drug targets.

title: An Expanded View of Complex Traits: From Polygenic to Omnigenic
synopsis: Proposes the "omnigenic" model to explain why complex-trait association signals are spread across most of the genome. Because gene regulatory networks are highly interconnected, any gene expressed in disease-relevant cells can affect core disease genes. As a result, most heritability comes from peripheral genes outside core pathways.

title: Development and validation of QRISK3 risk prediction algorithms to estimate future risk of cardiovascular disease: prospective cohort study
synopsis: QRISK3 updates the QRISK2 10-year cardiovascular risk model by adding new risk factors. It includes CKD stage 3-5, blood pressure variability, migraine, corticosteroids, SLE, atypical antipsychotics, severe mental illness and erectile dysfunction, while HIV/AIDS was dropped as non-significant. Sex-specific Cox models were derived on 7.89 million English primary-care patients and validated on 2.67 million, reaching a Harrell's C of 0.88 in women and 0.86 in men, with overall performance similar to QRISK2.

title: Nextflow enables reproducible computational workflows
Gfi1Cre mice have early onset progressive hearing loss and induce recombination in numerous inner ear non-hair cells
synopsis: The widely used Gfi1Cre hair-cell driver was checked for specificity and side effects using immunofluorescence and flow cytometry. Cre recombination reached many non-hair cells, mostly resident macrophages that outnumber hair cells in the neonatal inner ear. Heterozygous Gfi1Cre mice developed early-onset progressive hearing loss and small but significant changes in hair-cell-enriched transcripts, while vestibular function stayed normal up to 10 months.

title: Overview of the BioBank Japan Project: Study design and profile
synopsis: BioBank Japan is a patient-based registry launched in 2003 to support personalized medicine, enrolling patients with any of 47 common diseases at 12 institutes between 2003 and 2008. About 200,000 participants were registered, with baseline DNA, annual serum and clinical data through 2013. Baseline data cover 199,982 people (53.1% male, mean age about 62), and survival data cover 141,612.

title: Evaluation of Polygenic Risk Scores for Breast and Ovarian Cancer Risk Prediction in BRCA1 and BRCA2 Mutation Carriers
source: JNCI: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
synopsis: Polygenic risk scores built from GWAS SNPs for breast and ovarian cancer were tested in 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 carriers using a weighted cohort approach. The ER-negative breast cancer PRS predicted best in BRCA1 carriers (HR 1.27 per SD) and the overall breast cancer PRS in BRCA2 carriers (HR 1.22), while the ovarian cancer PRS was strongly predictive in both groups. Absolute risks differed by more than 10% between the top and bottom PRS deciles; for example, BRCA2 carriers' ovarian cancer risk by age 80 ranged from 6% to 19%.

title: Colocalization of GWAS and eQTL Signals Detects Target Genes
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Asks whether the same causal variant underlies a GWAS locus and an eQTL, to identify target genes and tissues. eCAVIAR is a probabilistic colocalization method that allows multiple causal variants per locus and uses only summary statistics. In simulations and eQTL data from 45 tissues, it prioritizes likely relevant tissues and target genes for glucose- and insulin-related trait loci.

title: Systematic mapping of functional enhancer–promoter connections with CRISPR interference
synopsis: Aims to find which noncoding regions actually control a gene's transcription. CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens were used to map functional enhancer-promoter connections at the GATA1 and MYC loci. The approach offers an unbiased functional way to test candidate enhancer-promoter links.

title: Alternative polyadenylation of mRNA precursors
synopsis: A review of alternative polyadenylation (APA), a widespread eukaryotic mechanism that produces different 3' ends on Pol II transcripts and varies by tissue, proliferation and differentiation. It covers APA's roles in mRNA metabolism, protein diversity and localization. It also covers APA's mechanisms: changing levels of core processing factors and RNA-binding proteins, and regulation through transcription.

title: HiChIP: efficient and sensitive analysis of protein-directed genome architecture
synopsis: HiChIP is a protein-centric chromatin conformation method for mapping genome architecture tied to a chosen protein. Compared with ChIA-PET, it yields over 10-fold more conformation-informative reads and needs over 100-fold less input. HiChIP of cohesin shows multiscale genome architecture with higher signal-to-background than in situ Hi-C.

title: Basset: learning the regulatory code of the accessible genome with deep convolutional neural networks
synopsis: Basset is an open-source deep convolutional neural network tool that predicts chromatin accessibility directly from DNA sequence. Trained on DNase-seq peaks from 164 cell types, it beats earlier methods. Its predicted allelic accessibility changes are much larger for likely causal GWAS SNPs than for nearby SNPs in linkage disequilibrium, which makes it useful for annotating noncoding variants.

title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
synopsis: Stakeholders from academia, industry, funding agencies and publishers jointly drew up and endorsed the FAIR principles, a concise and measurable guide to making scholarly data reusable. Unlike similar efforts focused on human users, FAIR stresses that machines should be able to find and use data automatically. This is the first formal publication of the principles, with their rationale and example implementations.

title: 3’UTR Shortening Potentiates MicroRNA-Based Repression of Pro-differentiation Genes in Proliferating Human Cells
synopsis: Does 3'UTR shortening in proliferating cells do more than let growth genes escape microRNA repression? Using 3' sequencing to map human UTR ends across several cell lines, conserved miRNA sites turned out to cluster just upstream of APA sites, especially in pro-differentiation/anti-proliferative genes and for the miR17-92 cluster. Shortening may therefore move these sites near the UTR end, where they are more active, and strengthen repression of anti-proliferative genes.

title: Integrative approaches for large-scale transcriptome-wide association studies
FINEMAP: efficient variable selection using summary data from genome-wide association studies
synopsis: FINEMAP fine-maps GWAS loci from summary statistics, using a shotgun stochastic search over the most important causal configurations instead of checking every possible configuration. It gives accurate results in a fraction of the runtime of existing methods. That makes it suited to large GWAS and sequencing datasets.

title: Functional genetic screens for enhancer elements in the human genome using CRISPR-Cas9
synopsis: Two CRISPR-Cas9 genetic screens were built to find functional enhancers in their native chromatin context, as an alternative to episomal reporter assays. Cas9 was aimed at transcription factor binding sites within enhancers, which identified several functional elements, including enhancers that mediate p53 (TP53) and ERα (ESR1) gene regulation. A tiling CRISPR screen also pinpointed functional domains within individual enhancers.

title: Genome-Wide Polyadenylation Maps Reveal Dynamic mRNA 3′-End Formation in the Failing Human Heart
synopsis: Is 3′UTR length regulated by alternative polyadenylation (APA) in the human heart, and does this change in heart failure? 3′-end sequencing (e3′-Seq) of healthy and failing hearts revealed disease-specific APA, with shortened 3′UTRs in RNA-binding genes and longer 3′UTRs in cytoskeletal/actin-binding genes. RNA-seq showed 3′UTR length inversely correlated with expression, and the APA regulator PABPN1 was strongly reduced in failing hearts.

title: Million Veteran Program: A mega-biobank to study genetic influences on health and disease
synopsis: This report lays out the design of the Million Veteran Program, a VA observational cohort and mega-biobank that combines questionnaires, electronic health records and blood samples for genomic testing. Enrollment began in 2011 and reached 397,104 veterans at about 50 sites by August 2015. Of the 199,348 genotyped so far, 92% are male, 77.2% white and 13.5% African American.

title: RFX transcription factors are essential for hearing in mice
synopsis: Little is known about what drives postnatal hair cell maturation, so cell-type-specific functional genomic analysis was applied to auditory and vestibular epithelia transcriptomes from early postnatal mice. RFX transcription factors emerged as conserved key regulators of hair-cell-specific genes, with Rfx1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 found in developing hair cells. Rfx1/3 conditional knockout mice were deaf because their initially normal outer hair cells were quickly lost.

title: A global reference for human genetic variation
synopsis: The final 1000 Genomes Project release reconstructs genomes of 2,504 people from 26 populations using low-coverage WGS, deep exome sequencing and microarray genotyping. It catalogs over 88 million phased variants (84.7M SNPs, 3.6M indels, 60,000 structural variants), capturing more than 99% of SNPs above 1% frequency across ancestries. The paper also describes global variation patterns and what they mean for common-disease studies.

title: Partitioning heritability by functional annotation using genome-wide association summary statistics
synopsis: Asks how much different functional parts of the genome, including cell type–specific elements, contribute to complex-trait heritability. Introduces stratified LD score regression, which partitions heritability from GWAS summary statistics while accounting for linked markers, and applies it to 17 diseases and traits (mean N = 73,599). Conserved regions are strongly enriched across traits, FANTOM5 enhancers are highly enriched for immune diseases, and CNS cell types are enriched for BMI, age at menarche, educational attainment and smoking.

title: Genetic variance estimation with imputed variants finds negligible missing heritability for human height and body mass index
synopsis: GREML-LDMS, a method for estimating heritability in unrelated individuals, was applied to about 17 million imputed variants in 44,126 people. Simulations show imputation captures roughly 97% of common-variant and 68% of rare-variant variation. Imputed variants explain 56% of height variance and 27% of BMI variance, so likely heritabilities of 60–70% and 30–40% leave little missing heritability.

title: Predicting effects of noncoding variants with deep learning–based sequence model
synopsis: Aims to predict functional effects of noncoding variants directly from sequence. DeepSEA, a deep learning framework trained on large-scale chromatin-profiling data, learns a regulatory sequence code and predicts chromatin effects of alterations at single-nucleotide resolution. This capability improves prioritization of functional variants, including eQTLs and disease-associated variants.

title: Mapping Nucleosome Resolution Chromosome Folding in Yeast by Micro-C
synopsis: Micro-C is a Hi-C variant that fragments chromatin with micrococcal nuclease instead of restriction enzymes, giving nucleosome-resolution folding maps. In budding yeast it shows abundant self-associating domains of one to five genes, with strong boundaries at promoters of highly transcribed genes and RSC-bound regions of rapid histone turnover. Mutant analyses implicate RSC, Ssu72, Mediator, Rtt109 and the H4 N-terminal tail in yeast genome folding.

title: A method to predict the impact of regulatory variants from DNA sequence
Mapping long-range promoter contacts in human cells with high-resolution capture Hi-C
synopsis: Capture Hi-C (CHi-C) was used to profile long-range contacts of almost 22,000 promoters in 2 human blood cell types, yielding over 1.6 million shared and cell type-restricted interactions spanning hundreds of kilobases. Active genes contact enhancer-like elements, while inactive genes contact elements with repressive marks that may act as long-range silencers. Interacting loci are enriched for disease-associated SNPs.

title: Disruptions of Topological Chromatin Domains Cause Pathogenic Rewiring of Gene-Enhancer Interactions
synopsis: Can disrupting topologically associated domains (TADs) cause disease by rewiring enhancer-promoter contacts? Human limb malformations with deletions, inversions or duplications at the WNT6/IHH/EPHA4/PAX3 locus were studied, alongside matching CRISPR-engineered mice and patient fibroblasts. Rearrangements that break CTCF-associated boundaries misplace Epha4 limb enhancers, which then drive ectopic expression of other genes, suggesting criteria for judging structural variant pathogenicity.

title: Understanding multicellular function and disease with human tissue-specific networks
synopsis: Genome-wide functional interaction networks were built for 144 human tissues and cell types by Bayesian integration of thousands of experiments. The tissue-specific networks predict lineage-specific responses to perturbation, show how gene roles change between tissues and link related diseases. The resulting NetWAS method reranks nominally significant GWAS genes with these networks and finds disease genes more accurately than GWAS alone; networks and tools are available through the GIANT webserver.

title: MAGMA: Generalized Gene-Set Analysis of GWAS Data
synopsis: MAGMA performs gene and gene-set analysis of GWAS data, addressing LD-related power loss, poor detection of multi-marker effects and costly permutation. Gene analysis uses multiple regression, with a separate regression-based gene-set layer that handles continuous gene properties and multiple sets jointly. In simulations and Crohn's disease data, MAGMA had more power than other tools, correct type 1 error, and ran considerably faster.

title: A DIseAse MOdule Detection (DIAMOnD) Algorithm Derived from a Systematic Analysis of Connectivity Patterns of Disease Proteins in the Human Interactome
synopsis: What connectivity patterns in the human interactome define disease modules? Network analysis of proteins from 70 complex diseases showed they do not form locally dense communities; connectivity significance, a measure of how many links a protein shares with known disease proteins, was the strongest predictor. That finding is the basis of DIAMOnD, an algorithm that grows full disease modules from seed proteins, tested on synthetic data and validated across many diseases.

title: UK Biobank: An Open Access Resource for Identifying the Causes of a Wide Range of Complex Diseases of Middle and Old Age
synopsis: Introduces UK Biobank, a large population-based prospective cohort set up as an open-access resource. Its aim is to study genetic and non-genetic determinants of the complex diseases of middle and old age.

title: Second-generation PLINK: rising to the challenge of larger and richer datasets
synopsis: PLINK 1.9 is a rewrite of the PLINK GWAS toolset built for larger imputed and sequencing datasets. It uses bit-level parallelism and faster algorithms, including new Hardy-Weinberg and Fisher's exact tests, which speed most operations up by 1-4 orders of magnitude and let it handle datasets too large to fit in RAM. An extended file format, the basis of PLINK 2.0, adds support for genotype likelihoods, phase, multiallelic variants and ref/alt alleles.

title: Uncovering disease-disease relationships through the incomplete interactome
synopsis: Disease modules (localized clusters of disease proteins in the interactome) are used to relate diseases despite incomplete protein-protein interaction maps. A mathematical threshold for data coverage determines when a disease module can be detected. Network distance between modules predicts disease pairs with shared protein components, co-expression, symptoms and comorbidity, revealing links even where no disease genes are shared.

title: Integrative analysis of 111 reference human epigenomes
synopsis: The NIH Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium analysed 111 reference human epigenomes from primary cells and tissues. They profiled histone marks, DNA accessibility, DNA methylation and RNA expression. The analysis maps regulatory elements, coordinated regulatory modules and their likely activators and repressors.

title: LD Score regression distinguishes confounding from polygenicity in genome-wide association studies
lab: the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium
synopsis: Inflated GWAS test statistics can come from true polygenic signal or from confounding such as population stratification and cryptic relatedness, and existing methods could not tell these apart. LD Score regression separates the two by regressing association statistics on each variant's linkage disequilibrium score. Its intercept gives a more powerful and accurate correction than genomic control, and polygenicity explains most of the inflation in many large GWAS.

title: Tissue-based map of the human proteome
synopsis: The aim was to chart where the roughly 20,000 human protein-coding genes are expressed across the body. Expression was profiled in 32 human tissues using RNA measurements together with antibody-based profiling that locates the proteins themselves. The resulting tissue-level proteome map can be explored through an interactive website.

title: Pan-cancer network analysis identifies combinations of rare somatic mutations across pathways and protein complexes
synopsis: Rare mutations spread thinly across many genes make cancer drivers hard to detect. HotNet2, a new algorithm for finding significantly mutated subnetworks, was applied to 3,281 TCGA tumors from 12 cancer types. It found 16 significant subnetworks, covering known signaling pathways and less studied complexes such as cohesin and condensin, often with co-occurring mutations and dozens of rarely mutated genes that other evidence links to cancer.

title: A 3D Map of the Human Genome at Kilobase Resolution Reveals Principles of Chromatin Looping
synopsis: In situ Hi-C was used to build haploid and diploid 3D genome maps for nine cell types, reaching 1 kb resolution in human lymphoblastoid cells with 4.9 billion contacts. Genomes split into contact domains (median 185 kb) that group into six subcompartments, and about 10,000 loops were found linking promoters and enhancers. Loop anchors bind CTCF, and over 90% of the motif pairs face each other (convergent orientation).

title: QuantSeq 3′ mRNA sequencing for RNA quantification
Dynamic analyses of alternative polyadenylation from RNA-seq reveal a 3′-UTR landscape across seven tumour types
synopsis: DaPars detects dynamic alternative polyadenylation de novo from standard RNA-seq. Across 358 TCGA tumour/normal pairs from seven tumour types, it found 1,346 genes with recurrent tumour-specific APA, 91% with shortened 3′UTRs that can escape microRNA repression (e.g., GLS). Some APA events added prognostic value beyond clinical variables, and CstF64 emerged as a master regulator of 3′UTR shortening.

title: Integrating Functional Data to Prioritize Causal Variants in Statistical Fine-Mapping Studies
synopsis: A probabilistic fine-mapping framework that combines association strength with functional annotations, estimating each annotation's weight from summary statistics across all loci and allowing multiple causal variants. In 1000 Genomes-based simulations it cut the variants needed to capture 90% of causal ones from 13.3 to 10.4 per locus. In a blood lipid meta-analysis, exons and TSSs raised causal probability, and 90% credible sets shrank from 17.5 to 13.5 variants.

title: Rare-Variant Association Analysis: Study Designs and Statistical Tests
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Review of the statistics behind rare-variant association studies, covering study designs, cost-effective sequencing and genotyping platforms, and analysis pipelines. It compares the assumptions and performance of gene- or region-based burden, variance-component and combined omnibus tests. It also covers meta-analysis, adjusting for population stratification, imputation, follow-up studies and rare-variant heritability.

title: RAREMETAL: fast and powerful meta-analysis for rare variants
synopsis: RAREMETAL is a fast software tool for meta-analysing rare variants from sequencing or array data. It accepts several input formats and handles both related and unrelated individuals. It runs single-variant tests, burden tests and conditional association analyses.

title: Bayesian Test for Colocalisation between Pairs of Genetic Association Studies Using Summary Statistics
synopsis: Introduces a Bayesian test (coloc) of whether two association signals, such as a GWAS and an eQTL, share a causal variant, using only single-SNP summary statistics. Reanalysing 966 liver expression samples with a lipid meta-analysis of over 100,000 Europeans, it supported 26 of 38 reported colocalisations and found 14 new ones. For SYPL2, IFT172 and TBKBP1 it instead pointed to SORT1, GCKR and KPNB1.

title: CFIm25 links alternative polyadenylation to glioblastoma tumour suppression
synopsis: Knockdown of the 3'-end processing factor CFIm25 increased proximal poly(A) site use, and a regression model applied to standard RNA-seq found shortened 3' UTRs in at least 1,450 genes (11% of expressed mRNAs), along with upregulated oncogenes such as cyclin D1. Glioblastomas with low CFIm25 showed shortened 3' UTRs in its target genes. Reducing CFIm25 increased glioblastoma tumorigenicity and tumor size, while overexpressing it suppressed tumor growth.

title: Transcriptional enhancers: from properties to genome-wide predictions
synopsis: A review of how enhancers are predicted genome-wide from features of their sequence and chromatin. It also covers high-throughput assays that find enhancers directly by measuring their activity, along with current technical advances and open challenges in regulatory genomics.

title: A general framework for estimating the relative pathogenicity of human genetic variants
synopsis: CADD combines many diverse annotations into one deleteriousness score (C score) per variant. A support vector machine was trained to tell 14.7 million high-frequency human-derived alleles from 14.7 million simulated variants, and scores were precomputed for all 8.6 billion possible SNVs, with short indels also scorable. C scores track pathogenicity, disease severity, regulatory effects and complex-trait associations, and they outperform any single-annotation method.

title: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types
synopsis: Introduces a multi-tissue epigenetic clock of 353 CpGs, trained on 8,000 samples from 82 Illumina array datasets covering 51 tissues and cell types. DNA methylation age is near zero in embryonic stem cells and iPSCs, tracks cell passage number, gives a highly heritable age-acceleration measure and works in chimpanzee tissue. Across 6,000 tumors of 20 cancer types, age is accelerated by 36 years on average.

title: 2013 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Assessment of Cardiovascular Risk
Transposition of native chromatin for fast and sensitive epigenomic profiling of open chromatin, DNA-binding proteins and nucleosome position
synopsis: ATAC-seq maps open chromatin quickly by having a transposase insert sequencing adaptors directly into native chromatin, using a two-step protocol on 500–50,000 cells. At nucleotide resolution it shows open sites, transcription factor footprints and nucleosome positions, and it sorts DNA-binding factors by whether they avoid, tolerate or overlap nucleosomes. Profiling one person's CD4+ T cells on consecutive days showed the method is fast enough for clinical decision-making.

title: Alternative cleavage and polyadenylation: extent, regulation and function
synopsis: Review of alternative polyadenylation (APA), which is widespread because many protein-coding and long non-coding RNA genes carry multiple poly(A) sites. It covers the polyadenylation machinery, methods for identifying APA events, and how poly(A) site choice is regulated. It also discusses how isoforms differing in coding sequence or 3′UTR affect mRNA stability, localization and translation, and their roles in biology and disease.

title: The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project
synopsis: Most GWAS loci for common diseases don't change protein-coding sequence, so regulatory variation probably explains much of disease risk. The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project was set up to address this. It describes plans for a shared database and tissue bank for studying how genetic variation relates to gene expression across human tissues.

title: Genome-Wide Quantitative Enhancer Activity Maps Identified by STARR-seq
synopsis: The number, positions, cell-type specificity and strength of enhancers in animal genomes are still largely unknown. STARR-seq is a method that measures enhancer strength quantitatively across the whole genome. The resulting maps give insight into how the regulatory genome is organized.

title: eRNAs Are Required for p53-Dependent Enhancer Activity and Gene Transcription
synopsis: Genome-wide p53 binding profiles revealed p53-bound enhancer regions (p53BERs) located far from known p53 target genes, with conserved p53 motifs and enhancer hallmarks. These p53BERs have enhancer activity and contact several neighboring genes on the same chromosome to regulate them from a distance. They also produce enhancer RNAs in a p53-dependent way, and these eRNAs are needed for full target-gene activation and p53-dependent cell-cycle arrest.

title: Genome-wide Methylation Profiles Reveal Quantitative Views of Human Aging Rates
synopsis: Built a model of the methylome's aging rate from more than 450,000 CpG markers in whole blood from 656 people aged 19–101. Aging rate depends on sex and genetic variants, helps explain epigenetic drift and shows up in the transcriptome. The model holds in other tissues and shows faster aging in tumors.

title: Bayesian refinement of association signals for 14 loci in 3 common diseases
lab: the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
synopsis: Densely genotyped 5,500 SNPs across 14 GWAS loci in 8,000 samples covering T2D, CAD, Graves' disease and controls, then used Bayes' theorem to build 95% credible sets of causal SNPs. At TCF7L2, CTLA4 and CDKN2A-CDKN2B (T2D), one SNP carried most of the posterior probability, and four other loci had small credible sets. Few SNPs in the credible sets had known functional annotations.

title: Systematic Localization of Common Disease-Associated Variation in Regulatory DNA
synopsis: Maps where common disease-associated GWAS variants fall relative to regulatory DNA marked by DNase I hypersensitive sites, broken down by tissue and disease. Many noncoding associations lie in regulatory DNA, with enrichment in relevant transcription factor binding sites and networks. This points to tissue- and development-specific regulatory roles that connect gene regulation to adult-onset disease.

title: An integrated encyclopedia of DNA elements in the human genome
synopsis: ENCODE set out to work out what the roughly three billion bases of the human genome actually do. The consortium systematically mapped transcription, transcription factor binding, chromatin structure and histone modifications, which let it assign biochemical functions to 80% of the genome, much of it outside protein-coding regions. The candidate regulatory elements connect physically to expressed genes and are statistically enriched for disease-associated variants.

title: Snakemake—a scalable bioinformatics workflow engine
synopsis: Snakemake is a workflow engine for building bioinformatics pipelines in a readable, Python-based language. The same workflow runs unchanged on anything from a single-core workstation to a compute cluster. It was the first system to automatically infer multiple named wildcards (variables) in input and output filenames.

title: Alternative Cleavage and Polyadenylation during Colorectal Cancer Development
synopsis: Does alternative cleavage and polyadenylation (APA) shift as colorectal cancer progresses, and could these shifts serve as biomarkers? Next-generation sequencing of 15 patient samples, validated in 50 patients including 5 normal/carcinoma pairs, found progressive APA changes: 3′UTR shortening in cell-cycle and RNA-processing genes, lengthening in adhesion and extracellular-matrix genes, linked to higher cleavage/polyadenylation factor expression. qPCR confirmed APA changes in DMKN, PDXK and PPIE.

title: Optimal Unified Approach for Rare-Variant Association Testing with Application to Small-Sample Case-Control Whole-Exome Sequencing Studies
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics

title: E2F mediates enhanced alternative polyadenylation in proliferation
synopsis: How is enhanced alternative polyadenylation linked to proliferation? Poly(A)-site deep sequencing of two human cell models, each profiled in proliferative, arrested and transformed states, revealed global 3' UTR shortening and more intronic poly(A) cleavage with proliferation, with a much weaker link to transformation. Genes encoding 3'-end processing factors were broadly upregulated in proliferating cells, partly driven by E2F transcription factors.

title: Topological domains in mammalian genomes identified by analysis of chromatin interactions
synopsis: Hi-C was applied to human and mouse embryonic stem cells and differentiated cell types to map higher-order chromatin organization at high resolution. Megabase-sized 'topological domains' turn out to be a pervasive feature that limits heterochromatin spread and is stable across cell types and conserved between species. Domain boundaries are enriched for CTCF, housekeeping genes, tRNAs and SINE retrotransposons.

title: The Poly(A)-Binding Protein Nuclear 1 Suppresses Alternative Cleavage and Polyadenylation Sites
synopsis: Which factors control alternative cleavage and polyadenylation (APA)? A reporter-based RNAi screen identified PABPN1, and genome-wide APA profiling in human cells showed its loss broadly shortens 3' UTRs through increased proximal cleavage-site use, which in Cyclin D1 weakens microRNA repression. The triplet-repeat expanded PABPN1 that causes OPMD had a similar effect in mouse and human cells by sequestering endogenous PABPN1 in nuclear aggregates.

title: Systematic dissection and optimization of inducible enhancers in human cells using a massively parallel reporter assay
synopsis: Introduces MPRA, which clones microarray-synthesized regulatory elements with unique sequence tags into reporter plasmids and reads out tag expression by high-throughput sequencing. Over 27,000 variants of a synthetic cAMP-regulated enhancer and the interferon-β enhancer were tested in human cells, mapping functional transcription factor binding sites at single-nucleotide resolution. Quantitative sequence-activity models (QSAMs) trained on the data were used to design enhancer variants with high induced and low basal activity.

title: High throughput gene expression analysis of the inner ear
synopsis: A critical review of ten years of microarray studies of inner ear gene expression in mice. It covers studies that searched for deafness genes, developmental transcriptional networks and functional miRNAs, along with work on responses to ototoxic drugs, hypergravity and caloric restriction and on networks downstream of deafness genes. Using public GEO datasets, it also shows that data from independent experiments can be combined to gain new insights, as RNA-seq becomes more common.

title: Selective inhibition of microRNA accessibility by RBM38 is required for p53 activity
synopsis: A genetic screen for RNA-binding proteins that control miRNA access to target mRNAs identified RBM38, a p53-induced protein whose blocking of miRNA repression is needed for proper p53 function. RBM38 acts selectively by binding uridine-rich regions near miRNA sites and does little to block miR-34a action on SIRT1. In large human breast cancer cohorts, promoter hypermethylation that lowers RBM38 expression was linked to wild-type p53 status.

title: Cell Type–Specific Transcriptome Analysis Reveals a Major Role for Zeb1 and miR-200b in Mouse Inner Ear Morphogenesis
synopsis: A new sorting protocol separated newborn mouse auditory and vestibular tissues into their major cell types, and transcriptome profiling of the sorted cells revealed cell-type-specific expression clusters. Computational analysis pointed to transcription factors and miRNAs that set cell identity, especially the Zeb1/miR-200b pathway controlling epithelial versus mesenchymal fate. ZEB1 pathway misregulation in Twirler mice, which have inner ear malformations, suggests a new mechanism behind deafness and balance disorders.

title: Matrin 3 Binds and Stabilizes mRNA
synopsis: Investigates the poorly understood nuclear matrix protein MATR3, an ATM substrate. MATR3 binds RNA through its RRM2 domain and interacts with RNA-processing proteins in an RNA-dependent way, and RIP-seq found small noncoding RNAs among its targets. Microarrays identified 77 transcripts whose levels depended on MATR3.

title: Rare-Variant Association Testing for Sequencing Data with the Sequence Kernel Association Test
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: Single-marker tests have little power for rare variants in sequencing studies. SKAT is a score-based variance-component regression test that checks a whole region's common and rare variants against continuous or binary traits, with covariate adjustment and analytic p values. It scanned 1000 genomes in 30 kb windows in 7 hours on a laptop, outperformed alternative tests in simulations and Dallas Heart Study triglyceride data, and comes with power and sample-size calculations.

title: Integration of Transcriptomics, Proteomics, and MicroRNA Analyses Reveals Novel MicroRNA Regulation of Targets in the Mammalian Inner Ear
synopsis: miRNA, transcriptome and proteome profiles of microdissected mouse auditory and vestibular sensory epithelia were combined and analyzed with the FAME algorithm to find functional miRNA–target interactions. Of 157 miRNAs detected, 53 differed between cochlea and vestibule, and some targets appeared only at the protein level, pointing to translational repression. miR-135b was experimentally confirmed to regulate PSIP1-P75 in vestibular hair cells, suggesting it shapes differences between cochlear and vestibular hair cells.
