title: Complex and dynamic landscape of RNA polyadenylation revealed by PAS-Seq
synopsis: PAS-Seq is a deep-sequencing method that maps poly(A) junctions and quantifies their relative usage across the transcriptome. In human and mouse, 40–50% of expressed genes showed alternative polyadenylation, and the method also captured conserved histone mRNA and mitochondrial RNA polyadenylation. Profiling mouse ES cells, neural progenitors and neurons showed widespread 3′UTR lengthening during differentiation.

title: Network medicine: a network-based approach to human disease
synopsis: Review arguing that diseases rarely stem from a single faulty gene and usually reflect perturbations of interconnected cellular networks. It outlines network medicine tools for finding disease modules and pathways and relating apparently distinct phenotypes. These approaches can help find new disease genes, interpret GWAS and sequencing variants, and identify drug targets and biomarkers.

title: SPIKE: a database of highly curated human signaling pathways
synopsis: SPIKE (Signaling Pathways Integrated Knowledge Engine) is a database of carefully curated interactions in human signaling pathways, with literature references for each interaction and pathway maps drawn by curators. It mainly covers DNA damage response, cell cycle, programmed cell death and hearing-related pathways. The data can be exported in several formats, and a standalone tool supports pathway analysis and dynamic visualization.

title: A Pumilio-induced RNA structure switch in p27-3′ UTR controls miR-221 and miR-222 accessibility
synopsis: Explains why the tumour suppressor p27 stays high in quiescent cells even though its repressors miR-221/222 are abundant: their target sites in the p27 3′ UTR are blocked. After growth factor stimulation, Pumilio-1 (PUM1) is upregulated and phosphorylated, then binds the 3′ UTR. This binding changes the local RNA structure and exposes the miRNA sites, so p27 is suppressed and cells enter the cell cycle quickly.

title: Major role for mRNA stability in shaping the kinetics of gene induction
synopsis: Asks how much mRNA stability, rather than sequential transcription-factor activation, shapes the timing of transcriptional responses. Analysis of many expression datasets alongside a kinetic mathematical model showed that fast-induced genes tend to have unstable mRNAs, a strong global anti-correlation. This relationship was weaker for repressed genes, where normally stable mRNAs often dropped faster than transcriptional shut-off alone could explain, pointing to active regulation of decay.

title: Expander: from expression microarrays to networks and functions
synopsis: A step-by-step protocol for analyzing gene expression microarray data with Expander 5.0. It goes from data import, normalization and filtering through clustering and network-based analysis. The resulting gene groups are then tested for Gene Ontology enrichment, co-regulation by transcription factors or microRNAs, and co-location on the genome.

title: Associating Genes and Protein Complexes with Disease via Network Propagation
synopsis: PRINCE is a global network-propagation method that ranks disease genes using a scoring function that varies smoothly over a protein interaction network and uses prior knowledge; it also predicts which protein complexes are linked to a disease. In cross-validation on 1,369 OMIM diseases it ranked the true causal gene first for 34% of them, inferred 139 coherent disease complexes and beat existing methods. For prostate cancer, Alzheimer's disease and type 2 diabetes it proposed new candidate genes and complexes.

title: Comprehensive Mapping of Long-Range Interactions Reveals Folding Principles of the Human Genome
synopsis: Hi-C is a method that captures interactions between all pairs of genomic loci in the nucleus and reads them out by deep sequencing. It was used to map the 3D folding of the human genome at 1 Mb resolution. The map splits the genome into two spatial compartments that follow local chromatin state, and remodeling of these compartments tracks changes in chromatin state.

title: Widespread Shortening of 3′UTRs by Alternative Cleavage and Polyadenylation Activates Oncogenes in Cancer Cells
synopsis: Cancer cell lines were compared with similarly proliferating non-transformed lines to explain why oncogene proteins can be overexpressed without genetic alteration. Cancer lines often expressed mRNA isoforms with 3' UTRs shortened by alternative cleavage and polyadenylation; these isoforms were more stable and made about ten-fold more protein, partly by escaping microRNA repression. The short IGF2BP1/IMP-1 isoform caused far more oncogenic transformation than the full-length mRNA.

title: Potential etiologic and functional implications of genome-wide association loci for human diseases and traits
synopsis: Introduces an online catalog of published GWAS SNP-trait associations and uses it to describe trait-associated SNPs. These SNPs were common (median risk allele frequency 36%) with modest effects (median OR 1.33). Compared with random array SNPs, they were enriched in nonsynonymous sites (OR 3.9) and 5-kb promoter regions (OR 2.3), were depleted in intergenic regions, and showed little enrichment in regions under positive selection.

title: WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis
synopsis: WGCNA is an R package that brings weighted correlation network methods together in one consistent toolkit, with tutorials. It builds co-expression networks, detects modules of highly correlated genes, summarizes each module by its eigengene or an intramodular hub gene, and relates modules to external sample traits. It also screens genes to find candidate biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

title: Proliferating Cells Express mRNAs with Shortened 3' Untranslated Regions and Fewer MicroRNA Target Sites
synopsis: Activated primary mouse CD4+ T cells showed a conserved shift toward upstream polyadenylation sites, producing shorter 3' UTRs, and this shift tracked proliferation across many cell types and tissues. Forcing expression of full-length 3' UTRs lowered protein output, which deleting predicted microRNA target sites sometimes reversed. Proliferation therefore goes with a broad loss of 3' UTR-based regulation.

title: SPIKE – a database, visualization and analysis tool of cellular signaling pathways
synopsis: SPIKE is a community knowledge base for organizing and interpreting cellular signaling pathways. It has three parts: a tiered database holding curated literature interactions alongside data from large public sources, an interactive visualization tool that can overlay genomic and proteomic data on pathway maps, and an inference engine that searches networks for new functional links. Registered users can upload data so that research groups can build the database together.

title: PLINK: A Tool Set for Whole-Genome Association and Population-Based Linkage Analyses
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
synopsis: PLINK is an open-source C/C++ toolset for whole-genome association studies that can quickly handle hundreds of thousands of markers in thousands of individuals. It covers data management, summary statistics, population stratification, association testing and identity-by-descent estimation. It focuses on using identity-by-state and identity-by-descent sharing to correct for stratification and to find long shared segments between distant relatives, which could help map loci carrying several rare variants.

title: Genome-Wide Mapping of in Vivo Protein-DNA Interactions
synopsis: ChIP-seq combines chromatin immunoprecipitation with ultrahigh-throughput sequencing to map where transcription factors bind across the whole genome in vivo. Applied to NRSF/REST, it found 1946 binding sites in the human genome with ±50 bp resolution and high accuracy (ROC area ≥0.96). The precise positions revealed noncanonical NRSF motifs and new candidate targets, including key regulators of pancreatic islet development.

title: Newborn Hearing Screening — A Silent Revolution
EXPANDER – an integrative program suite for microarray data analysis
synopsis: EXPANDER 2.0 is an integrated package that lets biologists run the whole microarray analysis workflow in one place. It covers normalization and filtering, clustering and biclustering, Gene Ontology enrichment, and promoter cis-element analysis to find the transcription factors behind expression changes. It comes with precompiled GO and promoter data for yeast, worm, fly, rat, mouse and human.

title: Transcription profiling of inner ears from Pou4f3ddl/ddl identifies Gfi1 as a target of the Pou4f3 deafness gene
synopsis: To find genes regulated by the hair-cell transcription factor Pou4f3 (mutated in human DFNA15 hearing loss), inner ears of E16.5 wild-type and Pou4f3 mutant mice were compared on high-density oligonucleotide microarrays, with RT-PCR and in situ hybridization used to confirm hits. Gfi1 expression dropped significantly without Pou4f3 and tracked its expression pattern. Gfi1 mutants showed outer hair cell degeneration like Pou4f3 mutants, making Gfi1 the first known downstream target of a hair-cell-specific transcription factor.

title: Prediction of Mammalian MicroRNA Targets
synopsis: Which mRNAs do vertebrate miRNAs regulate? Searching for conserved pairing to the miRNA 5′ region predicted more than 400 mammalian target genes. False-positive rates estimated with shuffled controls were 31% for human/mouse/rat targets and 22% when pufferfish was included.

title: STRING: a web-server to retrieve and display the repeatedly occurring neighbourhood of a gene
synopsis: Genes that repeatedly sit next to each other across genomes tend to encode functionally linked proteins. STRING (search tool for recurring instances of neighbouring genes) runs iterative searches to find genes that recur near a query gene and displays them in genomic context, yielding candidate functional partners. As an example, it suggested a functional context for an RNA methylase with unknown specificity.

title: Connexin 26 mutations in hereditary non-syndromic sensorineural deafness
synopsis: To find genes behind non-syndromic sensorineural deafness, a pedigree with autosomal dominant deafness and three recessive pedigrees linked to DFNB1 (13q11-12) were studied. A connexin 26 (Cx26, gap junction) mutation segregated with dominant profound deafness, and premature stop codons in Cx26 were found in the recessive families. Cx26 is highly expressed in human cochlea, making it the first known non-syndromic autosomal deafness gene.
